papers.title: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics identify a CD276-rich vascular matrix-associated CAF state linked to adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: BackgroundTargeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations have improved treatment outcomes in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but primary non-response and post-treatment residual progression remain common. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit marked heterogeneity and are closely associated with tumor treatment tolerance; however, specific stromal states associated with treatment non-response, post-treatment residual disease, and immune exclusion remain insufficiently characterized.MethodsThis study integrated ccRCC single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk transcriptomic cohorts annotated with clinical outcomes, CosMx and Visium spatial transcriptomic data, and multiplex immunofluorescence results. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis showed that vMat-CAF was enriched in tumor tissues and relatively enriched in non-responders; bulk clinical cohorts further showed that it was associated with adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations. Further analyses suggested that predicted vMat-CAF-derived LAMA4/COL4A1-CD44 communication was associated with tumor EMT-like programs; meanwhile, vMat-CAF exhibited high CD276 expression, and the association between CD276 and adverse clinical outcomes was more evident in the vMat-CAF-high context. Moreover, spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence showed that CD276-high vMat-CAF was enriched in perivascular regions and was associated with a spatial distribution pattern characterized by insufficient infiltration of CD8+ T cells into the tumor center.ConclusionsvMat-CAF is a CD276-enriched perivascular stromal state associated with adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations in ccRCC. Further analyses connected this state with tumor EMT-like programs, the context-dependent clinical significance of CD276, and restricted CD8+ T-cell infiltration into the tumor center, supporting a candidate perivascular stromal-immune gating model.

papers.title: ATF7 coordinates early transcriptional priming to enable direct cardiac reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on the canonical transcription factor cocktail MEF2C, GATA4, and TBX5 (MGT), yet successful lineage conversion requires additional non-cocktail regulators that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional transitions underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (ATF7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss-of-function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT-mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0-3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while restoring expression of fibroblast- and extracellular-matrix-associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non-reprogrammed state. CUT&RUN mapping across days 0, 3, and 6 of reprogramming shows that ATF7 binds dynamically to lineage-relevant regulatory regions, engaging cardiac loci-including those encoding Gata4 and Tbx5-early in reprogramming, and increasingly occupying fibroblast-associated loci at later stages. Integration of ATF7 binding sites with published single-cell chromatin accessibility data identifies substantial overlap with iCM-enriched regulatory signatures, particularly at day 3, highlighting this stage as a critical node of ATF7 activity. Together, these findings reveal that ATF7 executes a bifunctional regulatory role by simultaneously promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation and repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks. Our study establishes ATF7 as a previously unrecognized regulatory component necessary for efficient MGT-driven cardiac reprogramming and provides a preliminary mechanistic framework for its dual lineage-modulating functions.

papers.title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma.
papers.abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

papers.title: Integrated functional genomics and tissue-resolved transcriptomics identify PARD6B as a context-dependent proliferative dependency in high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: IntroductionHigh-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by profound genomic instability and tissue-level heterogeneity, complicating the translation of cell-line dependencies into patient-relevant vulnerabilities.MethodsThis study developed a function-first, tissue-resolved framework integrating DepMap CRISPR screening, four independent HGSOC single-cell RNA sequencing cohorts, paired malignant-microenvironment analyses within the same physical samples, spatial transcriptomics, normal fallopian-tube single-cell references, and experimental perturbation.ResultsAmong 18,513 genes evaluable across 11 HGSOC models, 1,762 met prespecified recurrence criteria, and 58 remained after exclusion of common-essential and broadly dependent genes. par-6 family cell polarity regulator beta (PARD6B) was dependent in eight of 11 models, with a stable dependency phenotype across DepMap releases. Across 29 patients from four independent single-cell cohorts, PARD6B was recurrently detected in malignant cells. Within matched tissue samples, PARD6B was strongly enriched in malignant cells relative to fibroblast, endothelial, and immune compartments, whereas enrichment relative to mesothelial-like cells was modest and did not reach multiplicity-adjusted significance. Patient-level tissue analyses further supported malignant-compartment enrichment. Importantly, PARD6B remained readily detectable in normal fallopian-tube secretory and ciliated epithelium, indicating that its functional selectivity cannot be inferred from tumor-versus-normal expression alone. In KURAMOCHI and OVCAR-8 cells, two independent PARD6B-directed shRNAs suppressed short-term growth and clonogenic capacity, increased G1 representation and reduced S-phase entry, and produced a progressive competitive-fitness disadvantage, with stronger effects in KURAMOCHI cells.ConclusionsTogether, these findings identify PARD6B as a recurrent, context-dependent proliferative dependency in HGSOC and establish a function-first, tissue-resolved framework for distinguishing tumor-cell vulnerabilities from expression patterns across the tumor microenvironment and normal epithelium. Further studies are warranted to define the molecular determinants of PARD6B dependence and its therapeutic index.

papers.title: Regenerative Surface Engineering of Dental Implants: Biological Strategies and Translational Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Improvements in early biological responses to engineered dental implant surfaces have not consistently translated into superior long-term survival, marginal bone stability, or prevention of peri-implant disease relative to contemporary surfaces. This narrative review focuses on titanium implants and abutments, examining six complementary strategies: osseointegration, soft-tissue integration, antibacterial activity, osteoimmunomodulation, periodontal ligament regeneration, and multifunctional and smart surfaces. It evaluates their biological rationale alongside the preclinical and clinical evidence supporting their use. Experimental studies demonstrate changes in cell attachment, bone formation, microbial control, and immune regulation, while responsive systems coordinate these functions through controlled release or activation. Most emerging approaches remain supported predominantly by preclinical evidence. Future development should match surface functions to the requirements of each implant region and healing stage. Clinical translation requires reproducible performance and comparative studies demonstrating benefits in patient-relevant outcomes, including loading safety, tissue stability, and long-term maintainability.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and multi-omics integration for cardiac regeneration: from cell fate decoding to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Heart failure remains among the leading causes of death worldwide, and its burden is increasing as populations age. The adult mammalian heart has almost no capacity to replace cardiomyocytes lost to injury: most cardiomyocytes leave the cell cycle, and the infarcted muscle is replaced by scar, so that function declines progressively. This constraint is not fixed. Neonatal mice regenerate myocardium for a brief window that closes within the first postnatal week, whereas adult zebrafish retain the capacity throughout life; the machinery for regeneration therefore exists, but is held in check. Cell-based therapy was expected to circumvent the problem, yet its clinical benefit has remained modest: transplanted cells survive and engraft poorly, their fate resists precise control, and the host microenvironment actively suppresses regeneration. These shortcomings are symptoms of a single underlying difficulty-scale. The regulatory logic of cardiac regeneration is distributed across transcriptional control, intercellular communication, spatial microenvironments and protein interactions, so that no omics layer examined in isolation, however high its resolution, can recover the integrated picture from high-dimensional, sparse and heterogeneous data. This review proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-multi-omics integration framework for cardiac regeneration. We survey the methodological progress that becomes available when single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics and proteomics are modelled jointly, and examine what these approaches can and cannot establish about cardiac lineage cell fate determination, about regeneration trajectory reconstruction, and about the failing-heart microenvironment. We then consider the translational pathways, and the limits of the evidence for each. The resulting evidence is uneven: the sections on the failing-heart microenvironment rest largely on direct cardiac data, whereas most of the methodological progress has been made outside the heart and transfers only under additional assumptions. One qualification is therefore stated at the outset: evidence for AI in cardiac regeneration is still scarce. The review is positioned as a methodological framework and a forward-looking perspective rather than a synthesis of established conclusions, and the evidence supporting each principal claim is graded, from direct experimental evidence in the heart to methodology.

papers.title: MIF and CXCL8 shape inflammatory myeloid-epithelial crosstalk in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a machine learning and integrative transcriptomic investigation.
papers.abstract: BackgroundProgression from high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) to cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is accompanied by extensive epithelial remodeling and changes in the inflammatory immune microenvironment. However, how stage-specific epithelial states interact with inflammatory myeloid responses, spatial immune organization, and patient prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated these changes and identified inflammation-related molecular features associated with clinical outcome.MethodsSingle-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic and survival cohorts, and drug-response data were integrated. Stage-associated cell states, epithelial trajectories, gene co-expression programs, and predicted cell-cell communication were analyzed across normal cervical tissue, HSIL, and squamous cell carcinoma. Machine-learning survival models were developed in TCGA-CESC and evaluated in GSE39001, GSE52903, and CGCI-HTMCP-CC. Pathway enrichment and immune deconvolution were used to assess biological and immune features associated with the prognostic model. Drug-response prediction, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and immunohistochemistry provided additional computational and tissue-level evaluation.ResultsHSIL was characterized by a proliferative epithelial state, whereas SCC was enriched for an epithelial state associated with keratinization stress, interferon responses, and inferred copy-number abnormalities, accompanied by increased inflammatory myeloid populations. Spatial transcriptomic analysis showed stronger immune and myeloid programs at the invasive front than in the tumor core. Predicted epithelial-myeloid communication in SCC prominently involved MIF-CD74 receptor complexes and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling. A five-gene prognostic model consisting of MIF, SPP1, CXCL8, CALML5, and CD74 achieved C-indices of 0.748, 0.696, and 0.691 in TCGA-CESC, GSE39001, and GSE52903, respectively. Higher risk scores were associated with hypoxia, glycolysis, TGF-β/EMT signaling, stromal remodeling, and reduced adaptive immune programs. MK-2206 showed favorable predicted interactions with MIF and CXCL8, with greater modeled stability for the CXCL8 complex. Immunohistochemistry confirmed progressively increased CXCL8 and MIF expression from normal cervix to HSIL and SCC.ConclusionProgression from HSIL to SCC was associated with coordinated epithelial remodeling, inflammatory myeloid activation, and spatial reorganization of the immune microenvironment. MIF-CD74 and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling were implicated in epithelial-myeloid communication, while the five-gene inflammatory model showed reproducible prognostic performance across independent cohorts. These results support further investigation of MIF- and CXCL8-related inflammatory signaling in cervical cancer progression and prognosis.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia.
papers.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are interconnected subcortical nuclei with a complex topographical organization that orchestrate goal-directed behaviors and are implicated in neurodegenerative movement disorders. We generated a cellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics atlas of the BG in human, rhesus macaque, and common marmoset, sampling over one million cells in each species. By integrating spatial data with a cross-species consensus single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cell-type taxonomy, this atlas reveals principles of molecular organization within and across structures. Extensive spatial sampling across the rostral-caudal axis illuminates complex, yet highly stereotyped, multi-axis gene expression gradients superimposed onto discrete compartments of the striatum. Additionally, we identify core-shell organization of the internal globus pallidus. This unified, cross-species spatial transcriptomics atlas will be a foundational resource for characterizing the molecular and functional organization of the BG and their roles in health and disease.

papers.title: High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Millimeter-Scale Malignant Territories and Immune Exclusion patterns in Human Salivary Gland Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the salivary gland (SGACC) is a rare malignancy with frequent late recurrence and limited response to systemic and immune therapies. Bulk and single-cell sequencing do not preserve tissue architecture, so the spatial organization of its MYB-driven myoepithelial and luminal tumor cells, stroma, and immune cells remains poorly defined. This study aimed to map the SGACC tumor microenvironment at near-cellular resolution. Methods Visium HD based spatial transcriptomics was performed on four SGACC tissue sections from three patients with tubulo-cribriform tumor form in stage III - IV. Bins of 10 x 10 µm were annotated and deconvolved with cell2location using an integrated single-cell reference of 119,189 cells from 20 donors. Pseudobulk differential expression, spatial autocorrelation, potency and spatial trajectory inference, permutation-based territory analysis, Hotspot module detection, and marker-based immune profiling were applied. Results MYB-expressing luminal (LECs-MYB) and myoepithelial (MECs-MYB) epithelial cells occupied 55.7% of bins on average. The MECs-MYB to LECs-MYB ratio increased from the nest interior toward the tumor edge, where cancer-associated fibroblasts rose sharply. Potency and trajectory analyses placed MECs-MYB upstream of LECs-MYB. Malignant states formed territories of up to 38.0 mm² that persisted over 1.5 mm in three sections and contained spatially restricted programs. Hypoxic stressed territories also showed mTORC1, unfolded protein response, and cell-cycle programs. T/NK, myeloid, MHC class I and II, and plasma cell signatures were 1.4-to 5.7-fold higher in stroma than in tumor nests, whereas VTCN1 (B7-H4) was the only B7 family ligand enriched within nests. Conclusions SGACC shows an ordered arrangement of malignant lineages, millimeter-scale malignant territories, MHC class – I and II enriched stroma, and immune-excluded nests enriched for B7-H4. These features provide evidence to be validated in larger cohorts with protein-level and clinical data. Simple Summary Adenoid cystic carcinoma is a rare cancer of the salivary glands that often returns years after treatment and responds poorly to current drugs and immunotherapy. Most earlier studies broke the tumor apart before measuring gene activity, losing the localization of cell in tumor. In this study, we measured gene activity directly on four thin tissue slices from the tumors of three patients at near single-cell detail. The two main types of cancer cells were arranged in an ordered pattern within tumor clusters, and cancer cells of the same type formed large regions several square millimeters in size, each with its own local gene activity. Immune cell signals stayed mostly in the surrounding supportive tissue and rarely reached the tumor clusters, while the tumor cells showed high activity of the gene for B7-H4 that can dampen immune responses. The patient with the longest recorded survival had an altered territory make up from that of other patients that points towards features that studies with larger cohort size can test and develop targeted treatment approaches.

papers.title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations.
papers.abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics uncovers pharmacokinetic and tumor-intrinsic determinants of resistance to trastuzumab deruxtecan in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is effective in both HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancers, but clinical responses are heterogeneous. Exploratory longitudinal analyses of paired pre-treatment and post-progression samples reveal increased cancer-to-vessel distance at resistance. Our study identifies spatial features associated with ADC response and resistance in clinical samples and provides a rationale for further investigation of candidate determinants.

papers.title: Intestinal BMP SMADs impart the mid-villus pattern through a transcription factor cascade mechanism.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Decode Tumor-Microenvironment Crosstalk in Colorectal Cancer Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Metastasis remains the principal cause of death in colorectal cancer (CRC), and accumulating evidence indicates that it is not a tumor-autonomous process. Dissemination and organ-specific colonization of the liver, lung, and peritoneum are governed by continuous, bidirectional crosstalk between malignant cells and the cellular and extracellular compartments of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Deciphering this crosstalk requires knowing not only which cell states are present but also where they reside and with whom they interact. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) resolves cellular heterogeneity at single-cell resolution but requires tissue dissociation, which erases in situ spatial information; spatial transcriptomics (ST) restores that dimension by mapping gene expression on intact sections and, with deconvolution algorithms, anchoring scRNA-seq-defined subpopulations back to their native coordinates. Organized around the metastatic cascade of local initiation, circulatory dissemination, and distant colonization, this review examines how the combined application of the two technologies has clarified tumor-microenvironment crosstalk at each stage. At the primary site, cancer stem cell heterogeneity, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) plasticity, and reciprocal signaling between budding cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts at the invasive front jointly determine invasive capacity and organotropism. During dissemination, we consider the clonal origins and transcriptional phenotypes of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and the clustering and immune-evasion programs that enable their survival under shear stress and immune surveillance. At the metastatic site, we address multilayered remodeling of the immune contexture, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix organization, vascular structure, and metabolic programs, emphasizing how macrophages, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and extracellular vesicles jointly construct an immunosuppressive niche permissive to colonization. Together, these findings frame organ-specific metastasis as the spatially coordinated co-evolution of tumor cells with tissue-resident immune and stromal populations, and highlight microenvironment-directed therapeutic opportunities and spatially informed prognostic biomarkers for precision oncology.

papers.title: Identification of immune- and cellular senescence-related genes in keloids through integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analysis.

The identified key genes are associated with cellular senescence-related transcriptional changes and immune microenvironment characteristics in keloid tissues. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression patterns at the bulk-transcriptome level, suggesting their relevance in keloid pathogenesis. papers.title: MuSpec: an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder recovers conserved granuloma niches and nominates host-directed repurposing candidates in human pulmonary tuberculosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. Tuberculosis (TB) granulomas are spatially organised host–pathogen structures, and the spatial arrangement of immune and stromal cells within the granuloma shapes disease outcome. Spatial transcriptomics can now resolve these structures at single-cell resolution, but most spatial-niche models have been developed and validated on tumour tissue. There is a shortage of unsupervised methods benchmarked on infectious-disease granulomas, and little evidence on how such niche models behave under input noise, missing modalities, and cross-sample transfer — the conditions that decide whether a niche atlas is translational or merely descriptive. Methods. We assembled MuSpec , an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder, and applied it to two single-cell-resolution Stereo-seq slides from human TB lung: B1 (pulmonary granuloma; Y40012NC13; 36,382 cells) and P1 (peri-lesional lung; Y40012LA11; 51,834 cells). Each cell was represented as a 39-dimensional input (7-dimensional cell-type composition from cell2location deconvolution against a 146,345-cell peripheral-blood scRNA-seq reference, 30 expression principal components, and 2 spatial coordinates). MuSpec smooths the input at three kNN scales (k = 10/20/30), rasterises each scale onto a ≤ 224² lattice, and passes the three feature maps through four deep-learning modules built on published attention-and-fusion designs — ASFF cross-scale fusion, TripletAttention, ExternalAttention, and a Fourier graph network (FGN) — to produce a 16-dimensional niche embedding; a shared encoder is trained jointly across both slides with an MSE reconstruction loss plus a spatial-smoothing loss, and niches are obtained by KMeans (K = 9). We benchmarked MuSpec against BANKSY at matched numbers of spatial domains, ran a three-seed module ablation and a 34-configuration single-factor hyperparameter sweep, and used the recovered granuloma signature for multi-library signature-reversal drug repurposing (LINCS L1000 chemical perturbations, GEO perturbations, NIBR DRUGseq 2025, and the original CMAP, merged) and AutoDock Vina docking against the host target SP110. On every matched-K comparison, MuSpec embeddings separated niches far more sharply than BANKSY (Δsilhouette + 0.31 to + 0.40 on both slides); MuSpec’s own K = 9 silhouette was 0.322 (B1) and 0.285 (P1). papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of gene expression data. Additionally, PIANO achieves robust integrations and trains 10× faster than previous methods. PIANO accurately integrates single-cell data across species and across single-cell and spatial transcriptomics modalities. As practical applications, PIANO models spatially resolved gene expression during Alzheimer's disease progression in human brains and integrates over 100 million cancer cells to model drug perturbations. In summary, PIANO's integration and generative modeling capabilities will empower novel insights for a wide range of future studies.

papers.title: Liver immune tolerance and regulated cell death in transplantation and hepatocellular carcinoma: shared mechanisms, divergent outcomes.
papers.abstract: The liver constantly encounters gut-derived antigens, microbial molecules, and food antigens. This environment has shaped a tissue-specific tolerance network centered on tolerogenic antigen presentation, immune-checkpoint activation, regulatory cell expansion, and metabolic suppression. This feature protects the liver during prolonged inflammation and gives it an immunological identity that most solid organs lack. Regulated cell death (RCD) and dead-cell clearance form a critical mechanistic layer within this network. Efficient efferocytosis of apoptotic cells reinforces resolution and tolerance, whereas necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis disrupt cell membranes and release danger signals that reshape myeloid activation, T-cell function, and the tumor microenvironment. In liver transplantation, this tolerogenic tendency produces donor-specific hyporesponsiveness, allowing a selected subset of stable recipients to stop immunosuppression while maintaining graft function-a state called operational tolerance. In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), tumors exploit the same immunosuppressive axes to block anti-tumor T-cell infiltration and effector function. Anti-PD-L1 therapy combined with anti-angiogenic treatment improves survival, demonstrating that partial disruption of tumor immunosuppression is therapeutically effective. Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell sequencing reveal that SPP1-positive macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts form a tumor immune barrier that excludes lymphocytes, showing that hepatic tolerance is organized in space. This duality becomes most dangerous in HCC recurrence after liver transplantation, where immune checkpoint inhibitors boost anti-tumor immunity but also raise the risk of acute rejection, graft failure, and death. Unlike reviews focused on hepatic immune tolerance, regulated cell death, or HCC immunobiology in isolation, this review integrates these processes across the physiological liver, transplantation, HCC, and post-transplant recurrence. We define this coordinated hyporesponsive state as the liver immune tolerance program (ITP), generated by cellular, molecular, spatial, metabolic, and cell-death-related networks. Rather than treating these processes separately, we position RCD and dead-cell clearance as a "death-to-immunity axis," systematically compare ITP remodeling in the physiological liver, transplantation, and HCC, and use post-transplant HCC recurrence as a clinical crossover setting in which graft protection and antitumor immune surveillance become therapeutic considerations. On this basis, we propose precision immune homeostasis: rather than choosing between immunosuppression and immune activation, immune status should be adjusted to an individualized range that protects the graft while preserving anti-tumor immune surveillance.

papers.title: SYNDRI: Context-aware removal of transcript spillover in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at single-cell resolution, but imperfect segmentation often misassigns transcripts between neighboring cells, a problem known as transcript spillover. Across MERFISH, CosMx, and Xenium datasets, SYNDRI achieves the highest aggregate performance across metrics of cell-type separation, reference similarity, and preservation of within-cell-type heterogeneity. papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic dissection of tumor-associated macrophage heterogeneity in cervical cancer: multi-omics perspectives and immunotherapy resistance.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) exhibit profound phenotypic and functional heterogeneity in cervical carcinoma, acting as key regulators of disease progression, extracellular matrix remodeling, and primary resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). This critical review synthesizes high-dimensional single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) datasets to delineate distinct myeloid archetypes, principally osteoclast-like SPP1+ TAMs, phagocytic C1QC+ TAMs, and early-inflammatory CXCL9+ subsets. In high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV)-driven tumors, viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 suppress cGAS-STING-dependent innate sensing and fuel CCL2 and CSF-1 chemokine secretion, driving stromal recruitment and preferential skewing toward immunosuppressive SPP1+ TAMs. Spatial transcriptomic profiling reveals that SPP1+ TAMs co-localize with alpha-SMA+ cancer-associated fibroblasts along invasive margins, forming dense desmoplastic mantles that physically and chemotactically exclude cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes from tumor cores. Conversely, C1QC+ TAMs reside within coordinated peritumoral immune hubs that facilitate productive antigen presentation. We resolve critical evidence boundaries across multi-omics layers, establishing that while scRNA-seq and spatial mapping are rich in human cervical cancer, purified TAM epigenomics, proteomics, and direct metabolomics remain scarce, requiring cautious interpretation of cross-tumor extrapolations. Mechanistically, myeloid-mediated resistance is governed by a tripartite architecture: defective antigen recognition, spatial exclusion, and active effector exhaustion via PD-L1, TIM-3, and metabolic starvation. Finally, we evaluate therapeutic modalities, showing that pan-macrophage depletion via CSF1R inhibition carries off-target toxicities and rebound myeloid recruitment, whereas targeted functional reprogramming and spatial disruption offer superior translational potential.

papers.title: Integrative 3D imaging and deep learning approach reveals cardiac fibroblast dynamics after myocardial infarction.
papers.abstract: Cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) are key mediators of heart failure progression, driving fibrotic scar formation after myocardial infarction (MI). Conventional preclinical assessment of MI relies on two-dimensional histology, which cannot resolve the three-dimensional (3D) architecture of the injured heart. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of CF activation is critical for identifying new drug targets, yet spatial mapping of gene expression in intact hearts remains challenging. To address this, we developed a high-throughput imaging pipeline that combined single-cell-resolution gene expression profiling in cleared whole hearts with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy and an AI-driven analysis framework optimized for MI characterization. These markers were detected by day 3 post-infarction in the endocardium and border zone, preceding collagenous scar formation, then expanded across the infarcted myocardium before declining toward baseline during scar maturation. These findings revealed a spatially organized progression of fibrosis-associated gene expression that began in defined regions of the injured heart and subsequently extended throughout the infarcted myocardium. Whole-organ gene-expression imaging combined with deep-learning-based analysis enabled quantitative spatiotemporal mapping of molecular remodeling and provides a framework for investigating disease progression in intact organs.

papers.title: A public-data spatial transcriptomic framework for invasive lung adenocarcinoma tumor ecosystems and prognosis.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of cellular heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is defined neuropathologically by the presence of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, yet these canonical lesions alone cannot account for its clinical, regional and cellular heterogeneity. AD is a multicellular, spatially organized disease shaped by the interactions of neurons, glia and vascular cells within distinct anatomical microenvironments. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing have made it possible to dissect the transcriptional signatures of individual cell populations in the AD brain, revealing selective neuronal vulnerability, stage-dependent glial remodelling and widespread disruption of cell-cell communication networks, whereas spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging have anchored these molecular changes to their tissue context. Studies of defined populations, such as people with autosomal-dominant AD or Down syndrome-associated AD, and of the oldest-old cohorts help disentangle the molecular changes that are causal drivers from those that are downstream consequences. Across individuals, AD heterogeneity is further shaped by sex and ancestry, underscoring the need for broader representation of these factors in single-cell and spatial studies. These advances are also reshaping translational pipelines through multi-omic benchmarking of animal models and single-cell-based drug-repurposing strategies. papers.title: An interpretable deep learning framework for revealing fine-grained spatial domains.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables gene expression profiling with preserved spatial context, yet accurate spatial domain delineation remains challenging. We present RIF, a robust and interpretable deep learning framework for fine-grained spatial domain identification. In an invasive ductal carcinoma dataset of more than 720,000 cells, RIF-defined domains suggest an epithelial-mesenchymal transition gradient, including reduced hormone dependence and extracellular matrix remodeling.

papers.title: MIF-CD74 orchestrates synovial macrophage metabolic-inflammatory reprogramming by ENO2 interaction to drive osteoarthritis pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Synovitis is a central driver of osteoarthritis (OA) progression, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms sustaining inflammatory circuits in the synovium remain incompletely understood. Multiomics and mechanistic studies revealed that CD74 interacts with the glycolytic enzyme enolase 2 (ENO2). To translate this axis therapeutically, we developed synovium-targeted cationic lipid nanoparticles decorated with MIF-mimetic peptides (PcLNPs) for the delivery of CD74 siRNA. Intra-articular administration of PcLNPs efficiently targeted CD74+ macrophages, attenuated their inflammatory and glycolytic phenotypes, and ameliorated murine OA progression in vivo. Our findings establish the CD74/ENO2/HIF-1α/β-catenin axis as a critical integrator of metabolic reprogramming and inflammation in OA synovitis and present a potential targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for disease modification.

papers.title: Intraoperative Radiographic Visualization of the Schneiderian Membrane Using the Novel Hydraulic Contrast Lift Protocol: A Retrospective Clinical Case Series.
papers.abstract: Background: Limited intraoperative visibility during transcrestal sinus floor elevation complicates assessment of membrane elevation and possible perforation before graft placement. This retrospective case series evaluated the clinical feasibility and preliminary clinical and radiographic outcomes of the Hydraulic Contrast Lift (HCL) protocol. Materials and methods: A retrospective case series was conducted on seven patients treated with the HCL protocol. The technique uses a hydraulic delivery system to inject a radiopaque contrast medium beneath the Schneiderian membrane. Primary procedural endpoints were membrane visualization and controlled elevation without radiographic signs of perforation. Clinical endpoints included integration of the bone substitute, implant osseointegration, and implant survival. Bone height changes were assessed using preoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and post-healing periapical radiographs or CBCT. Results: Successful intraoperative membrane visualization was achieved in all seven cases (100%), with no radiographic evidence of Schneiderian membrane perforation. The mean preoperative residual bone height was 4.5 ± 2.0 mm (range: 1.5-8 mm), and the mean postoperative bone height gain was 9.0 ± 3.3 mm (range: 4-12 mm). Five patients (71.4%) received simultaneous implant placement and two (28.6%) underwent delayed placement. All grafted areas showed radiographic continuity with adjacent bone, and all implants achieved successful osseointegration. Implant survival after implant loading (9-47 months; mean: 28.1 ± 12.8 months) was 100%. Conclusions: Within the limitations of this small retrospective case series, the HCL protocol appeared feasible, enabling intraoperative radiographic visualization of the sinus membrane and controlled elevation. No radiographic signs of membrane perforation or clinical complications were observed. Radiographic bone height gain and favorable implant outcomes were documented during follow-up. Larger prospective studies are needed to evaluate safety, reproducibility, and long-term clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Premalignant immune remodeling in laryngeal carcinogenesis: a framework to define when immune interception becomes testable.
papers.abstract: Laryngeal dysplasia presents a clinical dilemma because lesions with similar histology can have different outcomes. Single-cell, spatial and pathology studies show immune remodeling before invasion, yet differences between lesion stages do not establish future progression risk within dysplasia. We consider three potentially coexisting explanations of a premalignant immune signal, namely reactive recruitment, ineffective antitumor activity and a stromal niche that supports progression. Each requires different spatial and functional evidence. We adapt established validation principles to five evidence requirements concerning lesion identity, future invasion, spatial and functional state, causal reversibility and clinical readiness. Their purpose is to separate risk stratification from target validation, rather than require one marker to perform both roles. Existing laryngeal studies address parts of this framework, but none establishes that targeting a premalignant immune circuit prevents cancer. The immediate priority is to compare histologically comparable lesions with known outcomes and test candidate interactions in models that retain noninvasive epithelium. Short window studies may subsequently establish target engagement and biological activity, but clinical prevention requires separate evidence of reduced invasive cancer risk and acceptable harm.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk in gouty arthritis.
papers.abstract: Gouty arthritis is an inflammatory joint disease driven by the deposition of urate crystals, with its pathological core involving innate immune activation and synovial microenvironment remodeling. Recent studies have revealed that the crosstalk between macrophages and fibroblasts plays a critical regulatory role in disease initiation, amplification of acute inflammation, and chronicity. However, the molecular network of this crosstalk and its dual role in maintaining and disrupting joint homeostasis remain insufficiently understood, and direct evidence in gouty arthritis is limited. Drawing on evidence from fibrotic diseases, rheumatoid arthritis, and other inflammatory arthropathies, this review outlines three pathways potentially mediating this crosstalk: the PRG4-CD44 immunomodulatory axis maintains joint homeostasis by regulating synovial lubrication and immune tolerance; SPP1+ matrix-remodeling macrophages drive fibroblast activation and tissue fibrosis; the mechanotransduction pathway senses mechanical microenvironment changes induced by urate crystal deposition and coordinately regulates the inflammatory response. It further delves into the potential mechanisms of these pathways in acute inflammatory flares and chronic tissue destruction, while exploring therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways, including PRG4 recombinant protein, SPP1 neutralizing antibodies, and mechanotransduction inhibitors, aiming to establish a critical framework for future validation of precision interventions in gouty arthritis.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics for gene discovery identifies Slc13a5 as a modulator of bone mechanoadaptation.
papers.abstract: Bone is a dynamic tissue that continuously adapts its structure in response to mechanical loading, an essential process for maintaining skeletal health. In addition, Slc13a5 cKO mice exhibited lower resorption around the neutral axis after loading compared to controls. papers.title: TiO2 particles induce CHIT1 and YKL-40 in human macrophages: implications for implant-associated inflammation.
papers.abstract: Titanium is widely used for orthopedic and dental implants because of its biocompatibility and mechanical properties. However, corrosion and mechanical wear can result in the release of titanium-containing particulate debris, which may contribute to chronic peri-implant inflammation and implant failure. Metabolic activity, assessed using the Alamar Blue assay, was maintained or increased following exposure to 25, 50, 100, and 200 ppm TiO2, with a statistically significant increase observed at 100 ppm in M0 macrophages, while no significant changes were detected in M1 or M2 macrophages. Transcriptomic analysis identified CHIT1 and CHI3L1 as the two most upregulated members of the Glyco_18 protein family. RT-qPCR confirmed significant induction of CHIT1 following TiO2 exposure in M0, M1, and M2 macrophages, while CHI3L1 expression was significantly increased in M0 and M2 macrophages. Increased gene expression was accompanied by a concentration-dependent increase in YKL-40 secretion, with statistically significant increases observed from 100 ppm TiO2 onwards. At 100 ppm, extracellular CHIT1 protein levels increased significantly in M0 and M1 macrophages, despite no corresponding significant increase in CHIT1 enzymatic activity. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed altered intracellular localization of CHIT1 following TiO2 exposure, with accumulation in the trans-Golgi network (TGN) of M1 macrophages and disruption of TGN organization in M0 and M2 macrophages. Furthermore, CHIT1 and YKL-40 were detected in CD68-positive macrophages within peri-implant tissues obtained from patients undergoing removal of titanium fracture fixation implants, supporting the clinical relevance of the in vitro findings. Collectively, these findings identify CHIT1 and YKL-40 as macrophage-associated proteins responsive to TiO2 particle exposure and support their further investigation in biomaterial-associated inflammation.

papers.title: Senescence-associated stromal remodeling in bone marrow aging and hematologic and bone-metastatic diseases
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence is implicated as a driver of age-related tissue dysfunction and chronic inflammation. However, no single marker defines a senescent cell, and distinguishing senescence from other stressors requires both experimental perturbation and comparison across contexts. Human marrow aging was characterized by interferon and IL6/JAK/STAT3 activation in hematopoietic progenitors, myeloid-biased output, and progressive loss of naive CD4 T cell identity. Spatially, CDKN1A was concentrated in vascular stroma, and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) expression rose with age coordinately across stromal cell types within individual donors (mean pairwise rho = 0.46), consistent with shared influences on stromal aging. Malignancy was associated with distinct and disease-specific senescence-associated states rather than uniform amplification of aging programs. Senescent fibroblasts spatially adjacent to tumor in breast and prostate cancer bone metastases shared an upregulated secretory program comprising 148 genes encoding secreted proteins, alongside upregulated matrix-remodeling and cellular adhesion signatures. Osteolineage cells found in metastasis sites as well as in MPN marrow also displayed distinct senescence-associated phenotypes, including enlarged, multinucleated osteoclasts and CDKN1A+ osteoblasts with upregulated secretory programs. However, senescence-associated secretory programs and matrix dysregulation in stromal cells was not observed in MM, indicating that these features are not generic consequences of tumor burden within the bone marrow but rather arise from specific cancer-stromal interactions. Residual hematopoietic regions showed altered myeloid and erythroid composition and transcriptional states. To complement these human datasets, we used a mouse model in which doxorubicin-induced senescence reproduced molecular and compositional hallmarks of marrow aging that were selectively reversible with senolytic treatment. These data establish normal marrow as a quantitative baseline for senescence and separate shared from context-specific senescent states.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Vascular Wall Cells during Ductus Arteriosus Development and Closure
papers.abstract: Background: The transition from fetal to postnatal circulation requires closure of the ductus arteriosus (DA), involving smooth muscle cell contraction followed by anatomical remodeling. However, the spatial organization and developmental transcriptional dynamics of vascular wall cells during this transition remain poorly understood. Methods: We analyzed vascular morphology and spatial transcript profiles of the mouse DA and aorta at five stages from embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5) to postnatal day 2.5 (P2.5), enabling paired comparisons within tissue sections. Selected findings were compared with an independent mouse single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset. Histological and spatial transcript analyses were also performed on human DA tissue and the adjacent pulmonary artery. Results: The DA exhibited transiently higher cell-cycle-associated transcription across multiple vascular wall populations at E16.5, preceding medial thickening at E18.5 and postnatal luminal closure. Prenatally, DA mural cells exhibited greater contractile-associated gene expression than aortic mural cells. This difference diminished after birth, accompanied by a marked shift toward synthetic-like transcriptional programs associated with extracellular matrix remodeling and proteolysis. Ductal endothelial cells exhibited postnatal divergence from aortic endothelial cells in matrix- and adhesion-associated gene expression. Adventitial fibroblasts displayed distinct extracellular matrix- and insulin-like growth factor-associated expression profiles. In a human postnatal DA specimen, synthetic-like mural cells were enriched in regions of disrupted elastic lamellae and prominent collagen staining and shared selected remodeling-associated markers with postnatal mouse DA mural cells. Conclusions: DA development and closure involve temporally organized transcriptional changes across vascular wall populations, characterized by prenatal cell-cycle-associated activity and rapid postnatal reorganization of mural transcriptional programs. These findings provide a spatial framework for understanding vascular cell plasticity and multicellular remodeling during DA closure.

papers.title: A transcriptomic-driven segmentation and cell simulation framework for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics and cell-cell communication
papers.abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics platforms, such as Visium HD and Atera, enable transcriptome-wide profiling at near-single-cell resolution. However, accurate cell segmentation to define spatial boundaries relies heavily on histological images. Previous approaches struggle in tissues with high cell density, inflammation, or mineralization, leading to transcriptomic bleed-through and inaccurate clustering. To address this, we developed TENGU (Transcript-signal Enrichment and Grouping Unit), a comprehensive end-to-end bioinformatic software package. Unlike existing tools, TENGU employs a transcript-first segmentation approach, prioritizing transcript-signal density as the primary modality and utilizing histological images only as a secondary supplement in unresolved regions. These initial boundaries are further optimized through a transcriptomic-driven cell simulation algorithm that iteratively refines boundaries based on localized gene expression probabilities, effectively minimizing spatial scattering and preserving biologically distinct molecular signatures. The pipeline seamlessly integrates tissue segmentation, high-resolution cell-type annotation, and spatially aware cell-cell communication (CCC) analysis. We rigorously benchmarked TENGU against the 10x Genomics and Bin2cell pipelines for segmentation, and against CellNEST for spatial CCC inference, across diverse and technically challenging microenvironments. TENGU demonstrated superior transcriptomic distinctness in the murine brain and successfully captured matrix-embedded osteocytes in decalcified bone. In murine osteomyelitis, TENGU outperformed CellNEST in sensitivity, localizing both reactive bone remodeling (Tgfb) and dense, abscess-encapsulating inflammatory (Il1a/Il1) networks. TENGU also resolved species-specific pro-tumorigenic hubs (MDK-SDC4) in a human colorectal cancer xenograft and generalized effectively to the Atera platform, delineating CXCL12-CXCR4 and LGALS3-TGFBR2 signaling within highly compacted human breast cancer tissue. By mitigating image-dependent constraints, TENGU provides a highly adaptable, robust computational framework to decode the functional micro-anatomy of healthy and pathological tissues.

papers.title: Mapping Senescence Landscapes in Metabolic Liver Disease Progression
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects more than 30% of the population, often progressing from reversible steatosis to irreversible fibrosis and cirrhosis. Although cellular senescence is implicated in driving MASLD, the evidence in human tissue and the mechanism are lacking. Furthermore, scRNAseq data validated the Visium results and identified a previously unappreciated population of senescent Schwann cells in the diseased liver niche. These findings map the spatial origination and paracrine propagation of pathological senescence and identify senotypes associated with liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Lattice and Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Architectures for Dental Implants: A Scoping Review of Design, Manufacturing, and Performance.
papers.abstract: Dental implant longevity depends on both biological integration and mechanical compatibility with bone. Dense titanium and Ti-6Al-4V implants are far stiffer than peri-implant bone, a mismatch that promotes stress shielding and marginal bone loss. Architected lattice and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures, enabled by additive manufacturing (AM), lower effective stiffness and create interconnected space for bone ingrowth, vascularization, and osseointegration, yet the value of any single architecture is hard to isolate because geometry, density, material, processing, and surface state act together. This scoping review maps the evidence on lattice and TPMS dental implants and how design strategy, AM route, and material system govern mechanical reliability and biological validation. Studies were charted by material, architecture, AM route, model scale (15 full implants, three implant-like or root-analogue models, 10 scaffold or coupon specimens), validation level (L1-L5) and outcome. Across the 28 included studies, titanium and Ti-6Al-4V dominate (19 studies, 12 of them fabricated by laser powder bed fusion), while zirconia from vat-based ceramic routes emerges as an esthetic, biologically promising alternative (six studies). The evidence remains uneven: 24 studies included simulation, 16 physical mechanical testing, 11 in vitro biology, three in vivo validation and only two a fatigue endpoint, and none reached clinical-level evidence. A lattice implant thus behaves as the combined product of its material, architecture, process, and surface; progress depends on reporting manufactured geometry, demonstrating fatigue and debris safety, and pairing in vitro with in vivo osseointegration. On the present evidence base, architecture-level statements are best read as design hypotheses and evidence trends rather than as clinically preferred configurations.

papers.title: Deciphering Hepatic Host Transcriptomic Responses to Leishmania Infection: Integrating Evidence from In Vivo and In Vitro Studies.
papers.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a life-threatening, vector-borne systemic disease caused by the parasitic protozoans Leishmania donovani and Leishmania infantum. Among the affected organs, the liver represents a unique immunological environment in which, in commonly used experimental murine models, infection is often controlled through the coordinated formation of granulomas around infected Kupffer cells. However, effective hepatic parasite control does not necessarily result in complete parasite elimination, and the course of infection may vary across host species and experimental models. Understanding the molecular mechanisms governing parasite clearance and persistence has been greatly advanced by transcriptomic technologies. The transition from bulk RNA sequencing to single-cell RNA sequencing and, more recently, spatial transcriptomics has enabled increasingly detailed characterization of hepatic immune responses, revealing cellular heterogeneity, spatial organization, and regulatory networks underlying host-parasite interactions. In parallel, the development of advanced in vitro models, including multicellular co-cultures and organoid-based systems, has provided complementary platforms for investigating these mechanisms under controlled experimental conditions. This review provides an integrated analysis of transcriptomic studies investigating hepatic host responses to Leishmania infection across different experimental models and transcriptomic approaches. We examine the molecular pathways underlying host defense, granuloma formation, and parasite persistence, compare the complementary insights provided by distinct transcriptomic approaches, and critically evaluate the extent to which in vitro models reproduce the hepatic transcriptional landscape observed in vivo. By integrating findings across experimental platforms and transcriptomic resolutions, we identify conserved immune signatures, model-specific limitations, and key biological and technological knowledge gaps that should guide the development of more physiologically relevant experimental models and future transcriptomic studies of the liver during VL.

papers.title: Genomic and Functional Technologies for Studying Cancer Stem Cell Dynamics, Metastasis, and Therapy Resistance.
papers.abstract: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are a functionally defined and plastic subpopulation of tumor cells. While the precise definition of CSCs is still debated, studies demonstrate that CSCs are capable of driving recurrence, metastases, and therapeutic resistance. Prior reviews on the genomic characterization of CSCs have primarily focused upon biological mechanisms, therapeutic categories, or the leverage of a single experimental platform. However, no prior reviews have provided a cross-platform comparison of the methodologies used to characterize CSC dynamics, metastasis and therapy resistance. We provide the mechanistic basis, application to CSC dynamics, advantages and limitations, and methods of integration among these complementary approaches, including the leveraging of new artificial intelligence tools. While we describe the details of each individual platform, ultimately, we show that the integration of techniques is critical to future studies of CSCs.

papers.title: Insights on Intestinal Fibrosis: From Stromal Cell Heterogeneity and Metabolic Reprogramming to Novel Therapeutic Strategies.
papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of inflammatory bowel disease, and it can lead to fixed strictures, intestinal obstruction, and repeated surgical intervention. Although effective control of inflammation may limit ongoing tissue injury, no approved therapy selectively prevents or reverses established intestinal fibrosis. In this review, we integrate classical extracellular-matrix pathways with recent single-cell, spatial, and metabolic evidence to provide a multicellular framework for intestinal fibrogenesis. Single-cell studies indicate that intestinal fibroblasts comprise overlapping and environmentally responsive states rather than fixed lineages. Their activation is shaped by reciprocal communication with immune cells, epithelial and endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, creeping fat, and the intestinal microbiota. Metabolic reprogramming provides an additional layer of regulation through glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway, glutamine-proline metabolism, lactate-associated signaling, and extracellular metabolite sensing. However, the strength of evidence varies among these mechanisms, and direct links between defined fibroblast states and specific metabolic dependencies remain limited. In this review, we further discuss therapeutic opportunities targeting immune-stromal communication, pathogenic fibroblast programs, cellular metabolism, extracellular-matrix turnover, and mechanotransduction. Translating these opportunities into stage-specific interventions will require spatially resolved functional models to validate causal targets and fibrosis-selective biomarkers to assess therapeutic effects.

The spatial organization of the ETMR immune microenvironment remains poorly understood, limiting our understanding of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance.MethodsWe defined the spatial organization of ETMR using spatial transcriptomics across 11 samples from 9 patients, integrated with independent publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data.ResultsImmune cells were largely excluded from the tumor core, while the peritumoral border formed an immunosuppressive niche enriched for B-cells and M2-like macrophages. These cells exhibited conserved transcriptional programs associated with gliosis, extracellular matrix generation, immune suppression, and cellular exhaustion. At this interface, the CD74-MIF signaling axis was enriched, suggesting a possible coordinated mechanism underlying peritumoral macrophage and regulatory B-cell abundance. Integration with the ETMR developmental continuum further revealed spatial covariation between tumor developmental states and immune and stromal features. Multilayered rosettes, a histopathological hallmark of ETMR, showed spatially confined interferon-responsive, immune-associated transcriptional programs, enriched for type I and II interferon signaling and antigen-processing pathways. This suggests that despite global immune exclusion, localized regions of interferon-responsive and immune-associated transcriptional activity persist within the tumor.ConclusionThese findings define a compartmentalized spatial immune architecture in ETMR characterized by relative immune depletion in tumor-rich regions, immunoregulatory and stroma-associated programs at selected tumor interfaces, and localized interferon-responsive transcriptional activity within rosette-associated regions. This spatial framework provides a basis for future mechanistic studies of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance in ETMR.

papers.title: Generating scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq using a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides detailed, genome-wide gene expression profiles at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of disease-driving cell types and genes. However, scRNA-seq remains costly, and there are extremely limited samples generated in even the most extensive human disease studies. In contrast, bulk RNA-seq data is abundant but averages gene expression across all cell types, losing cell-specific detail. To further leverage this abundance of RNA-seq data, methods have been developed to infer cell type proportions and average expression from bulk data using scRNA-seq as a reference. Additionally, generative AI models have been developed to generate more of an existing scRNA-seq dataset, spatial transcriptome data from bulk, and a complete single-cell dataset from bulk, with an incomplete set of single-cell data, for large cohort studies. However, there is a lack of tools specifically dedicated to generating representative single-cell RNA-seq from bulk RNA-seq data. To address this, we develop an innovative, modular framework, termed Bulk2SC, that takes full advantage of powerful generative AI approaches and existing scRNA-seq data to generate representative scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq. Bulk2SC uses a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder for data generation together with any tool that predicts cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq data. We demonstrate the superior performance of Bulk2SC relative to tools that generate scRNA-seq from bulk RNA-seq as part of broader computational frameworks on published datasets from multiple tissue types. We also apply and assess Bulk2SC on a benchmark deconvolution dataset that contains paired bulk and single nucleus RNA-seq data. The modular design of Bulk2SC allows for deconvolution of single datasets as well as straightforward implementation within larger computational frameworks.

papers.title: Emerging Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics: From Multi-Kingdom Interactions to Genetic Variation and Population Diversity.
papers.abstract: Plants are composed of highly specialized cell types. Their identity, location, and interactions collectively determine their development, environmental responses, and evolutionary adaptation. The emergence of single-cell/nuclear technologies has transformed plant biology by enabling the study of gene expression at cellular resolution, while spatial transcriptomics preserve the developmental and spatial context. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the current experimental and computational landscape of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in plants. We discuss the strengths, limitations, and applications of available technologies, ranging from transcriptomics at cell level to high-resolution spatial platforms, as well as recent advances in bioinformatics analysis, data integration, and community resources. Beyond methodological advances, we highlight how these technologies are redefining our understanding of plant development, responses to abiotic stress, and interactions among different kingdoms, by revealing dynamic cellular states, regulatory networks, and spatially organized biological processes that remain inaccessible to bulk analyses. We discuss the emerging integration of single-cell approaches with population genomics, evolutionary biology, and genetic demultiplexing, which opens up new avenues for identifying the cellular basis of natural variation and adaptive evolution.

papers.title: TYR as a Candidate Diagnostic Biomarker for Diabetic Foot Ulcer: An Integrated Bioinformatics, Machine-Learning, and Multi-Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by chronic non-healing wounds and a high risk of amputation, and early molecular diagnosis remains an unmet clinical need. Methods: RNA-sequencing data from GSE134431 (13 DFU vs. eight diabetic foot-skin samples) were analyzed with a limma-equivalent empirical-Bayes moderated t-test, identifying 721 differentially expressed genes. Because the LASSO/SVM-RFE intersection was configuration-sensitive and did not recover the prioritized genes, tyrosinase (TYR) was treated as a pre-specified candidate selected by differential-expression significance, melanin-pathway enrichment, and biological plausibility; its ranks among the 721 DEGs by adjusted p-value, |log2FC|, and training AUC are reported. Performance was evaluated by nested leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), apparent AUC with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and external cohorts (GSE80178 and GSE68183; quantile-normalized and z-scored per dataset). Single-cell data (GSE165816) were re-analyzed to quantify TYR before and after quality control, and CIBERSORT was used for immune deconvolution with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and group-adjusted correlations. Results: In nested LOOCV, TYR was re-selected in all 21 folds with a held-out AUC of 0.971. TYR was significantly downregulated in the external cohorts (merged six DFU vs. 12 non-DFU: p = 0.0047, direction-aware AUC = 0.903, bootstrap CI 0.736-1.000), including the within-GSE80178 comparison of DFU versus diabetic foot skin (p = 0.0238). In single-cell analysis, TYR was genuinely expressed after quality control (64.2% of melanocytes), and melanocyte proportions were reduced in DFU at the sample level (p = 0.040). After correction for multiple testing, resting and activated mast cells, CD4+ memory-activated T cells, and follicular helper T cells differed between DFU and controls, and TYR showed a group-adjusted positive correlation with M1 macrophages (R = 0.460, p = 0.036). Conclusions: TYR is a reproducible candidate diagnostic biomarker for DFU supported by nested validation, external cohorts, and single-cell evidence. HOXC10, which was not replicated externally, is retained as an exploratory observation only. Larger prospective cohorts with diabetic non-ulcer controls and functional experiments are required.

papers.title: Closed-loop, tooth-to-implant biointerface engineering: dental pulp stem cells at titanium surfaces for cell-enabled osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHEDs) are underused, tooth-derived regenerative resources with particular relevance to implant dentistry. Routinely extracted third molars, orthodontically removed premolars, and exfoliated deciduous teeth provide recurrent sources of viable pulp tissue that are largely discarded, creating an opportunity to convert surgical waste into a clinically linked regenerative product. This review critically examines how dental pulp-derived cells interact with titanium and titanium-based biomaterials and evaluates their potential for osseointegration and peri-implant bone regeneration. Across the available evidence, these cells adhered to titanium, responded to micro-, nano-, and meso-scale topography, and were modulated by surface chemistry, wettability, ion incorporation, ultraviolet photofunctionalization, plasma treatment, and biofunctional ligands. These interfaces influenced attachment, proliferation, osteogenic differentiation, angiogenic signaling, immunomodulation, antibacterial activity, and mineralized matrix formation. In vivo studies further demonstrated improvements in peri-implant bone formation, bone-implant contact (BIC), trabecular architecture, and early mechanical fixation after DPSC or SHED delivery. Collectively, the available evidence provides preliminary preclinical support for the biological feasibility of engineering dental pulp-derived cell-titanium interfaces but is insufficient to establish clinical readiness. We therefore propose the SEED framework-Source, Expansion, Engineered interface, and Delivery-for closed-loop tooth-to-implant regeneration. SEED leverages the procedural proximity of tooth harvesting to dental care and integrates cell sourcing, clinically compatible expansion, instructive titanium design, and site-specific delivery. Translation remains limited by the small number and heterogeneity of animal studies, short follow-up periods, limited evaluation under functional loading, incomplete information regarding transplanted-cell fate, and frequent reliance on serum-containing culture systems. Future studies will require standardized, clinically compatible and preferably xeno-free processing, application-specific potency testing, longitudinal cell tracking, disease-relevant models, and long-term functional validation under microbial, inflammatory, vascular, and mechanical challenge. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Dental pulp-derived stem cells provide a distinctive opportunity to connect an accessible, frequently discarded biological resource with engineered implant biomaterials. This systematic review integrates evidence from 33 in vitro/ex vivo and four preclinical in vivo studies to determine how titanium topography, physicochemical properties, and biofunctionalization regulate dental pulp-derived cell behavior and implant-related bone regeneration. Beyond evidence synthesis, we identify major material-cell and translational design gaps and introduce the SEED framework-Source, Expansion, Engineered interface, and Delivery-to conceptualize these variables as an integrated regenerative system. The resulting closed-loop tooth-to-implant paradigm reframes titanium from a passive cell carrier into an instructive regenerative interface and provides a biomaterials-centered roadmap for developing cell-enabled strategies for osseointegration.

papers.title: Bone Retention Without Osseointegration During Antiresorptive Therapy: A Rat Model of Immediate Implant Placement Following Prolonged Ligature-Induced Periodontitis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Immediate implant placement in sites with prolonged ligature-induced periodontal disease during antiresorptive therapy is poorly modeled. This study investigated whether zoledronic acid (ZA) could preserve peri-implant bone sufficiently to support osseointegration in a rat challenge model. Methods: Thirty-two adult male Wistar rats received saline (SAL) or ZA (ZOL). Ligature-induced periodontitis was maintained for seven weeks around the mandibular first molar, followed by extraction and immediate placement of a commercially pure titanium implant. Animals were euthanized after 28 days. Removal torque (RTQ), SEM-EDX, and micro-computed tomography were assessed alongside undecalcified histology, which underwent qualitative evaluation and blinded exploratory semiquantitative scoring. Results: Median RTQ and peri-implant bone volume fraction (BV/TV) were numerically higher in ZOL than SAL animals (RTQ: 4.0 vs. 2.5 N·cm, p = 0.104; BV/TV: 46.5% vs. 28.0%, p = 0.113), but neither difference reached statistical significance. Histology showed near-complete absence of new bone-implant contact, with median scores of 0 in both groups. Compared with SAL, ZOL specimens showed descriptively greater retention of alveolar architecture, while 4 of 8 specimens had no detectable viable bone in the assessed peri-implant region. Epithelial coverage scores were lower in ZOL than in SAL (median: 0 vs. 2; nominal p = 0.027). Conclusions: Under the combined experimental conditions, retention of peri-implant mineralized tissue did not correspond to meaningful regenerative osseointegration. The findings distinguish bone quantity and mechanical anchorage from direct biological integration and should not be extrapolated directly to routine clinical implant therapy.

papers.title: Volatile Sulfur Compound Profiles Across Peri-Implant Health, Mucositis and Peri-Implantitis: A Cross-Sectional Study of Factors Associated with Halitosis in Patients with Dental Implants.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Halitosis is common in patients with dental implants, but the contributions of peri-implant disease and prosthesis design remain unclear. We compared volatile sulfur compound (VSC) profiles across peri-implant health, mucositis, and peri-implantitis and evaluated factors associated with halitosis. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 74 patients with implants in function for at least 12 months, classified according to the 2018 World Workshop definitions (26 health, 25 mucositis, and 23 peri-implantitis). Hydrogen sulfide, methyl mercaptan, and dimethyl sulfide were measured by portable gas chromatography alongside organoleptic scores, tongue coating, salivary flow, and the Halitosis Associated Life-quality Test. A prespecified multivariable regression was complemented by exploratory cross-validated diagnostic, decision-curve, and mediation analyses. Results: Median total VSC increased across health, mucositis, and peri-implantitis, driven primarily by methyl mercaptan. Halitosis prevalence also increased across groups. Cement retention and limited cleaning access were independently associated with higher VSC. An exploratory model combining log-transformed methyl mercaptan, tongue coating, and smoking showed good cross-validated discrimination, and peri-implant bleeding statistically accounted for part of the association between peri-implantitis and VSC, although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Conclusions: Peri-implantitis is associated with a methyl mercaptan-dominant breath profile, and modifiable prosthetic factors are associated with malodour. Whether breath analysis adds to conventional clinical examination was not tested and requires prospective evaluation.
