papers.title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
papers.abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. We define the Predictive Dermatome as a computationally derived, anatomically localized skin region characterized by a shared or probabilistically related biological aging state and trajectory inferred from integrated molecular, structural, imaging, clinical, and exposomic data. Unlike a conventional neurological dermatome, which denotes a cutaneous territory associated predominantly with sensory innervation from a spinal nerve root, the Predictive Dermatome is not defined by nerve distribution. The proposed framework integrates spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, single-cell or single-nucleus reference maps, optical coherence tomography, confocal or ultrasound imaging, histology when available, tape-strip biomarkers, extracellular matrix and glycation-related measurements, and exposomic data streams. We describe the learning task, input-output structure, spatial graph construction, modality-specific encoders, transformer-based token fusion, training objectives, regularization strategies, and missing-modality handling. Rather than requiring spatial omics or tissue sampling for every clinical patient, the framework uses transcriptomic, proteomic, histologic, and extracellular matrix measurements as discovery and validation layers from which clinically deployable surrogate models could be trained using non-invasive and minimally invasive inputs. We also outline preprocessing steps for high-dimensional spatial transcriptomic data, cross-modal image-omics registration, validation stages, uncertainty estimation, and ethical safeguards including privacy-preserving learning and bias auditing across skin phototypes. The Predictive Dermatome should therefore be viewed as a staged research architecture for precision dermatology, not as a currently validated clinical decision system. Its value lies in defining how molecular geography, imaging, and environmental exposure may eventually converge to support localized risk stratification, longitudinal monitoring, and biologically guided intervention in skin aging and regenerative dermatology.

papers.title: Spatial SASP-GAT: dual-graph attention networks for masked SASP gene reconstruction in spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measurements are incomplete, and it is unclear how much of a predefined gene program, such as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), can be predicted from its tissue context. We present Spatial SASP-GAT, a dual-graph GATv2 framework that reconstructs masked expression of 54 SASP genes from spatial neighbourhoods and a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, and use it to quantify the contribution of each information source. We evaluated 64 HEST-1k slides (38 training, 13 validation, 13 locked test) and an external Visium HD cohort (12 slides) with an availability-aware protocol. Adding spatial context lowered the validation masked MSE from 0.2681 (expression-only) to 0.2026, whereas the PPI branch alone did not. The full model reached a masked MSE of 0.1716 (locked test) and 0.4208 (external), but it did not outperform training-free neighbourhood baselines (Ring2Mean, 0.1569) or an adapted STAGATE (0.1614) on the test set. When the target gene was hidden throughout the two-hop receptive field of the spatial branch, the spatial branch no longer improved reconstruction on the locked test set, and its mean gain on the external cohort was small. Edge-free and degree-preserving rewired PPI controls retained most of the improvement of the full model over the spatial-only model, and the spatial gain was not specific to SASP genes. Reconstructed profiles agreed only partially with the observed clustering. The principal contribution is a systematic evaluation of spatial and PPI information, not improved reconstruction accuracy; the task is SASP expression reconstruction, not identification of senescent cells.

papers.title: An SPP1-Associated Macrophage State Marks Lesion-Centred Inflammatory Persistence During Subacute Spinal Cord Injury.
papers.abstract: Persistent subacute neuroinflammation limits tissue repair after spinal cord injury (SCI), yet how macrophage state heterogeneity is organized within lesion-centered inflammatory niches remains unclear. We integrated time-resolved mouse single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics with trajectory analysis, regulatory network inference, ligand activity analysis, exploratory in silico Spp1 perturbation, and interpretable machine learning, followed by tissue-level and donor-recipient validation. Time-resolved profiling revealed early neutrophil and monocyte recruitment, subsequent macrophage accumulation, and delayed microglial activation. Macrophage subclustering resolved seven injury-responsive states comprising inflammatory, transitional, tissue-associated, lipid-associated, SPP1-associated, repair-associated, and homeostatic programs. Among these states, SPP1_Mac expanded prominently, peaked at 7 days post-injury, and retained marked inflammatory activity. Spatial mapping localized the SPP1_Mac signature and focal Spp1 expression to lesion-centered regions within a broader Cd44-enriched cellular territory. Regulatory network, ligand activity, communication, and machine learning analyses prioritized SPP1-associated signaling within this state-niche organization. Injured spinal cords showed increased lesion-associated SPP1 and CD44 expression and enrichment of SPP1 within IBA1-positive myeloid regions. In a BV2-to-RAW264.7 donor-recipient system, donor cell Spp1 silencing attenuated recipient cell CD44 and CD86 expression, the proportion of F4/80⁺CD86⁺ cells, and IL-1β and TNF-α secretion following conditioned medium transfer. Together, these findings support a state-niche-communication framework in which SPP1_Mac represents a prominent cellular feature associated with lesion-centered inflammatory persistence during subacute SCI, providing a biological foundation for further stage-informed investigation of the post-SCI inflammatory microenvironment.

papers.title: SpatialMuSC: Spatial Graph-Conditioned Diffusion Refinement for Robust Spatial Multi-Omics Integration.
papers.abstract: MotivationEmerging spatial multi-omics technologies enable the simultaneous profiling of multiple molecular layers within the same tissue section, offering new opportunities to interrogate tissue organization in its native spatial context. However, sequencing-derived spatial multi-omics data are often affected by intrinsic perturbations, such as technical noise, missing values, sparsity and measurement bias. These perturbations make existing methods that mainly use spatial graphs for neighborhood aggregation insufficient to recover continuous tissue-region structures, while unconstrained representation learning may propagate noisy associations and lead to fragmented spatial domains.ResultsWe present SpatialMuSC, a robust spatial multi-omics integration framework centering on spatial graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency. SpatialMuSC introduces spatial topology as conditional information into the latent diffusion process, enabling spatial adjacency to guide neighborhood aggregation, spatial structure propagation and graph-aware denoising of latent states. Perturbation-invariant fusion consistency further encourages stable multi-omic fusion under perturbed observations. We evaluate SpatialMuSC on diverse spatial multi-omics datasets across different tissues and sequencing platforms, including 10x Visium, Stereo-CITE-seq, SPOTS and spatial epigenome-transcriptome data. Across these benchmarks, SpatialMuSC consistently outperforms ten state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification and tissue-structure preservation. Ablation analyses confirm the contributions of graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency, rather than post hoc graph smoothing or graph propagation alone. In particular, SpatialMuSC effectively distinguishes adjacent tissue regions, preserves block-wise smoothness and layered architectures, and shows more stable performance in missing-observation stress tests, while hippocampal marker, enrichment, and paired RNA-ATAC analyses identify a GCL-associated neuronal program and a TTR-associated accessibility feature in a choroid plexus-enriched domain.Availability and implementationThe source code is available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/SpatialMuSC.Supplementary informationSupplementary data are available online.

papers.title: Scar Treatments in Hand Surgery.
papers.abstract: Scar formation after hand surgery poses unique functional and aesthetic challenges because of the hand's complex anatomy, dense sensory innervation, and reliance on supple skin and tendon glide. Hypertrophic scars, keloids, adherent scars, and contractures can cause pain, hypersensitivity, restricted motion, and impaired activities of daily living, yet evidence guiding scar management in hand surgery remains limited and largely extrapolated from burn and general surgical populations. This review synthesizes current evidence on the biology, classification, prevention, and treatment of scars as they pertain to hand surgery. Nonoperative management, including silicone gel sheeting, compression therapy, intralesional corticosteroid injection, laser therapy, and hand therapy, forms the foundation of care. Operative interventions, ranging from scar excision and Z-plasty to skin grafting, local flap reconstruction, dermal substitutes, and tenolysis, address established contracture and adhesion when conservative measures fail. Emerging therapies, such as autologous fat grafting, growth factor modulation, platelet-rich plasma, and botulinum toxin A, show early promise but require validation in hand-specific trials. Optimal outcomes depend on a collaborative, individualized approach integrating patient risk stratification, meticulous surgical technique, and close coordination with hand therapy throughout the care continuum.

papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence implicates nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) in the pathogenesis of various malignancies, yet the biological pathways underlying its effects on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have not been fully elucidated. In summary, this study identifies TOP2A as a potential molecular candidate associated with NNK-related HCC progression and suggests a possible relationship between TOP2A and ORM1 that may contribute to NNK-associated molecular alterations in HCC.

papers.title: Effects of implantoplasty on titanium dental implant corrosion, cytotoxicity and extracellular matrix proteins (collagen 1, 3, and elastin) under in vitro conditions.
papers.abstract: Implantoplasty (IP) is a commonly employed mechanical technique to remove bacterial biofilms adhering to the titanium surfaces of dental implants. Based on the intraoral machining and smoothing of the titanium surface using rotating instruments, this procedure inevitably alters the physicochemical properties of the implant. Therefore, the aim of this study is to evaluate the effects of implant surface modifications on corrosion resistance, cell viability (via MTT assay), and implant-tissue interface stability (by analyzing collagen type 1, collagen type 3, and elastin expression) in comparison with untreated control samples. Using tungsten carbide burs and silicon carbide polishers, implantoplasty was performed to simulate a 5 mm bone loss in the SLA surface area of dental implants. Surface topography (Sa) was determined using a 3D profilometer. Corrosion resistance was evaluated using electrochemical tests in Hank's solution. Corrosion parameters such as corrosion current density (icorr), and corrosion potential (Ecorr), were determined. The effects of implants on cell viability were analyzed using the MTT test. In addition, collagen type 1, type 3 and elastin levels were evaluated using ELISA to determine implant-tissue interface stability. Although implantoplasty significantly reduced surface roughness and increased the initial corrosion rate approximately sevenfold compared to SLA controls, cell viability remained well above the 70% cytocompatibility threshold across all groups. These findings suggest that despite the altered initial electrochemical parameters, the modified surfaces exert no cytotoxic effects on fibroblast cells, demonstrating favorable short-term in vitro cytocompatibility.

papers.title: Cohort profile of the Korea Osteonecrosis of the Jaw (KONJ) multicenter registry and biobank: design and clinical characteristics.
papers.abstract: IntroductionWe describe the establishment and profile of the Korea Osteonecrosis of the Jaw (KONJ) cohort, an ongoing multicenter registry and biobank for longitudinal clinical and omics research on medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ).Material and methodsInitiated in 2018 and expanded to four Korean tertiary centers, KONJ combined a Main clinical registry of retrospective and prospective records with a prospectively enrolled Core cohort. A web-based registry captured medication histories, dental events, disease status, and treatment. The Core protocol specified sampling at diagnosis or around surgery and post-cure for MRONJ. Tissue collection depended on the procedure. Staging followed American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons criteria.ResultsAt the 30 August data lock, KONJ comprised 982 unique patients, including 389 in the Core cohort. The clinical analysis included 702 patients: 477 with MRONJ, 200 at risk, and 25 with stage 0 findings. Among patients with MRONJ (mean age, 74.7 ± 9.7 years), 90.6% were women and 84.5% had osteoporosis. Denosumab was the most frequent documented agent (26.8%), and stage 2 accounted for 74.2%. Tooth extraction and dental implants were associated with MRONJ in 43.4% and 20.8%, respectively, and 93.7% underwent surgery. First-timepoint specimens were collected from 185/207 Core participants with MRONJ and 76/86 at-risk participants.DiscussionKONJ combines ongoing clinical registration with protocol-defined biospecimen sampling at clinically relevant time points. MRONJ in this tertiary-center cohort predominantly affected older women with osteoporosis. It provides a foundation for clinical, biomarker, and omics studies of MRONJ development, treatment, and healing.

papers.title: Strontium-90 Radiotherapy Suppresses Fibrosis by Attenuating the FAK-RhoA/ROCK-YAP/TAZ Mechanosignaling Axis in Hypertrophic Scars.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scar (HTS) fibrosis is sustained by abnormal mechanical signaling, but how strontium-90 (Sr-90) superficial radiotherapy counteracts this process is unclear. We combined primary HTS fibroblasts and a rabbit ear HTS model with atomic force microscopy, molecular and functional assays, histology, and RNA sequencing to examine cell mechanics and FAK-RhoA/ROCK-YAP/TAZ signaling. Sr-90 reduced fibroblast stiffness and stress-fiber organization, inhibited nuclear YAP/TAZ localization, TEAD activity, profibrotic gene expression, migration, adhesion, and collagen-gel contraction, while increasing LATS1/2 phosphorylation and suppressing FAK/Src-RhoA/ROCK-MLC2 signaling. YAP/TAZ overexpression partially reversed these effects, TEAD1/4 silencing diminished the reversal, and non-phosphorylatable YAP-5SA/TAZ-4SA mutants produced stronger rescue than the corresponding wild-type proteins under irradiation. In rabbits, Sr-90 reduced scar pathology, YAP/TAZ-TEAD interaction, and FAK-RhoA signaling and downregulated Hippo- and focal-adhesion-related transcriptional programs. These findings show that Sr-90 suppresses HTS fibrosis by weakening the mechanical-signaling network that converges on YAP/TAZ and by enhancing LATS1/2-dependent YAP/TAZ inactivation.

papers.title: Finerenone attenuates experimental autoimmune myocarditis and modulates cardiac macrophage and Th17-cell responses.
papers.abstract: IntroductionAutoimmune myocarditis is characterized by immune-mediated myocardial injury and remodeling. However, whether the selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist finerenone modulates the cardiac cellular microenvironment in autoimmune myocarditis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of finerenone on experimental autoimmune myocarditis (EAM) and its regulation of the cardiac cellular microenvironment.MethodsAn EAM model was established in BALB/c mice by α-myosin heavy chain immunization, followed by finerenone treatment. Echocardiography, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and RT-qPCR were used to evaluate cardiac injury, inflammation, fibrosis, and function. Single-cell RNA sequencing, T-cell receptor clonotype analysis, transcription factor regulatory network analysis, and cell-cell communication analysis were performed to characterize finerenone-induced changes in cardiac immune and stromal cell populations. Flow cytometry and macrophage-CD4+ T-cell co-culture experiments were performed to further validate the immune-related findings.ResultsFinerenone alleviated myocardial injury, inflammatory infiltration, and collagen deposition and improved left ventricular systolic function in EAM mice, including under a delayed-treatment regimen. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that finerenone remodeled the cardiac cellular microenvironment, reduced remodeling-associated Spp1+ macrophages and inflammation-associated Cxcl10+ macrophages, and suppressed IRF7-, STAT1-, STAT2-, and RFX5-associated transcriptional programs. Finerenone also reduced Th17-related inflammatory and cytotoxic programs and T-cell clonal expansion. Cell-cell communication analysis predicted reduced macrophage-Th17-cell communication, particularly MHC-II-associated signaling. Furthermore, macrophage-CD4+ T-cell co-cultures from finerenone-treated EAM mice exhibited reduced CD4+ T-cell proliferation and IL-17A+ CD4+ T-cell proportions compared with those from untreated EAM mice. Profibrotic fibroblast programs and neutrophil inflammatory signaling were also suppressed.DiscussionTargeting mineralocorticoid receptor-related immune networks may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for autoimmune myocarditis.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell-cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues.MethodsThis narrative review synthesizes findings from studies identified primarily through PubMed searches supplemented by manual curation of reference lists. Search terms included "single-cell," "spatial transcriptomics," "MASLD," "NAFLD," "NASH," "MASH," "steatohepatitis," and "liver fibrosis." Studies applying single-cell transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell eQTL analysis, and integrative multi-omics approaches were included. The last literature search was conducted in July 2026. Results: Single-cell technologies have revealed key cellular alterations during MASLD progression, including disrupted hepatocyte metabolic zonation, heterogeneous activation states of hepatic stellate cells, macrophage functional reprogramming, immune cell dysfunction, and dynamic remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment. Spatial transcriptomics has further resolved the spatial organization of these cellular changes, whereas single-cell eQTL analyses have linked genetic susceptibility loci to cell-specific regulatory programs. Single-cell profiling of intestinal, adipose, and vascular tissues has expanded the understanding of extrahepatic contributions and gut-liver communication in MASLD. These advances provide a foundation for drug target identification, mechanistic understanding of current and investigational therapies, and assessment of treatment response at cellular resolution.ConclusionSingle-cell multi-omics is transforming MASLD research from tissue-level characterization toward cellular-resolution understanding, providing novel insights into disease stratification, therapeutic target discovery, and biomarker development, and advancing precision hepatology.

papers.title: Kidney fibrosis mechanisms in the single‑cell era: From cellular heterogeneity to therapeutic opportunities (Review).
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease affects >13% of adults worldwide, yet no approved antifibrotic therapy is available. Recent advances in single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the understanding of renal fibrosis. These technologies have unmasked unexpected heterogeneity among myofibroblasts and macrophages, identified scar‑associated macrophage subsets and resolved the long‑standing debate over myofibroblast origins by confirming resident fibroblasts as the principal source. Spatial transcriptomics has further defined functional communities and pathologically distinct niches, including maladaptive repair niches centred on SOX9+ epithelial cells, profibrotic microenvironments enriched in tenascin‑C and immune‑activation niches where macrophages and fibroblasts co‑localize. Intercellular crosstalk networks involving TGF‑β, NOTCH and paracrine signals from injured tubules have been systematically mapped. These insights are now being translated into targeted strategies, such as surface marker‑directed agents against CD248 and fibroblast activation protein, epigenetic modulators including HDAC6 inhibitors and advanced 3D bioprinted human models. The present review synthesized these single‑cell and spatial discoveries to provide a conceptual framework for developing precision antifibrotic therapies for progressive kidney disease.

papers.title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that SPP1⁺ TAMs engage TM4SF1⁺ malignant epithelial cells via the SPP1-CD44 axis within a hypoxic niche, driving tumor stemness, invasion, and metastatic progression. SPP1⁺ TAMs exhibit a hypoxic, M2-polarized phenotype and their abundance correlates with worse overall and progression‑free survival in metastatic PTC patients. We further develop an integrative machine-learning model based on SPP1⁺ TAM‑derived molecular features that predicts lymph node status with high accuracy. Preclinically, pharmacological targeting of SPP1 attenuates tumor cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis, supporting its candidacy as a therapeutic target. Collectively, this study demonstrates how AI‑driven multi‑omics analysis can jointly identify a functionally validated target and generate a clinically deployable predictive model, illustrating a framework for bridging computational discovery with translational oncology.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Identify KLF9-Regulated NDUFA4L2 as a Mediator of Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Atherosclerotic Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells.
papers.abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling is a major determinant of atherosclerotic plaque progression, yet mitochondrial regulators linking lipid stress to VSMC dysfunction remain incompletely defined. This study investigated the role and upstream regulation of NDUFA4L2 in atherosclerosis. Human atherosclerosis scRNA-seq data comprising 12 source/anatomical dataset labels derived from 11 GEO series and 258 122 cells were integrated with human coronary spatial transcriptomic data. VSMC reclustering, pathway analysis, hdWGCNA, SCENIC, pseudotime analysis, and independent bulk transcriptomic assessment were performed to identify and contextualize candidate regulators. NDUFA4L2 knockdown and overexpression, KLF9 silencing, ChIP-qPCR, rescue experiments, and AAV-mediated in vivo silencing were conducted for functional validation. A transcriptionally distinguishable SMC state showing relative NDUFA4L2 enrichment was identified together with metabolic and remodeling-associated programs. Sensitivity analyses indicated that mitochondria-related transcriptional scores were dependent on signature definition and technical context and did not provide direct evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction. Spatial and patient-paired regional analyses indicated that mitochondria-related transcriptional signals were influenced by technical and vascular-wall transcriptional context and did not show consistent plaque-specific enrichment. NDUFA4L2 silencing alleviated lipid-induced loss of mitochondrial calcein retention, membrane depolarization, mitochondrial oxidative stress, and calcium accumulation, and partially normalized alterations in mitochondrial dynamics-related proteins and α-SMA expression, whereas NDUFA4L2 overexpression produced largely opposite effects. KLF9 silencing decreased NDUFA4L2 expression, ChIP-qPCR demonstrated KLF9 occupancy at the NDUFA4L2 promoter, and NDUFA4L2 restoration partially reversed the improvements in the measured mitochondrial parameters induced by KLF9 knockdown. In vivo, SM22α-driven AAV9-mediated NDUFA4L2 suppression reduced aortic plaque burden, vascular stenosis, serum IL-1β levels, and mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities in high-fat diet-fed mice. KLF9-regulated NDUFA4L2 contributes to alterations in mitochondrial homeostasis in lipid-stressed VSMCs and atherosclerotic remodeling, highlighting this regulatory axis as a potential molecular link between mitochondrial stress and vascular remodeling.

papers.title: Targeting Neutrophil Extracellular Traps to Inhibit Colon Cancer Tumor Necrosis and Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Tumor necrosis is associated with poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) yet is generally viewed as a passive consequence of tumor growth rather than a therapeutic target. We demonstrate that necrosis correlates with metastatic disease in human CRC independently of tumor size. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of primary CRC and colorectal liver metastases revealed that peri-necrotic programs are associated with metastatic progression. Patients with CRC exhibited increased circulating neutrophils, including NET-primed and CD177-low neutrophils with reduced extravasation capacity. Consistent with these findings, intravascular NET aggregates localized adjacent to necrotic regions in human CRC specimens. In a mismatch repair-proficient mouse model of CRC, neutrophil infiltration and NET formation increased during tumor progression, whereas genetic and pharmacologic NET inhibition reduced tumor necrosis, decreased metastasis, and enhanced chemotherapy efficacy. Together, these findings identify NET-driven tumor necrosis as an active promoter of CRC metastasis and support NET inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Liriopesides B ameliorates fine particulate matter-induced lung injury by directly targeting ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 Q2 to dismantle the macrophage lactylation-neutrophil extracellular trap axis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundFine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure drives progressive lung injury characterized by aberrant neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). Mechanistically, the E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBE2Q2 acts as a critical immunometabolic checkpoint that regulates lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) to sustain this pro-inflammatory cascade. High-content imaging identified LPB as a potent inhibitor of this lactylation axis. Biophysical deconvolution confirmed that LPB directly binds to UBE2Q2 (KD =3.98 × 10-6 M), disrupting the macrophage-neutrophil crosstalk. Finally, cell-specific reconstitution assays validated that the in vivo protective benefits of LPB are strictly dependent on the macrophage-intrinsic UBE2Q2 axis.ConclusionOur study decodes the UBE2Q2-LDHA-lactylation axis as a novel targetable vulnerability in environmental lung injury and highlights LPB as a mechanistically defined, natural product candidate for the targeted management of PM2.5-associated respiratory diseases.

papers.title: Pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface coordinates infection control and osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) compromises osseointegration through bacterial colonisation and dysregulated inflammation. Here, we pre-established a living biointerface by seeding immunity-and-matrix-regulatory cells (IMRCs) onto three-dimensional (3D)-printed titanium prostheses modified with silver (Ag) by plasma immersion ion implantation (Ag-PIII) before bacterial exposure, generating an IMRC-seeded Ag-PIII-modified titanium (TAM) construct. These findings provide preclinical support for pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface to alter the initial conditions of surface competition and integrate early infection control with subsequent osseointegration.

papers.title: Survival and Failure Rates of Dental Implants Placed in Sites of Previous Implant Failure: A Systematic Review of Retreatment Outcomes and Associated Clinical Risk Factors.
papers.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the survival and success of replacement dental implants placed at previously failed implant sites. The review quantitatively synthesized implant survival data and presented implant success, complications, and clinical risk factors through narrative synthesis because of differences in outcome reporting.Materials and methodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. PubMed (MEDLINE), Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for studies published up to December 2025. Original clinical studies evaluating replacement implants after previous implant failure were included. Implant survival proportions were pooled using a random-effects, single-arm proportion meta-analysis with the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation in R software (meta package).ResultsTwenty-one studies were included in the systematic review and 16 in the meta-analysis. Implant survival ranged from 73.1% to 99.0%, with a pooled survival estimate of 90.2% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 84.4-94.9%) and substantial heterogeneity (I² = 95.0%). Given this heterogeneity and the variable follow-up periods (12 months to more than 10 years), the pooled estimate should be interpreted as an approximate summary of reported survival rather than a long-term survival estimate. Smoking, poor bone quality, and previous peri-implantitis were the most frequently reported risk factors for failure, whereas bone augmentation and advanced implant surface characteristics were associated with lower reported failure risk in observational data. Most included studies showed moderate to high methodological quality and low to moderate risk of bias.ConclusionsReplacement implants placed at previously failed sites showed a pooled survival estimate of 90.2%; however, this estimate should be interpreted cautiously given the high heterogeneity, variable follow-up periods, and limitations of the available evidence. Future prospective multicentre studies with standardised outcome measures and long-term follow-up are needed to strengthen clinical recommendations.

Untargeted metabolomics showed remodeling in creatine, arginine, glutathione, and acyl-carnitine pathways, with key metabolites (creatine, guanidinoacetic acid, succinate, and fumarate) shifted toward WT. Integrated analysis converged on oxidative phosphorylation, arginine and proline metabolism, and immune signaling. papers.title: Androgen deprivation drives prostate cancer cells into a glycolysis-coupled senescence-like state.

papers.title: TISCH3: an expanded resource for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The Tumor Immune Single Cell Hub (TISCH) is a curated resource for exploring single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from the tumor microenvironment. papers.title: SpaCoDA: fast compositional deconvolution maps recurrent cellular niches across hundreds of spatial transcriptomics sections
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Spot-based spatial transcriptomics such as 10x Visium measures a mixture of cells in each spot. Results We present SpaCoDA, which fits each spot by variance-weighted non-negative least squares against a reference signature, re-estimates a gene-level platform factor between iterations, and converts RNA shares into cell fractions using cell-size and marker-capture factors. Niches are identified within each section from fused compositional (Aitchison distances) and spatial distances, and their prototypes are integrated across sections into meta-niches. Across 123 simulated configurations under three reference-mismatch scenarios, SpaCoDA was the only one of nine methods ranked within the top two on all four evaluation metrics in every scenario, second to RCTD in mean rank. On 12 imaging-derived datasets with known composition (six Xenium datasets, each evaluated at two annotation levels, and six CosMx/Xenium datasets from three patients), it achieved the best mean rank in every summary, while running 4 to about 1,800-fold faster than the other eight methods (233-fold faster than RCTD by median runtime) with the lowest peak memory. In breast cancer, the expression signature of a B-cell and plasma-cell meta-niche was associated with longer overall survival in TCGA-BRCA and METABRIC and was higher in tumors with a pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy in I-SPY2. In glioblastoma, signatures of a perivascular antigen-presenting myeloid meta-niche and of a proliferative, hypoxic meta-niche were associated with shorter survival in TCGA-GBM and three CGGA glioma cohorts. Conclusions SpaCoDA combines competitive accuracy with orders-of-magnitude lower computational cost, making composition and niche analysis practical at cohort scale. It provides a practical framework for such analyses, enabling disease subtyping and the identification of novel therapeutic targets, and shows promise for clinical translation.

papers.title: A periodontal Piezo1-dependent brain-bone interoceptive circuit couples occlusal force to craniofacial bone homeostasis.

papers.title: ASAOT: an accentuated structure-differentiated asymmetric optimal transport model for cell type and single-cell spatial mapping.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (STs) characterizes spatiotemporal gene expression and facilitates analysis of cellular architecture and cell-cell crosstalk within tissue microenvironments. Collectively, ASAOT addresses critical drawbacks of conventional methods via a sharpening regularization term, serving as a reliable tool for STs analysis and mechanism exploration of tissue spatial organization.

papers.title: Cellular Proliferation and Reprogramming in Pre-Metastatic Niches: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities.

While clinical validation remains an evolving frontier, targeting pre-metastatic niche priming represents a promising window that warrants rigorous clinical evaluation to intercept nascent metastasis before clinically detectable colonization occurs.

papers.title: Neuropeptides as neuroimmune modulators in chronic wound healing: mechanistic insights and emerging therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Continuous ex utero development of mouse zygotes to early organogenesis

papers.title: Confidence-guided spatial gene expression inference for reliability-aware prognostic analysis from histology

papers.title: Period-Specific Remodeling of Luminal Lineages and the Mammary Microenvironment in Dairy Goats

papers.title: RAD: A Read-structure Agnostic Demultiplexer for Single-Cell Long-Read Sequencing and Analysis
papers.abstract: Single-cell long-read sequencing (LRS) techniques enable the analysis of full transcript sequences within a cell. However, LRS introduces computational challenges for parsing information, often necessitating the development of custom workflows to handle complex read layouts, such as split combinatorial barcodes. To address these challenges, we introduce an error-robust, read-structure agnostic demultiplexer (RAD). In RAD, users can easily specify read structure, such as adapter sequence and relative barcode position, and can rapidly extract these elements for each read. RAD implements highly accurate barcode whitelist generation from long-read data alone, without the benefit of short-read support or priors while uniquely avoiding common but previously uncharacterized errors during demultiplexing. RAD's comprehensive barcode error correction protocols allow for more sensitive and precise barcode-read assignments. In synthetic and real-world benchmarks against gold-standard demultiplexers, RAD is faster and achieves better biological discovery capability in downstream gene expression analysis than existing pipelines. We show RAD can be applied to datasets ranging from high-definition long-read spatial transcriptomics to targeted long-read single-cell immune receptor sequencing, making it a powerful and scalable tool for both standard and custom long-read sequencing experiments.

papers.title: NOTCH3 p.R544C Drives Early Neurovascular Unit Dysfunction through Blood-Brain Barrier Failure, Complement Signalling and Metabolic Dysregulation
papers.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease is a major cause of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment, yet the mechanisms that initiate neurovascular dysfunction before irreversible brain injury remain poorly defined. CADASIL, caused by cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations, provides a genetically tractable model to resolve these early events. NOTCH3 p.R544C iPSC-derived endothelial cells showed impaired angiogenesis and migration, reduced barrier resistance, disrupted tight-junction organisation, and altered vascular, adhesion, and extracellular-matrix programmes. In multicellular BBB-like microtissues, these defects propagated across the neurovascular unit, producing disorganised vascular networks, enlarged luminal structures, and increased permeability, establishing BBB failure as an early disease layer. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed coordinated loss of endothelial BBB transport and efflux programmes with astrocytic complement, innate immune, and matrix-remodelling activation. Secretome profiling and patient-plasma measurements converged on complement- and matrix-associated mediators, including C1S and CLU, identifying complement-matrix activation as a second interconnected layer. Importantly, combined cilostazol and isosorbide mononitrate treatment improved barrier function and reduced selected complement- and matrix-associated proteins in mutant microtissues, supporting pharmacological reversibility of components of this early disease programme. Seahorse analysis further demonstrated reduced mitochondrial respiratory capacity associated with NOTCH3 p.R544C. In vivo, three-month-old mutant mice showed altered cerebral pyruvate metabolism and early microvascular abnormalities, whereas six-month-old mice developed more prominent extracellular-matrix, inflammatory, and gliovascular changes, supporting an age-dependent transition from early metabolic dysregulation to broader neurovascular remodelling. Together, these findings define NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL as an early multicellular neurovascular disorder organised across three interconnected mechanistic layers: BBB failure, complement-matrix signalling, and metabolic dysregulation, while identifying early BBB-centred dysfunction as a potentially tractable state before advanced cerebrovascular injury develops.

papers.title: Loss of contractile arteriolar smooth muscle cells and their GLP1R expression in human diabetic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists slow kidney disease progression in type 2 diabetes, and in the human kidney the receptor is localized mainly to arteriolar smooth muscle. In an independent single-nucleus atlas, smooth muscle GLP1R was lower in DKD than in reference kidneys, and smooth muscle content fell with arteriolar hyalinosis grade. In human DKD, arterioles lose contractile smooth muscle cells, and fewer of the remaining cells carry transcripts for the receptor targeted by GLP-1 receptor agonists at the disease stage in which these drugs are used. papers.title: SpaCut: Transcript-Aware Morphology Fusion for Robust Cell Segmentation in Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics (SST) offers unprecedented opportunities to decipher tissue architecture at subcellular resolution. Consequently, accurate cell segmentation is a fundamental prerequisite for analyzing SST data, as precise transcript assignment is essential for downstream single-cell interpretation. Existing methods often overlook the spatial organization of transcripts, rely on simplified geometric priors, or struggle to coordinate transcript-derived features with morphology-derived spatial guidance. This limitation restricts their adaptability to irregular cell shapes, often leading to transcript misassignment. To address this, we propose SpaCut, a unified deep learning framework designed to effectively integrate transcriptomic feature learning with dynamic morphological guidance. SpaCut comprises a Gene-Wise Attention (GWA) module and a Nuclei-Guided Attentive Fusion (NGAF) module. GWA encodes the high-dimensional transcript map and aggregates features across multiple depths. NGAF uses the encoded transcript features to modulate distance-based nuclear softmasks and refine nucleus-anchored cell boundaries through progressive training. Extensive evaluations across seven datasets from diverse platforms (including Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE, and Stereo-seq) demonstrate that SpaCut significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both segmentation accuracy and consistency with single-cell reference data. The source code is available at https://github.com/wenwenmin/SpaCut.

papers.title: Phase-Programmed Microneedles Enable Sequential Hydrogen and Quercetin Release for Scar-Reduced Regeneration of Burn Wounds.
papers.abstract: Burn wounds complicated by bacterial infection and fibrotic scarring remain a major clinical challenge, demanding therapeutics capable of coordinated infection control, inflammation modulation, and tissue regeneration. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed that QR/AB-MNs orchestrate a broad anti-fibrotic transcriptional program, concurrently attenuating pro-fibrotic signaling, cell-extracellular matrix interactions, and collagen synthesis. papers.title: Human Cortical Gene Programs Link Regional Expression with Laminar and Local Tissue Organization.
papers.abstract: Understanding brain function requires characterizing gene expression across cells and cortical tissue. papers.title: FViT: A Foundation-Tokenized Vision Transformer with Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Scale Ensembling for Deep Learning-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathology.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue morphology but is too costly for routine clinical use, motivating prediction of expression from hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) images. papers.title: A Review of Tooth-Related Bone Regeneration Research Based on Occlusion Using Bioactive Glass and Piezoelectric Ceramics.
papers.abstract: The functional regeneration of alveolar bone defects, which encompasses alveolar bone resorption and the destruction of periodontal supporting bone structures, is a research hotspot in the fields of oral and maxillofacial rehabilitation as well as periodontitis treatment. It also represents a core technical challenge for achieving periodontal tissue reconstruction in clinical practice. Commonly used traditional bone repair materials generally have insufficient bioactivity, limited osteoinductive efficacy, and poor mismatch with the physiological microenvironment of natural bone, making it difficult to meet the demands for efficient repair and long-term functional healing of complex alveolar bone defects. Bioactive glass (BG) combines excellent biocompatibility, osteoconductive properties, and intrinsic bone-inductive potential. It can regulate bone metabolic remodeling processes through the sustained release of bioactive ions and has become one of the most promising core functional materials in the field of bone regeneration and repair. Piezoelectric ceramics (PCs) possess a unique direct piezoelectric effect, capable of converting external mechanical loads into endogenous electrical signals, achieving precise coupling and transformation between mechanical energy and bioelectric signals. With the stimulation provided by physiological masticatory stress, piezoelectric ceramics can create a bioelectric microenvironment similar to natural bone tissue, thereby regulating the proliferation, differentiation, and mineralization of osteoblasts and promoting bone tissue regeneration and repair. This article systematically reviews the bioactive glass-piezoelectric ceramic composite system, focusing on the core mechanisms by which occlusal mechanical stress-mediated piezoelectric effects regulate alveolar bone regeneration. It provides an in-depth analysis of the osteogenic and angiogenic promoting effects of this composite material, summarizes the structural advantages, performance characteristics, and clinical application potential of the composite system, and aims to provide a systematic theoretical basis and technical reference for the iterative development of oral bone regeneration materials and precise clinical restorative applications.

papers.title: Neuroimmune networks underlying cutaneous inflammation: bidirectional crosstalk between the nervous system and immune cells.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous inflammation is a pathological process underlying various skin conditions. Its high prevalence, frequent recurrence, and complex pathogenesis present significant clinical challenges. Emerging evidence highlights the central role of neuroimmune interactions in cutaneous inflammation. Activation of these neuronal pathways induces the release of neuropeptides that promote vasodilation, immune cell recruitment, and neuronal sensitization. Furthermore, immune cells, keratinocytes, and fibroblasts engage in dynamic bidirectional communication with cutaneous nerves, collectively shaping the progression of inflammation. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in research on the neuroimmune networks underlying cutaneous inflammation, aiming to provide a theoretical foundation for a more comprehensive understanding of these disorders and the development of novel therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Fibrosis: Past Insights, Current Challenges, and Therapeutic Frontiers.
papers.abstract: Fibrosis is a maladaptive repair process marked by fibroblast activation, myofibroblast accumulation, and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, which can compromise tissue architecture and organ function. Its causes, cellular niches, reversibility, and therapeutic windows vary across the lung, liver, kidney, and heart. This review outlines the canonical pathological processes of tissue injury, inflammation, fibroblast activation, and matrix deposition, then discusses emerging evidence on metabolic reprogramming, hypoxia, epigenetic regulation, and mechanotransduction, while also considering cellular senescence and immune-stromal communication. We focus on the lactate-lactylation axis, which links altered metabolism to transcriptional and protein regulation through lactate production, transport, signaling, and histone or nonhistone lactylation. Evidence from numerous studies suggests that this axis may shape fibrosis-associated cell states, but its effects vary by organ, cell type, and disease stage. We therefore distinguish among associative observations, functional validation, and site-specific validation and assess whether lactylation acts as a driver, amplifier, or marker of fibrotic remodeling. We also evaluate current antifibrotic therapies and discuss metabolic and epigenetic interventions, modulation of immune-stromal interactions, and matrix-directed and precision-delivery strategies. Clinical translation requires context-specific causal evidence, standardized detection methods, biomarker-guided patient selection, and endpoints that distinguish slowed progression from fibrosis reversal.

papers.title: Digitally Planned Single-Stage Immediate Implant Placement and Periodontal Resective Surgery Followed by Dynamic Provisionalization: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Esthetic rehabilitation of the anterior maxilla may require simultaneous management of an extraction site and the periodontal architecture of the adjacent dentition. Altered passive eruption is often associated with discrepancies in gingival margins, clinical crown proportions, and osseous architecture that affect anterior esthetics. This case describes a digitally planned, single-stage approach combining immediate implant placement with periodontal resective surgery for correction of altered passive eruption. Methods: A 36-year-old female presented with a maxillary right central incisor affected by advanced external cervical root resorption, requiring extraction. Following clinical, radiographic, and digital assessment, a single-stage surgical intervention comprising extraction, immediate implant placement, hard- and soft-tissue augmentation, and periodontal resective surgery was performed in the maxillary anterior dentition. After a three-month healing period, the standard abutment was replaced with a multifunctional healing abutment. Provisionalization was initiated one month later, involving progressive modification of the emergence profile and peri-implant soft-tissue conditioning, followed by definitive restoration. Results: Healing was uneventful. At 1 year after placement of the definitive crown, the implant-supported restoration exhibited stable peri-implant crestal bone levels, complete mesial and distal papilla fill, and a harmonious soft-tissue contour relative to the adjacent natural central incisor. Conclusions: This case illustrates the feasibility of combining implant rehabilitation and correction of altered passive eruption within a single-stage treatment strategy. The clinical and radiographic findings at the 1-year post-restoration follow-up were consistent with stable peri-implant tissues and harmonious periodontal architecture.

papers.title: Immediate Subcrestal Morse-Taper Implant in a Fresh Extraction Socket, with Management of an Early Interdental Septal Complication Using Platelet-Rich Fibrin: A 56-Month Case Report.
papers.abstract: Background: Immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla shortens treatment time, but has long been associated with marginal bone loss, most often reported for equicrestal, internal-hex systems. Laboratory studies of Morse taper connections report reduced abutment micromovement and, for some assemblies, reduced microbial leakage, which has been proposed to make deep subcrestal placement biologically acceptable. Methods: We report a 62-year-old healthy man with a vertical root fracture of the maxillary right central incisor, treated with flapless extraction and immediate placement of a 4.5 × 15 mm Morse taper implant, 2 mm subcrestal to the mid-buccal bony crest (insertion torque 45 N·cm; implant stability quotient 72), with freeze-dried bone allograft in the jump space and an immediate non-functional provisional restoration. Early healing was complicated by wound breakdown with a probeable defect at the distal interdental septum (probing depth 5 mm from the adjacent soft tissue margin to exposed bone at its base), interpreted clinically as suspected localized septal osteonecrosis (no biopsy or culture was obtained) and presenting in a manner resembling alveolar osteitis. This complication was managed conservatively with six weekly applications of platelet-rich fibrin, after which healing was uneventful. A definitive cement-retained porcelain-fused-to-zirconia crown on a zirconia-titanium abutment was delivered 5 months after implant placement. Results: The first radiographic bone-to-implant contact lay 1.5 mm (mesial) and 2.0 mm (distal) apical to the platform at 15 months, at the level of the first implant thread, and 2.0 mm on both aspects at 56 months. The total early bone change could not be quantified because no comparable baseline measurement exists. Between 15 and 56 months, the non-standardized periapical radiographs showed no evidence of progressive resorption (distal level unchanged; mesial 0.5 mm difference of uncertain significance). After resolution of the early complication, the peri-implant tissues remained clinically healthy, and the esthetic result, documented with an adapted, clinician-assessed application of the pink and white esthetic score, was stable (17/20 at 15 and 56 months); the patient, himself a dentist, reported being satisfied with the outcome. Conclusions: In this well-selected patient, immediate placement and non-functional provisionalization of a subcrestal Morse taper implant were followed by an early septal complication that resolved after conservative management including platelet-rich fibrin, and subsequently by clinically healthy peri-implant tissues and no radiographic evidence of progressive crestal resorption between 15 and 56 months. As an uncontrolled single case with several concurrent favorable factors, this report documents the clinical course of the complication and its management and cannot attribute the outcome to any individual treatment component.

papers.title: Autogenous Tooth Sticky Bone Graft for Maxillary Radicular Cyst Defects: A Retrospective Case Series.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Radicular cysts (RCs) in the maxillary anterior aesthetic zone can cause substantial buccal bone loss and complicate implant rehabilitation. This retrospective case series evaluated autogenous tooth sticky bone (ATSB) from impacted third molars, covered with concentrated growth factor (CGF) membranes, for reconstructing these defects before delayed implant placement. Methods: Twenty patients with maxillary anterior RC-associated defects and ≥2 nonfunctional impacted third molars were treated under general anesthesia. ATSB was prepared chairside from partially demineralized dentin matrix (425-850 μm) and autogenous fibrin glue, placed after cyst enucleation, and covered with two CGF membranes. Implants were placed after 4 months. Clinical records, panoramic radiographs, and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans were reviewed. Results: The cohort comprised 12 males and 8 females (mean age, 31 years; range, 20-40). All donor and recipient sites healed uneventfully, without recorded infection or graft failure. Four-month CBCT showed increased radiopacity and trabecular-like structures within the defects. All implants achieved primary stability (implant stability quotient > 70) and showed radiographic findings consistent with osseointegration at 3 months; definitive restorations were recorded as functionally and aesthetically acceptable. Conclusions: In selected patients, ATSB with CGF membrane coverage may be a feasible option for post-enucleation reconstruction and delayed implant rehabilitation without an additional bone-harvesting site. Controlled studies with volumetric, histological, and long-term assessment are needed.

papers.title: Five- to Nine-Year Clinical and Radiographic Performance of Morse-Tapered Hybrid Dental Implants: A Retrospective Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The long-term clinical performance of Morse-tapered hybrid dental implants remains insufficiently documented. This retrospective cohort study evaluated implant, prosthesis, and abutment survival, marginal bone loss (MBL), and the influence of implant- and patient-related variables over a follow-up period of up to 108 months. Methods: Patients who received Morse-tapered hybrid dental implants between 2017 and 2020 and had at least 5 years of follow-up were retrospectively evaluated. Implant, prosthesis, and abutment survival, as well as radiographic MBL, were assessed. MBL was determined using standardized periapical radiographs obtained from baseline to 108 months. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and log-rank tests were used to evaluate survival outcomes, whereas longitudinal MBL was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models accounting for clustering at the patient level. Results: A total of 367 Helix GM® implants placed in 79 patients (mean age: 53.5 ± 13.4 years) were included, with follow-up ranging from 60 to 108 months. Cumulative implant survival was 99.2% at 108 months, with all implant failures occurring within the first year of function. Prosthesis survival ranged from 90.0% to 95.8%, and abutment survival ranged from 99.1% to 100%. Mean MBL remained below 1.0 mm throughout long-term follow-up. Implant survival and MBL were not significantly influenced by insertion torque, bone quality, loading protocol, or prosthetic rehabilitation design (p > 0.05). Smoking and depression were associated with implant failure in the study cohort (p Conclusions: Within the limitations of this retrospective, single-center cohort, the evaluated Morse-tapered hybrid dental implant system demonstrated favorable long-term clinical and radiographic performance, with high implant survival, favorable prosthetic outcomes, and limited marginal bone loss over up to 108 months of function. Implant survival and marginal bone stability were not significantly influenced by insertion torque, bone quality, loading protocol, or prosthetic rehabilitation design under the clinical conditions evaluated. These findings should be interpreted within the context of the specific implant system, clinical setting, and patient population investigated.

papers.title: The probiotic role of nitrite-producing Schaalia odontolytica in peri-implant health and early inflammation via pathogen inhibition and anti-inflammation.
papers.abstract: BackgroundNitrite has antimicrobial properties and can be converted to nitric oxide (NO), a gaseous signalling molecule. In the oral cavity, Schaalia odontolytica (S. odontolytica) reduces ingested nitrate to nitrite. Its association with healthy peri-implant tissues suggests a role in mitigating peri-implantitis by reshaping pathogenicity of other bacteria and modulating host immunity. However, interactions among S. odontolytica, oral pathogens, and host cells remain unclear.Materials and methodsS. odontolytica strains isolated and identified from healthy peri-implant sites were studied. Nitrite levels were measured using the Griess assay, and nitrite-related gene expression was analysed by quantitative PCR (qPCR). Competitive co-culture, bacterial adhesion, and assays for reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation inhibition assessed effects on pathogen adhesion and inflammatory stimulation. Inflammatory cytokine expression was assessed by qPCR and Western blotting. Therapeutic potential was evaluated in a rat peri-implantitis model.ResultsS. odontolytica showed significant nitrite-producing capability. In vitro, it inhibited adhesion of oral pathogens to host cells, reduced ROS generation, and downregulated inflammatory cytokines. In the rat model, local application alleviated disease progression.ConclusionS. odontolytica isolated from healthy peri-implant tissues alleviates peri-implant mucositis via nitrite production, inhibiting pathogenic bacteria, reducing host-cell ROS burst, and downregulating key pro-inflammatory cytokines.

papers.title: Serum Levels of Various Vitamin D3 Metabolites and the Vitamin D3 Metabolite Ratios in Peri-Implantitis: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This cross-sectional pilot study aimed to investigate serum levels of vitamin D3 and their association with the clinical parameters and inflammatory processes in peri-implantitis. Methods: A total of 30 patients with peri-implantitis and 30 healthy controls were recruited at the University Clinic of Dentistry, Medical University of Vienna. Peri-implantitis was defined by the presence of radiographic bone loss > 3 mm, along with pocket depth (PD) > 5 mm and bleeding on probing (BoP). The panel of 20 cytokines was measured in peri-implant crevicular fluid (PICF) samples using an ELISA-based Luminex multiplex assay. Peripheral blood was collected, and serum was isolated. To assess the level of vitamin D3, serum concentration of 25(OH)D3, 1,25(OH)2D3 and 24,25(OH)2D3 were measured by ELISA and the ratios 24,25(OH)2D3:25(OH)D3 (VMR1) and 1,25(OH)2D3:25(OH)D3 (VMR2) were calculated. Results: The experimental groups were age- and gender-matched (p > 0.05), while all clinical parameters were significantly increased in peri-implantitis compared to the healthy controls (p = 0.000). No difference in the serum levels of all vitamin D3 metabolites and their ratios was found between the peri-implantitis and healthy controls. In the peri-implantitis group, a significant positive correlation was found between 24,25(OH)2D3 and interleukin-17. Furthermore, significant positive correlations were found between VMR1 and osteoprotegerin, VMR1 and osteopontin, and VMR2 and osteopontin. Bone loss showed a tendency toward a positive correlation with 25(OH)D3 and a negative correlation with VMR1 and VMR2. Conclusions: Although no direct association was found between vitamin D3 status and peri-implantitis, vitamin D3 metabolite levels correlated with osteo-inflammatory markers.

papers.title: Orthopaedic Implants in the Oncologic and Irradiated Bone Environment: A Review.
papers.abstract: Patients who require an orthopaedic implant after cancer treatment present four linked problems: a bone bed damaged by radiotherapy or chemotherapy, large reconstructions under high mechanical load, a high risk of infection, and hardware that degrades the imaging and radiotherapy planning on which oncologic follow-up depends. This narrative review examines how each problem alters implant performance and which design responses have clinical support. Radiotherapy roughly doubles dental implant failure, is associated with loosening, infection, and periprosthetic fracture after arthroplasty, and leads to non-union in most radiation-associated femoral fractures treated by internal fixation. Deep infection affects about one in ten tumour endoprostheses. Additively manufactured porous titanium and porous tantalum support bone ingrowth, but follow-up rarely exceeds five years, and their large surface area may favour bacterial colonisation. Silver, iodine, and antibiotic-loaded hydrogel coatings are associated with fewer infections in observational studies, with low certainty. Carbon-fibre-reinforced polyetheretherketone (PEEK) reduces imaging artefact and dose perturbation, and biodegradable magnesium avoids hardware removal, but neither has a proven advantage in oncologic reconstruction. Throughout, evidence is labelled by its source-oncologic, extrapolated, or preclinical-and the comparative studies still needed are specified.

papers.title: Prosthetic Rehabilitation of Posterior Edentulous Regions in a Beagle Mandible Using Canine-Specific Dental Implants.
papers.abstract: This case report describes the surgical, prosthetic, radiographic, and histologic outcomes of prosthetic rehabilitation of a healed edentulous mandibular ridge in a beagle using canine-specific dental implant systems. Two customized implant systems with distinct macrogeometry, thread configuration, collar design, and prosthetic connection characteristics were used to restore the edentulous sites. Digital intraoral impressions were obtained after an 8-week healing period and used to develop customized CAD/CAM-fabricated implant-supported prostheses. Implant stability was assessed by resonance frequency analysis at Weeks 8 and 26, with individual implants showing variable changes in implant stability quotient (ISQ) values. Clinical observations were documented during follow-up, which extended to 24 months after prosthetic delivery, whereas radiographic assessments were performed immediately after implant placement, at 8 weeks, and after prosthetic delivery. Terminal histologic evaluation demonstrated direct bone-to-implant contact, with mean bone-to-implant contact values of 53.2% and 62.6% for Systems A and B, respectively. This case illustrates the application of customized implant designs and digital prosthetic workflows in canine mandibular rehabilitation. The findings provide descriptive clinical and histologic observations, but long-term implant stability and radiographic bone-level maintenance cannot be established from this single-animal case.

papers.title: Peri-Implant Femoral Fractures Around Intramedullary Nails: A Multicenter Case Series.
papers.abstract: Background: Peri-implant fractures following intramedullary nailing of femoral fractures are an increasing concern in elderly orthopedic trauma patients. These fractures pose significant clinical challenges due to altered load transmission in osteoporotic bone, comorbidities and complex fracture patterns. Optimal management remains unclear and secondary prevention strategies such as osteoporosis treatment are underutilized. Materials and Methods: This retrospective multicenter study analyzed 11 patients who sustained peri-implant fractures after intramedullary femoral nailing between 2015 and 2022. Data collected included demographics, comorbidities, fracture characteristics, implant details, postoperative rehabilitation protocols, complications and functional outcomes measured by WOMAC and SF-12 scores. Results: The mean patient age was 85 years, with fractures most frequently occurring at the distal and proximal nail tips. Cardiovascular comorbidities were prevalent, with an mean Charlson Comorbidity Index of 4.27. Nearly half the fractures followed low-energy trauma such as falls. Complications affected 45.5% of patients and included infections, myocardial infarction, periprosthetic fracture and one death. Among available postoperative assessments, the mean WOMAC score was 49.0 (n = 10), and the mean SF-12 physical component score was 25.0 (n = 11). Functional outcomes were generally poor and only one patient was on anti-osteoporotic therapy. The small cohort does not allow reliable identification of implant-related risk factors. Conclusions: A personalized treatment framework integrating fracture morphology, implant stability, bone stock, comorbidity burden, joint status, and rehabilitation potential is clinically relevant, although this descriptive series cannot validate a decision algorithm. Peri-implant fractures in elderly, comorbid patients represent a complex clinical problem with high complication rates and poor functional recovery. The low rate of osteoporosis treatment highlights an important area for improvement. Management should be tailored to fracture morphology, existing fixation, bone stock, associated joint disease, and patient frailty. Larger prospective studies are needed to establish standardized treatment protocols and improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Extracellular Vesicles as Diagnostic Tools and Pathogenic Mediators in Periodontitis and Peri-Implantitis: A Systematic Review of Human Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Periodontitis and peri-implantitis are biofilm-associated inflammatory diseases in which conventional clinical and radiographic measures mainly reflect accumulated tissue damage, rather than ongoing molecular activity. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry proteins, nucleic acids and immune mediators that may reflect disease activity and treatment response. This systematic review evaluated human evidence on EVs in periodontitis and peri-implant diseases, asking which signals are consistent, whether EV measures add value to existing biomarkers, and which gaps must be addressed first. Methods: The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261277287). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched, with citation searching. Human studies of exosomes or specifically characterized EVs were eligible. Risk of bias was appraised with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or ROBINS-I. Synthesis was qualitative and structured by biomarker class, biofluid, consistency and isolation method. Results: Sixteen studies were included. The most consistent signal was increased EV concentration in gingival and peri-implant crevicular fluid, although the three supporting studies came from one research network. EV-associated complement proteins and cytokines implicated overlapping inflammatory pathways, indicating consistency at the pathway level, rather than at the level of individual molecules. However, no specific EV-associated microRNA was consistently validated across independent patient cohorts, and tetraspanin-associated findings varied according to the marker examined (CD9, CD63 or CD81). These findings suggest that the biological relevance of EV-associated inflammatory cargo is more consistently supported than the diagnostic reproducibility of individual EV biomarkers. Discrimination estimates were highest in the smallest cohorts, divergent findings coincided with differences in isolation method, and no study compared EV markers head-to-head with established biomarkers. No study followed healthy individuals to incident disease. Conclusions: EVs are biologically plausible candidates for disease characterization and treatment monitoring, but certainty is low for diagnosis and treatment monitoring and very low for therapeutic efficacy, and their incremental value over existing tools has not been tested. Harmonized host-EV methods, head-to-head comparisons and independent validation are priorities, followed by prospective risk-prediction cohorts.

papers.title: Osteomyelitis Following Mandibular Third Molar Extraction: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Clinical and Radiographic Characteristics and Time to Resolution.
papers.abstract: BackgroundOsteomyelitis after mandibular third molar extraction is a rare but serious complication that may require prolonged treatment and additional surgical intervention. Patients diagnosed with osteomyelitis after mandibular third molar extraction and treated between January 2020 and September 2025 were included. Patients with pre-existing odontogenic infection or osteomyelitis, a history of antiresorptive, antiangiogenic or immunosuppressive medication use, or prior head and neck radiation therapy were excluded.Predictor variablesThe predictor variable was a set of heterogenous factors categorized as demographic, clinical, radiographic, and treatment-related factors.Main outcome variableThe primary outcome was time to resolution, defined as the time from symptom onset to complete clinical resolution of osteomyelitis, with resolution defined as the absence of clinical signs and symptoms of infection.CovariatesNot applicable.AnalysesKaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to estimate time to resolution. Univariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were performed. Statistical significance was set at P ResultsThe sample was composed of 16 subjects with a mean age of 47.0 ± 14.5 years, and 12 (75.0%) were male. The median of time to resolution was 11.0 weeks (interquartile range: 5.8 to 12.8) and the median follow-up duration was 8.5 months (interquartile range: 6.0 to 14.5). papers.title: Photon-Counting CT in Musculoskeletal Imaging: Emerging Applications and Clinical Implications.
papers.abstract: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) is an emerging imaging technology that has the potential to significantly advance musculoskeletal (MSK) imaging through improvements in spatial resolution, spectral imaging, dose efficiency, and material characterization. Unlike conventional energy-integrating detector CT systems, PCCT directly detects and classifies individual X-ray photons according to their energy, enabling enhanced tissue differentiation, reduced electronic noise, and improved visualization of fine osseous structures. These properties are particularly relevant in musculoskeletal imaging, where accurate assessment of cortical bone, trabecular microarchitecture, cartilage, crystal deposition, and peri-implant structures is essential. Recent studies have demonstrated promising applications of PCCT across a broad range of MSK conditions, including fracture imaging, osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthropathies, crystal deposition diseases, CT arthrography, bone marrow assessment, and postoperative imaging around metallic implants. In addition, spectral imaging capabilities allow advanced applications such as virtual monoenergetic imaging, material decomposition, and virtual non-calcium imaging, which may improve detection of bone marrow edema, cartilage abnormalities, and crystal composition. However, the clinical maturity of these applications is still heterogeneous, with the most valid evidence for crystal arthropathies and imaging around orthopedic implants where the advantages offered by PCCT are more evident and are more clinically relevant, while most other applications remain investigational. Despite these advantages, several challenges remain, including increased data complexity, computational demands, cost, and the need for further clinical validation. This review summarizes the technical principles of PCCT, discusses its emerging musculoskeletal applications, and evaluates its potential advantages and limitations compared with existing imaging modalities.

papers.title: Botulinum toxin type A for prevention and treatment of hypertrophic and keloid scars from surgical and sharp traumatic wounds: Protocol for an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundBotulinum toxin type A has been increasingly investigated for both scar prevention and the treatment of established scars. Although multiple systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and network meta-analyses have evaluated its effectiveness, their conclusions vary due to differences in scope, methodological quality, and interpretations of clinical outcomes. This umbrella review aims to comprehensively synthesize the available evidence while assessing methodological quality, overlap, and certainty of evidence.ObjectivesTo provide a comprehensive summary of systematic review evidence on botulinum toxin type A for scar prevention and treatment by distinguishing prophylactic from therapeutic applications, evaluating methodological quality, quantifying overlap among primary studies, and appraising the certainty of evidence.MethodsThis protocol follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) and guidance from the Joanna Briggs Institute and the Cochrane Handbook for overviews of reviews. A systematic search will be conducted across major biomedical databases with supplementary manual searching. Eligible studies will include systematic reviews, with or without meta-analysis, and network meta-analyses including randomized controlled trials that evaluate botulinum toxin type A for fresh sharp wounds or established scars. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, data extraction, and methodological quality assessment using AMSTAR-2. Overlap among primary studies will be evaluated using a citation matrix and the Corrected Covered Area (CCA). Findings will be synthesized narratively, prioritizing evidence from the highest-quality, most comprehensive, and most recent systematic reviews, while other eligible reviews will be used to assess consistency and explain discrepancies. Certainty of evidence will be evaluated using an adapted GRADE approach for umbrella reviews.DiscussionThis umbrella review will address inconsistencies in scar outcome measures, botulinum toxin administration protocols, and prophylactic versus therapeutic applications. By applying rigorous and transparent methodology, it aims to provide reliable evidence to inform clinical practice, support future research, and improve scar management.RegistrationPROSPERO: CRD420251175682.

papers.title: Optimized Tissue Microarray for In Situ Characterization of Central Nervous System Tumors Using a Spatial Transcriptomics Platform.
papers.abstract: We present a standardized, end-to-end development and application of a Xenium tissue microarray (TMA) to profile glioblastoma, meningioma, schwannomas, and pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). The workflow covers: (i) pathology-guided selection of representative tumor regions (including tumor core and immune-rich interfaces when available); (ii) core extraction and array design to balance patient groups and clinical timepoints within each block; (iii) TMA embedding, sectioning, and slide preparation compatible with Xenium chemistry; (iv) assay execution, imaging, transcript decoding, and cell segmentation. This high-throughput workflow is specific for generating TMAs optimized for Xenium in situ spatial transcriptomics for different central nervous system (CNS) tumor types. Spatial profiling of CNS tumors in focused studies (i.e., clinical trials) is often limited by scarce tissue, heterogeneity across tumor regions, and batch effects introduced by processing specimens across multiple runs. Building a Xenium-compatible TMA enables uniform handling of many patient samples and time points on a single slide, thereby improving cross-sample consistency while reducing reagent cost and turnaround time. We also highlight practical troubleshooting steps encountered in tumor sections, such as tissue loss and segmentation artifacts in highly cellular or necrotic regions. Representative results are summarized using key assay quality metrics to assess performance across cores, including usable tissue area, numbers of segmented cells/nuclei per core, decoded transcript yield, genes detected per cell, and the fraction of transcripts assigned to cells. This protocol yields reproducible, cell-resolved spatial gene expression maps across multiple tumor regions in parallel, enabling direct comparison of naïve and recurrent disease within a therapeutic context. This TMA approach is broadly applicable to both untreated and treated biospecimens, where standardized processing and scalable spatial profiling are essential for biomarker discovery and mechanistic insight.
