papers.title: Single-Vesicle Analysis, Spatial Deconvolution and Functional Circuit Mapping in Extracellular Vesicle Biology.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles encode a universal language of intercellular communication-the 'ommunicome'-yet clinical translation has been constrained by extreme EV heterogeneity and the inability to trace circulating mRNA to its cellular origin. papers.title: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Correlation Improves the Prediction of Anticancer Drug Candidates.
papers.abstract: Predicting the anticancer effects of compounds is critical for computational drug evaluation. Ultimately, the proposed method provides a robust, region-aware computational framework for accurately characterizing the anticancer properties of compounds and offers a more nuanced paradigm for transcriptomics-based drug evaluation.

We examined relationships among research themes, their cited foundations, and their temporal representation.MethodsWeb of Science Core Collection and PubMed were searched for publications dated from 1900 through July 1, 2026. After deduplication and screening, 587 English-language articles and reviews were included. Bibliometric networks were analyzed using VOSviewer, R, and bibliometrix. Document-level cosine overlaps between keyword and reference clusters were evaluated using stratified permutations with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Temporal analyses used keyword proportions and citation-weighted reference-year profiles within three descriptive windows. Sensitivity analyses examined database composition, inclusion thresholds, and individual recent references.ResultsPublication output increased after 2021. China had the largest publication output, while the United States had the highest citation count and international-collaboration total link strength. Co-citation and keyword analyses identified four and three domains, respectively. K3-C2 had the largest observed cosine score (0.661), exceeding its null mean by 0.039 (adjusted P = 0.0072); K1-C1 also exceeded its null expectation (adjusted P = 0.0012). Among keyword-available publications, spatial transcriptomics increased from 0.0% to 1.7% and 8.3% across the three windows. The recent reference subset contained five references, all published in 2024; its C2 share was sensitive to individual references. Keyword-cluster agreement was high across database sources and moderate at the stricter occurrence threshold.ConclusionThe analysis identifies relationships among immune, cellular, stromal, spatial, and computational literature domains and descriptive changes in keyword representation. These findings provide a quantitative literature framework for further investigation of HNSCC immune profiling.

papers.title: Deciphering the Mechanisms Underlying Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer through Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Technologies: Current Approaches and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies are recent high-throughput sequencing advancements that enable transcriptome-wide profiling and characterization of cellular populations at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue spatial context. Their integration has been increasingly applied to cancer research, facilitating a deeper understanding of tumor biology and improving diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Growing evidence suggests that combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with ST offers a robust approach for exploring mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance. Together, these technologies support the prediction and monitoring of treatment responses and help identify novel therapeutic targets by revealing critical signaling pathways and immune cell populations associated with resistance. Artificial intelligence, including deep learning, computer vision, and generative models, further enhances the integration and analysis of data generated by scRNA-seq and ST, contributing to tumor resistance research. This review summarizes recent advances in the integrated application of scRNA-seq and ST to study tumor resistance and discusses the opportunities, challenges, and future directions of these technologies as a theoretical foundation for identifying therapeutic targets and developing treatment strategies.

papers.title: Multiplex immunohistochemistry in multiple myeloma: principles, spatial profiling applications, and emerging frontiers in immuno-oncology.
papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) progression and therapeutic resistance are dictated by the bone marrow microenvironment (BMME). Conventional single-marker immunohistochemistry (IHC) cannot resolve the complex cellular neighborhoods, non-cellular signaling networks, and spatial exclusion patterns that characterize this disease. Multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) and allied high-plex spatial imaging technologies now enable simultaneous visualization of 6 to over 60 protein targets on a single formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) section while preserving tissue architecture. This review first establishes a rigorous technical foundation by reclassifying mIHC and related high-dimensional imaging platforms according to their detection readout modality-fluorescence spectral unmixing/tyramide signal amplification (TSA) cyclic staining, DNA-barcode cyclic hybridization, metal-isotope mass spectrometric imaging, and regional-photolysis digital spatial profiling-and by clarifying several long-standing technical misconceptions (e.g., the historical relationship between PhenoCycler and Vectra Polaris, the cyclic nature of the Opal/TSA workflow, and the true elution chemistry of CODEX and t-CyCIF). We then present an expanded, bone-marrow-specific horizontal comparison of mIHC against flow cytometry, mass cytometry (CyTOF), imaging mass cytometry (IMC)/multiplexed ion beam imaging (MIBI), and spatial transcriptomics. Building on this technical scaffold, we organize the biological and clinical applications of mIHC along the natural disease continuum-monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) → smoldering myeloma (SMM) → newly diagnosed MM (NDMM) → post-treatment residual disease → relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) → extramedullary disease (EMD)-integrating T-cell, stromal, myeloid, and NK-cell compartments together with cytokine networks, metabolic competition, and bone-remodeling signals. We further delineate realized multimodal integration paradigms (mIHC combined with spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, digital spatial profiling, and artificial intelligence) and, separately, the technical, economic, and workflow bottlenecks-including spectral overlap, antibody cross-reactivity, turnaround time, cost, and the choice between bone marrow clot and decalcified trephine specimens-that currently constrain clinical translation. As methodological workflows for decalcified bone marrow specimens mature, mIHC is transitioning from a research tool to a critical component of precision immuno-oncology, offering actionable insights for overcoming CAR-T resistance and improving risk stratification.

papers.title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
papers.abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. However, NMF is mathematically ill-posed and a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the inherent ill-posedness and improve solution accuracy remains lacking. In our previous work, we investigated the necessary requirements for a given bulk RNA-seq dataset to satisfy the solvability conditions in NMF theory. Based on its weak solvability conditions of NMF, a new pipeline of pseudo-bulk tissue data augmented, geometric structure guided NMF model (GSNMF+) has been developed. As a semi-supervised model, it utilizes available single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data and has shown obvious improvements in scenarios where the target bulk data contain singular cellular compositions. Nevertheless, when the available scRNA-seq data are not fully consistent with the underlying cell-type-specific GEPs present in the bulk RNA-seq data, it remains a challenge that the deconvolution accuracy will significantly decrease. In this paper, we propose an iterative GSNMF algorithm to address this challenge. First, we propose a new computational algorithm for the GSNMF method (termed as the inner iteration) and provide a theoretical proof of its convergence. We then introduce an iterative process (termed as the outer iteration) to reduce potential discrepancies between available scRNA-seq and the latent cell type specific GEPs in the bulk-tissue data. The proposed methods are evaluated on both synthetic and realistic scRNA-seq data generated bulk-tissue datasets and have shown significant improvements in deconvolution accuracy, particularly in settings where the reference scRNA-seq data are inconsistent.

Fibro_IL1R1, Fibro_C7, and SMC_CNN1 were more abundant in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups, with higher activity of pathways related to inflammation and ECM remodeling. Tip endothelial cells were more abundant in Old Hsa and Old Mmu groups, with higher angiogenesis-related pathway activity, whereas venous endothelial cells had higher activity of pathways related to inflammation and ECM remodeling. In summary, our study characterizes remodeling features of the immune microenvironment and tissue architecture associated with prostate aging and BPH across species.

papers.title: Autonomous systems in oral and maxillofacial surgery: a narrative review of current applications, regulatory considerations, and medicolegal implications.
papers.abstract: Robotic and artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly described as autonomous in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS), although the operational meaning of that term varies widely across devices and procedures. This narrative review aims to classify robotic systems in OMS by level of autonomy and evidence stage, describe AI-driven surgical planning tools, and examine the regulatory status and liability implications of both. A PubMed search combining OMS procedural and anatomical terms with autonomy descriptors was conducted on March 2, 2026, supplemented by manual citation tracking, and findings were synthesized narratively. Dental implant placement accounts for most clinical activity. The single US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared OMS system provides haptic guidance only and does not execute any step independently. Other systems, none currently FDA-cleared, carry out the osteotomy and implant placement along a surgeon-approved plan and have been reported in patient series across single-tooth, full-arch, zygomatic, pterygoid, and sinus augmentation procedures. Beyond implants, a laser osteotome has performed Le Fort I cuts in a multicenter patient trial. Systems demonstrating autonomous mandibular tumor resection, maxillary repositioning, robotic orthognathic execution, and soft tissue tumor resection remain preclinical. AI-driven tools can segment craniomaxillofacial anatomy, identify landmarks, and generate surgical plans with accuracy comparable to expert reference standards, but their outputs are generally not linked to robotic execution in current OMS workflows. Competency standards, society guidelines, and specialty-specific consent language have not developed in parallel, possibly leaving the operating surgeon as the default bearer of risk when employing these technologies.

papers.title: Endocardial TIE1 synergizes with TIE2 to regulate the atrial internal muscular network assembly.
papers.abstract: Atrial cardiomyopathy is characterized by altered atrial structures, yet its underlying genetic basis remains inadequately explored. papers.title: Characterizing malaria parasite drug response using single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Gene expression analysis in malaria parasites has been used to define transcriptional regulatory networks but has been used less frequently to characterize parasite response to drug treatment or to show how parasites may evade killing. Here we highlight the potential of single-cell transcriptional sequencing to augment the process of MOA deconvolution. We develop a new analytical pipeline that involves comparing single-cell transcription patterns to existing profiles from synchronized parasites to comprehensively characterize life cycle stage enrichments that may be observed after chemical perturbations. papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics for studying cell competition in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Cell competition is a conserved fitness-surveillance process, first described in Drosophila epithelia, by which cells compare relative fitness with their neighbors so that less-fit "loser" cells are eliminated, extruded or forced to differentiate while fitter "winner" cells expand. In the tumor microenvironment (TME), this logic appears to be co-opted by transformed clones that eliminate normal epithelium, outcompete neighboring subclones and reshape stromal and immune compartments, making cell competition a potentially underappreciated contributor to cancer clonal evolution, immune escape and therapy resistance. Because competition is defined by a comparison between adjacent cells and by a demonstrated change in the relative representation of one population, it is difficult to resolve with bulk sequencing, which averages across precisely the heterogeneity that defines it. The convergence of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, spatial and single-cell proteomics, artificial intelligence (AI) and network-inference bioinformatics now allows competition-relevant cellular states, interfaces and signaling relationships to be measured at the resolution the problem requires. We emphasize at the outset that these technologies are, in almost all current applications, hypothesis-generating: they identify candidate competitive interfaces and putative winner and loser states from static measurements, and they do not by themselves demonstrate that competition has occurred. This review synthesizes advances across these domains; proposes an explicit three-tier evidence framework separating direct experimental evidence of cell competition from competition-relevant associations and from computational predictions; distinguishes cell competition from related processes such as clonal selection, immune editing and differential proliferation; and defines a putative cell competition network as a falsifiable construct whose edges include ligand-receptor, spatial-adjacency, metabolic and mechanical relations. We further outline a conceptual, context-dependent Cell Competition Score (CCS) as a testable specification rather than a biomarker-ready instrument, and set out the benchmarking, causal-inference and prospective-validation requirements that stand between current capability and any clinical application.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis highlights TM4SF4 + epithelial cells and the MMP14-associated signaling program in lung adenocarcinoma pathogenesis and microenvironment remodeling.

This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), genome-wide association study, and spatial transcriptomics to identify epithelial subpopulations associated with this crosstalk. Analyzing GSE196303 scRNA-seq data, we resolved 15 epithelial subpopulations. Using scPagwas, the TM4SF4 + subpopulation showed the highest trait-relevance score for LUAD genetic susceptibility (adjusted p TM4SF4 + cell enrichment in tumors; high abundance was associated with poorer overall survival in the median-cutoff analysis (hazard ratio = 1.43, 95% confidence interval = 1.07-1.92, p = 0.016) and with TME remodeling features (reduced immune/stromal scores and increased tumor purity). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and multi-evidence intersection identified MMP14 as a candidate hub gene. Spatial transcriptomics supported the heterogeneous distribution of MMP14, and functional enrichment linked MMP14-associated transcriptional programs to ECM remodeling, migration, and Hedgehog/Notch pathways. Expression validation confirmed MMP14 upregulation in LUAD cells and tissues. Collectively, TM4SF4 + epithelial cells and the MMP14-associated program may contribute to LUAD progression and TME remodeling, supporting them as candidate biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for further validation.

papers.abstract: BackgroundMicroplastics (MPs) and their toxic components (BPA, DBP, DEHP) pose global health threats, with the liver as primary target. papers.title: CROST 2.0: an expanded repository of spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: CROST (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/crost) is a public spatial transcriptomics resource that offers curated datasets, standardized analytical results, structured spatial knowledge, and interactive exploration tools. In version 2.0, our collection has expanded to 544 projects and 3538 samples, nearly a three-fold increase from version 1.0 (182 projects and 1033 samples). We have also substantially expanded the derived resources for spatial colocalization and spatially variable cancer genes. To facilitate spatial microenvironment analysis, CROST 2.0 introduces an analytical framework comprising niche-associated differential expression, spatially resolved gene-set activity analysis, spatial interaction hotspot and topic analyses, and molecular and cell-type niche analysis. CROST 2.0 also provides the Spatial Compare function to compare spatial gene expression, cell-type distributions, and niche composition across samples. It introduces the Cancer NicheDE module to systematically characterize cancer niche-associated differential expression and integrates an online cell-type annotation tool, SCType, enabling the use of single-cell reference information in spatial transcriptomic analysis. These updates extend CROST into an integrated spatial transcriptomics resource for characterizing spatial microenvironments, investigating cancer-associated spatial features, and comparing spatial patterns across samples.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing of Human Lamina Cribrosa Fibroblasts in Glaucoma.
papers.abstract: The molecular mechanisms that underlie the extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling of the human lamina cribrosa (LC) in glaucoma remain obscure. This is the first study to characterise human glaucomatous LC cells using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Our aim is to characterise transcriptional changes in human LC cells from glaucomatous and normal eyes and identify signalling pathways contributing to optic nerve head remodelling. scRNA-seq was performed on LC cells from glaucomatous and normal donor eyes. Differential gene expression was analysed using Seurat. Cell identity was assessed using SingleR and GTEx reference datasets. Pathway enrichment analysis was performed using Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), and transcription factor (TF) motif enrichment was evaluated using i-cisTarget. Validation was performed using quantitative PCR, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. LC cells were treated with ISRIB and 4-PBA. Analysis of 6131 LC cells using shared nearest-neighbour clustering and UMAP visualisation identified four broad transcriptional groups, which were used for subsequent transcriptional characterisation. Cell type mapping identified a fibroblast/mesenchymal cell origin. Glaucomatous LC fibroblasts demonstrated a pro-fibrotic transcriptional profile, with overexpression of multiple pro-fibrotic genes, master TF regulons involved in cell fate decisions, and TF motifs including SRF, as well as key integrated stress response (ISR) genes such as ATF4, ATF3 and CREB3L1. Enriched pathways included E2F, G2M, the Hallmark EMT gene set and MYC, while the p53 pathway was downregulated. Pharmacologic treatment with ISRIB or 4-PBA reduced expression of stress-response and ECM genes, while ISRIB attenuated the increased cellular metabolic activity observed in glaucomatous LC cells. Bioinformatic analysis of scRNA-seq of human glaucoma LC cells identified increased expression of myofibroblast genes, an EMT-associated/profibrotic transcriptional programme, and cell cycle signalling pathways, TF regulatory elements and stress response genes.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Translation/RBP-Related Fibroblast Signature for Drug Repurposing in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by persistent fibroblast activation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. However, transcriptional heterogeneity associated with translation- and RNA-binding protein (RBP)-related processes within IPF fibroblasts remains incompletely characterized. Here, we analyzed two independent human IPF single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts to identify fibroblast states that differed in Translation/RBP-related transcriptional programs while sharing high fibrotic output. Donor-paired pseudobulk analysis in GSE136831 identified a transcriptional signature distinguishing these states, and genes showing consistent directional changes in the independent GSE135893 cohort were retained to derive a cross-cohort signature. Reverse-connectivity analysis across CLUE, L1000CDS2, and iLINCS was then used to prioritize compounds predicted to transcriptionally oppose this signature. Candidate compounds were subsequently evaluated in transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-stimulated human fetal lung fibroblasts (HFL-1), with cell viability, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and collagen I used for initial phenotypic assessment. PP-1, PK-11195, dabrafenib, GSK-1059615, and dasatinib reduced both profibrotic markers within the tested concentration ranges, identifying them as candidates for further investigation. Together, these findings define a cross-cohort Translation/RBP-related fibroblast signature in IPF and support its use as a transcriptome-guided strategy for prioritizing compounds with antifibrotic phenotypic activity.

papers.title: Spatial Multi-Omics Integration with Mass Spectrometry Imaging: Decoding Metabolic Landscapes and Disease Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Spatial multi-omics links molecular measurements to tissue architecture, but integrating spatial transcriptomics with mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because the modalities differ in sampling unit, spatial resolution, data structure, and molecular-identification certainty. This review synthesizes the enabling technologies and presents an evidence-calibrated workflow spanning tissue acquisition, spatial registration, modality-specific preprocessing, cross-modal annotation, mechanistic modeling, and orthogonal validation. We examine how MSI can complement single-cell and spatial transcriptomic or proteomic measurements in studies of tumor-host interfaces, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, adipose-tissue organization, and decidualization at the maternal-fetal interface. Across these applications, spatial colocalization is most informative when annotation confidence is reported and key chemical identities are validated, registration error is quantified, and candidate cell-metabolite relationships are tested by isotope tracing or perturbation. We further discuss molecular ambiguity, resolution-sensitivity-throughput trade-offs, 3-dimensional reconstruction, interlaboratory reproducibility, and requirements for clinical translation. The central conclusion is that spatial multi-omics is best used to formulate anatomically explicit, falsifiable hypotheses rather than to infer causality from aligned maps alone.

CD4+ memory T cell abundance is a hypothesis-generating candidate context modifier of KLRB1-mediated prognosis. This finding requires external validation in a subtype-stratified cohort, and the present data do not support clinical use.

papers.title: Photon-Counting CT in Oral and Maxillofacial Imaging: Clinical Applications, Dose Efficiency, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) is an emerging imaging technology that combines ultra-high spatial resolution, improved dose efficiency, reduced electronic noise, and intrinsic spectral imaging. These characteristics are particularly relevant to oral and maxillofacial radiology, where accurate depiction of small osseous and dental structures is often required in the presence of metallic restorations or implants. This review summarizes the technical principles of PCCT and examines its current and potential clinical applications across dental and maxillofacial imaging. Available evidence indicates that PCCT can improve visualization of fine root canal anatomy, periodontal and trabecular bone structures, peri-implant interfaces, subtle maxillofacial fractures, and complex sinonasal anatomy. Its spectral capabilities, including virtual monoenergetic imaging and material decomposition, may substantially reduce metal-related artifacts and improve tissue characterization. Early studies also suggest that PCCT can provide high diagnostic image quality at reduced radiation dose, with potential advantages in pediatric imaging and in patients requiring repeated examinations. Beyond morphology, PCCT may support quantitative applications such as bone mineral density assessment, iodine mapping, treatment planning, and the development of imaging biomarkers and artificial intelligence-based analysis. Despite these promising findings, cone-beam CT remains the preferred modality for many routine dental indications because of its accessibility, lower cost, and established clinical workflow. Current evidence for PCCT in oral and maxillofacial radiology is still limited and is largely derived from technical, experimental, and early clinical studies. Further prospective comparisons with cone-beam CT and conventional CT are needed to define task-specific diagnostic benefits, optimized protocols, radiation-dose advantages, and cost-effectiveness. PCCT is therefore best regarded as a promising complementary modality with particular value in diagnostically challenging cases that require very high spatial resolution, spectral information, or effective metal-artifact reduction. Nevertheless, most oral and maxillofacial evidence remains exploratory; improved image-quality metrics should not be equated with superior patient-level diagnostic accuracy. Direct comparisons with optimized CBCT yield heterogeneous, protocol-dependent dose and diagnostic findings. No standardized indication-specific PCCT acquisition framework currently exists for routine oral and maxillofacial imaging. Clinical implementation should therefore be conditional on demonstrable diagnostic benefit at a justified radiation dose and acceptable resource cost.

papers.title: Nanosecond Pulsed Electric Fields Combined with Triamcinolone Acetonide for Hypertrophic Scar Treatment: In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scar (HS) is a common fibrotic disorder following wound healing for which no universally effective therapy currently exists. This study provides the first systematic investigation of the therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms of combining Nanosecond pulsed electric fields (nsPEF) with the corticosteroid Triamcinolone acetonide (TA). In vitro experiments using fibroblasts isolated from hypertrophic scar tissue demonstrated that nsPEF induced a dose‑dependent increase in cell membrane permeability, providing a mechanistic basis for enhanced transmembrane drug uptake via electroporation. Notably, nsPEF alone reduced fibroblast viability, induced apoptosis, and decreased α-SMA expression. Viability assays revealed that combining a longer pulse width (400 nanoseconds) with a moderate triamcinolone acetonide concentration (0.08 grams per liter) yielded the most pronounced synergistic inhibitory effect. Flow cytometry and α-SMA immunofluorescence staining further showed increased apoptosis and reduced α-SMA expression following combined treatment. In vivo, the rabbit ear scar model confirmed that nsPEF alone significantly improved macroscopic scar morphology, reduced the scar elevation index (SEI), and downregulated fibrotic markers. The combined treatment further reduced the SEI from 3.0 to 1.54, approaching normal skin values, and more profoundly decreasing fibrotic markers and abnormal collagen deposition. Collectively, these findings establish that combining nsPEF with TA constitutes a novel synergistic physical-pharmacologic paradigm and warrants further exploration as a potential therapeutic strategy for hypertrophic scarring.

papers.title: Gelatin hydrogels loaded with FAKI and ZIF-8@PDA nanoparticles for suppression of hypertrophic scar formation.
papers.abstract: Hydrogels is an attractive strategy for wound healing. However, it must balance antimicrobial efficacy with biocompatibility, addressing challenges such as insufficient antibacterial properties, limited effectiveness in complex wound healing, and poor scar formation control seen in conventional hydrogel dressings. Herein, we demonstrate an innovative ZIF-8@PDA nanoparticle-embedded gelatin hydrogel with integrated photothermal antibacterial activity (antibacterial rate close to 100% at 3 min) and good biocompatibility. Encapsulation of focal adhesion kinase inhibitors within the hydrogel has an initial release rate of approximately 28% within 24 h in vitro. The combined hydrogels accelerate the closure of bacterially infected inflammatory wounds and reduce the formation of hypertrophic scars in mice. Mechanistically, the hydrogel effectively blocks the mechanotransduction pathway through FAK/ERK/YAP cascade, mitigating fibroblast overproliferation and reducing fibrotic scar formation. These findings highlight a transformative approach in hydrogel design, showcasing the potential to significantly promote wound healing and reduce hypertrophic scar formation, thus paving the way for innovative advancements in next-generation wound management solutions.

papers.title: Laser-assisted Topical Corticosteroid Delivery versus Intralesional Steroid Injection for Hypertrophic Scars and Keloids: A Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundHypertrophic scars (HTS) and keloids are pathological responses to dermal injury that frequently lead to cosmetic disfigurement and functional limitations. Intralesional corticosteroid injection (ISI) is a commonly used treatment but is often associated with pain and local adverse effects. Laser-assisted topical corticosteroid delivery has emerged as a less invasive alternative. This meta-analysis aims to compare the efficacy and safety of these two treatment modalities.MethodsA systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus up to March 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing laser-assisted corticosteroid delivery with ISI for the treatment of HTS or keloids. Secondary outcomes included pain scores assessed by the visual analog scale (VAS), patient satisfaction, and the incidence of adverse events. Analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.3.ResultsEight studies involving 517 patients were included. The VSS scores in the laser-assisted corticosteroid delivery group were significantly lower than those in the ISI group (MD = - 0.19, 95% CI: - 0.33 to - 0.05, P = 0.009), suggesting that laser-assisted corticosteroid delivery is more effective. Laser-assisted drug delivery showed a trend toward lower pain scores (MD = - 2.42, 95% CI: - 4.94 to - 0.10, P = 0.06) and showed a non-significant trend toward higher patient satisfaction (OR = 2.32, 95% CI: 0.72 to 7.40, P = 0.16). No significant differences were observed in pain scores, patient satisfaction, or scar recurrence. papers.title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

papers.title: Wound atlas of Atlantic salmon skin.
papers.abstract: The process of wound healing offers a window into how cells coordinate to maintain tissue integrity, repair damage, and restore tissue function. Wound healing in Atlantic salmon, a species of considerable ecological and economic importance, is a tightly coordinated process involving multiple cellular programmes that eventually lead to scarless repair. Here, we present the first single-nucleus atlas of healing salmon skin wounds, providing a comprehensive view of its cellular organisation over multiple timepoints. We have profiled 29,706 nuclei from uninjured skin, 2 days post-wounding (dpw; inflammatory phase), and 14 dpw (proliferative phase), identifying 44 transcriptionally distinct cell clusters. Integration with previously published spatial transcriptomics dataset further enabled the localisation of these populations within the wound microenvironment. We have identified distinct spatial-temporal association for erythrocytes, thrombocytes, macrophages, differentiating muscle cells, fibroblasts, and tenocytes, highlighting their potential contributions to tissue repair. Furthermore, transcriptomic and histological analyses support a previously under-appreciated role for the myosepta in coordinating wound and muscle repair. By linking cellular transcriptional state to the tissue architecture, this spatially resolved wound atlas provides a framework for understanding the repair of cutaneous wounds in Atlantic salmon and establishes a valuable resource for studies of fish health. By exploring wound healing for insights on tissue function, this atlas also offers broader insights into the scarless wound healing biology in non-model organism vertebrates. Data visualisation of the single-nuclei RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics analysis is available on our web portal at https://bshihlab-salmonwoundatlas.share.connect.posit.cloud/.

papers.title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies.
papers.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. However, the concurrent challenges of implant-associated bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration remain formidable obstacles in clinical practice. Rather than being independent processes, bacterial infection and bone regeneration are intimately coupled through a complex signaling network-a concept increasingly recognized as the "infection-osteogenesis crosstalk." We begin with how TNT morphology-nanotube diameter above all-differentially steers osteoblast behavior and bacterial adhesion, and how the initial protein corona and immune microenvironment set the infection-to-bone-healing trajectory. From signaling, we move to the pathways behind infection-driven osteogenic suppression: the core signaling pathways through which bacterial virulence factors suppress osteogenesis, including TLR-mediated NF-κB activation, RANKL/OPG imbalance-driven osteoclastogenesis, and biofilm hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming. We then look at how macrophages (M1/M2 polarization, NLRP3 inflammasome), neutrophils (NETosis), and T cells shape the host response to infection and bone repair. We close with current synergistic design strategies-metal ion doping, antimicrobial peptide loading, organic-inorganic composite coatings, temporally controlled drug release-and next-generation smart responsive surfaces including pH-responsive, photothermal/photocatalytic, enzyme-responsive, and immunomodulatory coatings. This review aims to provide a mechanistic framework for understanding infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TNT surfaces and to guide the rational design of dual-functional implants that simultaneously combat infection and promote bone regeneration.

papers.title: Brainstem enkephalinergic neural circuit underlying cold-induced pain relief in mice.
papers.abstract: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified a cold-responsive neuronal subset within the lateral parabrachial nucleus (lPBN), the thermosensory relay region in the hindbrain, that mediates cold-induced analgesia in mice. Activation of these neurons and their projection to ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) increased the nociceptive threshold, while ablation of these neurons attenuated analgesia induced by cold-mimicking chemicals. We further identified that these neurons express precursor gene of enkephalin (Penk), which is necessary for TRPM8 (transient receptor potential melastatin 8)-mediated pain relief. Mechanistically, cold-responsive lPBN neurons frequency-dependently released enkephalin peptide into vlPAG to activate the descending pain modulation circuitry via disinhibition. Activation of cold-responsive neurons reduced spinal cord responses to noxious stimuli, suggesting the involvement of a top-down pain modulation pathway. papers.title: SpaceBlocks: an expert-supervised workflow for cohort-level spatial transcriptomics analysis
papers.abstract: Summary Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has become a central tool in tissue biology, with multiple technologies addressing the issue from a different angle. papers.title: spaDWGCN: a spatial distance weighted graph convolution network for accurate spatial tissue structure identification.
papers.abstract: The continuous development of spatial transcriptomics enables us to obtain gene expression matrices alongside spatial coordinate labels for cells or spots, providing tools for understanding spatial tissue microenvironments and spatially resolved cell-cell interactions. papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts: origins, functional heterogeneity and therapeutic potential.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are integral components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of nearly every hallmark of cancer. papers.title: Metallostasis remodeling in rheumatoid arthritis: focus on iron, copper, and zinc in the synovial microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease characterized by chronic synovitis, pannus formation, and progressive bone erosion. Although cytokine-targeted therapies have substantially improved clinical outcomes, a subset of patients still experience inadequate responses, ongoing structural damage, and a sustained disease burden. Metallostasis contributes to immunometabolic and redox regulation and influences cellular functional states; its disruption is better understood as a mismatch between systemic redistribution and local synovial enrichment or depletion, rather than as a simple increase or decrease in total elemental abundance. In RA, iron dyshomeostasis is reflected by the coexistence of systemic iron restriction and local joint iron enrichment; copper dyshomeostasis involves acute-phase redistribution and lysyl oxidase (LOX)-mediated matrix remodeling; and zinc dyshomeostasis is associated with a low-zinc phenotype, altered zinc transport, and modulation of immune signaling thresholds. Through effects on redox regulation, immune signaling, and extracellular matrix remodeling, disturbances in metal homeostasis may contribute to persistent inflammation, synovial invasion, and bone destruction. In this narrative review, we discuss the evidence base, mechanisms of action, and translational potential of iron, copper, and zinc in RA. Moving beyond whether metal levels are increased or decreased toward their distribution within the synovial microenvironment, associated changes in cellular function, and experimentally defined causal links may open new directions for stratification biomarker development and precision intervention in RA.

papers.title: Sialylation-Siglec glyco-immune checkpoints in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms of immune evasion, therapeutic resistance, and postoperative recurrence.
papers.abstract: Postoperative recurrence and incomplete responses to immunotherapy remain major obstacles to the long-term control of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Tumor-associated sialylation may promote immune escape by generating glycans that bind inhibitory members of the sialic acid-binding immunoglobulin-like lectin (Siglec) family on immune cells. This review critically examines HCC-specific evidence on abnormal sialylation, Siglec-related dysfunction of natural killer cells and macrophages, treatment-associated glycan remodeling, and possible links to molecular residual disease and postoperative recurrence. Glycan patterns vary substantially between tumors and within individual tumors. Total sialic acid abundance and the expression of a single sialyltransferase therefore provide only part of the information needed to identify functional Siglec ligands. Their activity also depends on glycan structure, chemical modifications, the molecule carrying the glycan, ligand density, surface accessibility, and spatial organization. The strongest HCC-specific evidence concerns the interaction between Siglec-9 and natural killer cells. Supporting findings include receptor and ligand expression, close spatial proximity within tumors, associations with adverse clinical outcomes, and recovery of natural killer-cell activity after pathway inhibition in preclinical models. Siglec-10-high tumor-associated macrophages are associated with an immunosuppressive myeloid state. Their endogenous ligands and receptor-specific roles in vivo require further characterization. In sorafenib-resistant HCC models, increased ST3 β-galactoside α-2,3-sialyltransferase 1 (ST3GAL1) expression accompanies greater Siglec-7 and Siglec-9 probe binding, while ST3GAL1 silencing improves natural killer-cell-mediated cytotoxicity. These findings support a functional contribution of altered glycosylation to treatment-related immune escape. Glycocalyx-dependent changes in adhesion, migration, and survival may also contribute to dissemination and residual-cell persistence alongside immune evasion. Direct studies are now needed to determine whether sialylation-Siglec signaling helps residual HCC cells survive after curative-intent therapy. Clinical translation will require identification of specific glycan-carrier pairs, spatial mapping of receptor-ligand contacts, receptor-specific validation in species-appropriate models, and prospective evaluation of glyco-immune biomarkers alongside circulating tumor DNA and established clinicopathological factors across HCC etiologies. Overall, current evidence identifies the sialylation-Siglec system as a biologically plausible and cell-specific immune-evasion network. It also provides a framework for biomarker-guided evaluation of Siglec-directed therapies and tumor-targeted desialylation and future studies of its contribution to HCC recurrence.

papers.title: Functional cooperation, adaptation and synchronization of subcellular processes in cellular neighborhoods as inferred from spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Tissue-level functions emerge from pathway activities distributed across neighboring cells. Yet analyses of spatial transcriptomics mostly focus on cell type composition or signaling through ligand-receptor pairs, leaving spatial relationships between effector processes undescribed. Using those networks for the analysis of published spatial transcriptomics datasets from human kidney biopsies, we identified functionally related SCP activities between a tissue spot and its neighbors. Two independent null models, shuffling of SCP labels within the network and shuffling of spots on the tissue slice, distinguish pairs that are functionally non-random and pairs that are additionally enriched within the immediate neighborhood, separating local from tissue-wide coordination. Our results suggest that tissue physiology reflects not only cell type composition but also functional coordination between neighboring regions.

papers.title: GASTON-VI efficiently quantifies spatial axes and molecular gradients from multi-sample, multi-modal spatial-omics data
papers.abstract: Many tissues exhibit an underlying spatial axis along which fundamental biological processes occur due to continuous spatial gradients of cell type and molecular state. Modern spatial-omics technologies measure molecular features (e.g. gene/protein expression) at 100,000s-1,000,000s of locations within a two-dimensional (2-D) tissue slice, with large-scale atlases profiling multiple tissue slices of the same organ type across different individuals and biological conditions (e.g. healthy versus diseased). However, existing computational methods for identifying spatial molecular gradients are limited to small spatial transcriptomics datasets (1000s of cells) of a single tissue slice, while methods for integrating multiple samples do not explicitly model spatial axes nor spatial molecular gradients along such axes. Here, we present GASTON-VI, a variational inference (VI)-based deep learning model which efficiently learns an underlying spatial axis and spatial molecular gradients along this axis from multi-sample, multi-condition spatial-omics data of any molecular modality (e.g. transcriptomics, proteomics). GASTON-VI jointly learns (1) a spatial coordinate (the "isodepth") for each individual tissue slice and (2) 1-D spatial modality functions that describe molecular gradients along the isodepth for tissues of the same biological condition, while utilizing a latent variable model to account for batch effects. Further, GASTON-VI implements a statistical test for identifying molecules with differential spatial gradients across biological conditions (e.g. healthy versus diseased). On spatial transcriptomics and proteomics data from the intestine, tonsil, and liver, we show that GASTON-VI recovers spatial axes and molecular gradients along these axes more accurately and efficiently than existing methods. In particular, applied to large-scale spatial transcriptomics and proteomics atlases, GASTON-VI reveals differential spatial gradients of gene expression along the portal vein-central vein axis in fibrotic livers, and differential spatial gradients of protein abundance along the muscularis-lumen axis across different regions of the intestine. papers.title: Subsequent Phases of Gene Expression Leading to Commitment and Differentiation in a Eukaryotic Cell
papers.abstract: Cell differentiation requires the specific control of gene expression for each cell type. However, the mechanism by which robust developmental outcomes arise from inherently noisy single-cell dynamics remains unclear. To address this question, we performed a formal analysis of longitudinal time series during the commitment and differentiation of giant single cells. We tracked how the discrete expression states of individual genes changed relative to each other. Despite marked variability in timing and trajectories from cell to cell, we identified reproducible temporal motifs and quantified the strength of temporal correlations among early- and late-regulated genes. Notably, a core gene set exhibited the same relative temporal order in establishing stable or transiently stable expression states in most cells. This suggests that a well-defined gene expression program emerges amidst apparent stochasticity. These results support a model in which induction to differentiation proceeds via a cascade of partially concurrent, discrete genetic switching events that collectively produce gradual, continuous shifts in expression at the population level. This framework reconciles apparently stochastic single-cell behavior with reliable developmental outcomes and suggests general principles for the temporal organization of gene regulation during differentiation. Furthermore, it provides analytic tools that can be broadly applied to longitudinal single-cell datasets to design temporally precise interventions in development and disease.

papers.title: Spectral analysis of gene-dependency networks reveals emergent organization across scales in CAR T biology
papers.abstract: CAR T-cell infusion products are commonly characterized in terms of their cellular populations and transcriptional programs, but these descriptions do not fully capture how a product is organized as a system. We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from the infusion products of 163 patients across eight cohorts to investigate how system-level transcriptional organization relates to both clinical outcome and how cellular features vary together across patients. For each patient, we constructed a gene-dependency graph using mutual information between the binary detection states of each gene pair across infusion cells. To characterize each patient's network architecture, we define spectral organization, O{lambda}, a measure of the relative persistence of collective patterns of gene dependence in the network. Using hierarchical Bayesian survival models, we assessed the associations of both O{lambda} and various established cellular features with treatment outcome. Higher spectral organization was associated with a higher hazard of treatment failure in both a continuous model (hazard ratio per standard deviation, 1.45, 95% credible interval 1.07-2.19) and a smooth transition model (hazard ratio comparing the high and low regimes, 2.03, 95% credible interval 1.10-3.53). When we investigated how cellular features covary across patients, we found that correlations among both T-cell programs and cell type proportions aligned more coherently with treatment failure risk in the high O{lambda} regime compared to the low regime, revealing a systems-level pattern that helps explain the clinical relevance of spectral organization. Gene set enrichment analysis further showed that more persistent architectures were associated with inflammation and cellular interaction pathways, whereas lower spectral organization was associated with biosynthetic and genome maintenance pathways, consistent with the hypothesis that the organizational state of an infusion product reflects its capacity to reconfigure in response to CAR T treatment. Altogether, our findings identify spectral organization as a property of the infusion product as a whole that connects gene-dependency architecture within individual products to the collective variation of cellular features across patients. This framework therefore motivates studying CAR T biology from a systems perspective alongside established descriptions of cellular state.

papers.title: Altered ultrasonic vocalizations in mouse models of FOXG1 syndrome
papers.abstract: FOXG1 syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with communication impairment as a defining clinical feature, yet vocal behavior has not been characterized in animal models of FOXG1. papers.title: Single cell mapping reveals phenotypic, immunometabolic and functional heterogeneity among age-associated B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and aging
papers.abstract: Abstract/Summary Introduction: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) comprise an antigen-experienced memory B-cell population that expands during aging but has also been implicated in autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This study aims to comprehensively profile the functional alterations that accommodate ABC expansion, emphasizing metabolic reprogramming within the B-cell compartment in SLE, particularly with regard to ABCs, in order to identify niche metabolic pathways utilized by ABCs that may represent useful therapeutic targets. Methods: An exploratory analysis was conducted using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to phenotypically and functionally characterize ABC populations in patients with SLE and lupus-prone MRL.lpr mice, using a broad array of community tools. We further conducted SCENITH-based metabolic profiling to assess metabolic differences among splenic follicular (FO), marginal zone (MZ) and CD21-CD23- double negative (DN) B cells, in the murine SLE-like MRL.lpr model, in which we tested the ability of B cell subsets to generate protein output, following exposure to specific metabolic inhibitors (2-deoxyglucose and oligomycin). In addition, we cross-examined CD21-CD23- DN B cells in the native context of aging by employing flow cytometry-based analyses of their redox status (NADH/FAD autofluorescence) and mitochondrial function (MitoTracker and TMRE staining) to investigate age-associated metabolic programming. Results: Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed substantial immunophenotypic and metabolic heterogeneity within the ABC compartment in SLE. Subclustering of ABCs revealed three separate and distinct ABC subsets, encompassing CD68 ABCs, NKG7 ABCs, and AREG ABCs, differing in their respecrive transcriptional, functional, and immunometabolic signatures. The CD68 ABC subset demonstrated signs of enhanced cytotoxicity, phagocytosis, lysosomal activity, and increased antigen-processing capabilities. The CD68 and NKG7 ABC populations exhibited increased inflammatory pathway activity, including pattern-recognition receptor signalling and NLRP3 inflammasome-associated activity, while the AREG ABC subset displayed signs of senescence, moderation, exhaustion, or anergy. hdWGCNA identified transcriptional modules associated with acetyltransferase activity, suggesting a potential link between metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodelling through epimetabolite availability, in particular acetyl-CoA. ABCs demonstrated, in general, coordinated amplification of glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid utilization, with substantial intragroup metabolic heterogeneity among the three ABC subsets. The CD68 ABCs emerged as the most hypermetabolic subset. In parallel, SCENITH-based metabolic comparison of CD21-CD23- DN B cells between mildly diseased male and severely diseased female MRL.lpr mice revealed increased utilization of alternative non-glucose substrates and enhanced glycolytic activity, but reduced overall protein synthesis capacity, indicating altered allocation of metabolic resources. Further interpretation of the transcriptomic analysis suggests that proteasomal activity could explain the lower protein levels in female MRL.lpr mice, as measured by SCENITH. In addition, in silico drug prediction pointed towards statins and proteasome inhibitors as potentially useful pharmacological agents for blocking cholesterol metabolism and protein degradation, respectively. Finally, the analysis of aged mice also revealed metabolic and redox alterations in ABC-enriched CD21-CD23- DN B cells under physiological aging conditions. Conclusions: Human ABCs appear to comprise a heterogeneous constellation of various subsets possessing different functional properties, as well as different pro-inflammatory or immunoregulatory statuses. ABCs exhibit a distinct hypermetabolic state associated with lupus-related immune dysregulation, but also with aging, in line with previous reports. However, as the disease manifests and progresses, protein production appears to be dampened, which could be attributed to ribosomal problems or proteasome-mediated protein degradation. Metabolic reprogramming is accompanied by enhanced phagocytic and lysosomal programs, which may facilitate the uptake of self-material and contribute to autoreactive immune responses, in particular anti-nuclear autoantibody production. Increased OXPHOS activity may accommodate epigenetic reprogramming towards the atypical memory phenotype displayed by ABCs. Identification of ABC-specific metabolic dependencies may provide opportunities for therapeutic intervention, with lipid consumption being of particular interest. These findings support further investigation of metabolic modulators, including HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and proteasome-targeting strategies, to limit their pathogenic activity in SLE by exploiting their niche metabolic vulnerabilities, in particular their hypermetabolic state and proteostatic stress.

papers.title: Substrate rigidity suppresses the NRF2 antioxidant program in breast cancer cells
papers.abstract: Matrix stiffness rises as breast tumors progress, but whether rigidity raises or lowers activity of the KEAP1-NRF2 antioxidant pathway is contested: work in breast cancer cells places the antioxidant response on soft matrix, while work in liver cancer places response on stiff. YAP and TEAD targets did not track rigidity, rising on hydrogels and glass but falling on cell-derived matrix. An unsupervised partition made without reference to any pathway recovered the same program and survived removal of proliferation genes. papers.abstract: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) biases spike timing with weak electric fields, but how recurrent circuitry and network state shape this response is unclear. We simulated tACS in a detailed cortical column model in two network states of varying coherence, roughly corresponding to REM-like and NREM-like states. Despite weak impacts on network firing rates, stimulation entrained network activity at realistically occurring field strengths. Global entrainment was initiated by direct entrainment of ongoing pyramidal cell activity, which subsequently recruited inhibitory interneurons in a state-dependent manner. The NREM-like network locked more strongly to all tested stimulation frequencies, independent of baseline spectral power, and displayed larger recurrent-connectivity-mediated phase lags. However, recurrent connectivity was not required for, and did not amplify, entrainment, but instead produced an offset in baseline network activity. Our results highlight the impact of network state on the response to tACS, and suggest that meso-scale models of electromagnetic-electrophysiological interactions must look beyond single-cell polarization and baseline oscillations at the stimulation frequency.

papers.title: IκBα loss impairs mitochondrial homeostasis and primes cells for senescence
papers.abstract: Inflammatory signaling and mitochondrial dysfunction are hallmarks of cellular senescence, yet how these processes are coordinated remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify I{kappa}B, a well-known inhibitor of NF-{kappa}B, as a regulatory factor that links mitochondrial homeostasis to stress-induced cell death and senescence. Knockdown (KD) of I{kappa}B did not by itself induce a fully established senescent state but instead generated a senescence-primed state characterized by cellular hypertrophy, reduced DNA synthesis, metabolic remodeling, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Time-course proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses revealed a selective reduction of mitochondrial inner membrane-associated proteins in I{kappa}B KD cells and attenuated early signaling responses to TNF stimulation, respectively. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further indicated that a smaller fraction of I{kappa}B KD cells was predicted to transition toward a pro-apoptotic state. Among canonical I{kappa}B family members, induction of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) was specific to I{kappa}B KD, even though mitochondrial dysfunction was more pronounced in I{kappa}B{beta} and I{kappa}B{varepsilon} KD. These findings suggest that I{kappa}B influences the balance between post-stress cellular senescence and cell death through mechanisms that include maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis.

papers.title: Unsupervised tensor integration of hippocampal and colonic multi-omics reveals enteric neural signatures in cognitive aging
papers.abstract: Background: Molecular changes in peripheral tissues may provide insights into cognitive aging, but identifying relevant genes without using behavioral outcomes for feature selection remains challenging. Results: We applied tensor decomposition-based unsupervised feature extraction to publicly available hippocampal and colonic transcriptomic and promoter DNA methylation profiles from mice across five age groups. A tensor comprising tissue, molecular modality, age group, biological replicate, and gene dimensions was constructed using 16,080 shared genes. Higher-order singular value decomposition identified a component with a monotonic age pattern, shared tissue contributions, and opposing transcriptomic and methylation contributions. This component yielded 1,577 selected genes without using cognitive scores for feature selection. The corresponding colonic methylation score correlated with overall cognition (r=0.589; Benjamini--Hochberg-adjusted P=9.87 x10-7), although no significant associations remained after age adjustment. The selected genes were enriched for enteric neuronal and glial markers derived from a published single-cell atlas, with 5.10-fold and 4.65-fold enrichment, respectively. Comparison with the broadest available Boruta-selected gene set identified only 64 overlapping genes, leaving 1,513 genes selected exclusively by the tensor approach in this comparison. These remaining genes retained significant enrichment for synaptic processes and enteric neuronal and glial signatures using library-specific backgrounds. Conclusions: Unsupervised tensor integration recovered an aging-associated relationship between colonic methylation and cognition while identifying a largely distinct set of functionally coherent candidate genes. These findings complement supervised feature selection and provide candidates for investigating enteric neural involvement in cognitive aging, without establishing an age-independent association or a causal gut-to-brain mechanism.

papers.title: β-tubulin tyrosination tunes glutamylation and parasite motility in Trypanosoma brucei
papers.abstract: Post-translational modifications of tubulin diversify microtubule function by generating distinct molecular states collectively known as the tubulin code. Whereas the reversible tyrosination cycle is a conserved feature of -tubulin throughout eukaryotes, in trypanosomatid parasites, {beta}-tubulin also carries a genetically encoded C-terminal tyrosine, which is subjected to detyrosination and whose biological role remains unknown. Here, we show that {beta}-tubulin tyrosination is rare across eukaryotes but highly conserved across trypanosomatids. Using genome editing to uncouple the tyrosination states of - and {beta}-tubulin in Trypanosoma brucei, we demonstrate that the {beta}-tubulin C-terminal tyrosine independently contributes to the regulation of microtubule glutamylation. Rather than depending on - or {beta}-tubulin alone, glutamylation levels reflect the combined tyrosination states of both subunits. Strikingly, either increasing or reducing {beta}-tubulin tyrosination produces opposing changes in parasite morphometry, single-cell motility and collective migration. Together, these findings establish {beta}-tubulin (de)tyrosination as an evolutionarily conserved component of the trypanosomatid tubulin code that contributes to microtubule regulation and function in T. brucei, extending the significance of tubulin tyrosination beyond the canonical -tubulin tyrosination cycle.

papers.title: Cortical neurons accumulate point mutations at similar rates in mice and humans
papers.abstract: Across vertebrate species, it has long been known that germline mutation rates per year are inversely proportional to reproductive ages. A similar pattern was recently reported in mammals for mutations in colonic epithelium, leading to speculation that this inter-species scaling may apply to many cell types. We tested whether a similar relationship holds in postmitotic cells, by estimating point mutation rates in mouse cortical neurons from PacBio HiFi circular consensus sequencing data. Our analysis revealed a significant effect of age on the number of point mutations, of 25.9 mutations per diploid genome per year (95% CI: [17.7, 34.1]). This rate is comparable to the one reported for human neurons, indicating that somatic rates need not scale with lifespan. Our findings further demonstrate that a readily available sequencing method can be used to reliably identify somatic mutations at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: Generation of human hindlimb/genital tubercle progenitors from pluripotent stem cells
papers.abstract: The hindlimbs and genital tubercle arise from a bipotent posterior lateral plate mesoderm (pLPM) progenitor population and share common genetic programmes, reflecting their deep evolutionary homology. Perturbations of this shared developmental programme underlie several congenital conditions, yet most insights into the divergence of pLPM fates come from traditional model organisms, emphasising the need for a human-based system. Here, we report the WNT-FGF-BMP-dependent differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into pLPM-derived hindlimb/genital tubercle progenitors (HGTps). BMP signalling drives transcriptomic changes reminiscent of the trunk-to-tail transition, a major reorganisation of the embryonic body plan that initiates pLPM/HGTp specification. We further show that retinoic acid acts biphasically: early exposure blocks these changes, whereas late exposure refines HGTp fate by suppressing alternative pLPM derivatives. Single-cell profiling reveals a spectrum of uncommitted progenitors and cells acquiring genital tubercle or hindlimb character, which map to posterior appendage populations of Carnegie stage 12-18 human embryos. Differentiating mesenchyme self-organises alongside a surrounding epithelium, mirroring appendage development in vivo. Grafted HGTp-derived spheroids incorporate into the genital tubercle-forming region of chick embryos, revealing their positional competence. Collectively, our work establishes a platform for the reverse engineering and disease modelling of human HGTps.

papers.title: Deciphering state bridges via a single-cell large language model
papers.abstract: Large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data provide a new avenue for precision medicine by uncovering cellular heterogeneity. However, systematic comparison of remodeling patterns across various biological states remains unavailable. Here, we first developed a computational framework based on a foundation model of single cell biology, Universal Cell Embedding (UCE), to harmonize annotations comprising 36 cell types. Based on an integrated dataset of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with 8,789 human samples comprising more than 59 million cells or nuclei across 614 biological states, we then embedded each state with a 36-dimensional vector in a unified space of cell-composition change and further deciphered states bridges by analyzing the relationships among the 614 state vectors. As a result, 22,161 significant bridges (P < 0.05) between the 614 states were revealed. Moreover, we successfully identified a number of well-known bridges such as bridge between Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease (P = 2.21e-15), suggesting the effectiveness of the proposed framework. More importantly, we uncovered a number of new bridges. Furthermore, analyses of the number of changed cell types (NCC) and Shannon entropy revealed heterogeneous and tissue-dependent patterns of cellular composition remodeling. This study provides a new strategy for identifying disease associations and potential therapeutic relationships by deciphering bridges between biological states from scRNA-seq landscape.

papers.title: Caveolin-1-dependent signaling and survival in distinct Ewing sarcoma cell states.
papers.abstract: Plasticity is a hallmark function of cancer cells, yet the mechanisms that enable dynamic switching between survival states remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify Caveolin-1, a membrane-domain scaffolding protein, as a regulator of survival signaling in a Ewing sarcoma (EwS) cell line. These CD99High cells exhibit unique morphology, transcriptional programs, and markedly enhanced survival both under chemotherapeutic challenge and in vivo. Importantly, CD99High and CD99Low states are reversible, providing EwS cells with a flexible route to survival-oriented plasticity. Mechanistically, we show that Caveolin-1 in CD99High cells orchestrates PI3K/AKT survival signaling by modulating recruitment of PI3K activity to the plasma membrane. We propose that the CD99High state establishes a Caveolin-1-driven signaling architecture that supports survival through mechanisms distinct from those used by CD99Low cells. These findings uncover a dynamic state transition in EwS cells and position Caveolin-1 as a regulator of cell-state-dependent survival signaling.

papers.title: Being Born versus Being Born Early: Disentangling Birth from Prematurity in Perinatal Brain Development
papers.abstract: Studies of preterm birth report both delayed and accelerated brain maturation, depending on whether preterm infants are compared with term newborns or with fetuses. We propose that these mixed observations arise because such comparisons conflate two distinct influences, the effect of birth on term-aged infants and the independent effects of being born prematurely. Using MRI data from 330 term and 118 preterm neonates in the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP), we developed a simple piecewise linear model that estimates prenatal and postnatal rates of development separately for term and preterm infants across volumetric, microstructural and connectivity measures. In term infants, birth accelerated volumetric growth, with total brain volume growing 44\% faster post-birth, with regionally specific alterations in microstructural trajectories. Deep white matter continued to mature, whereas superficial and cerebellar white matter reversed direction. Changes in cortical connectivity at birth followed the sensorimotor to association axis, shifting towards specialisation in sensory and insular cortex and towards more diverse connectivity in association cortex. In contrast, the effect of birth on preterm infants was much weaker, where development largely continued at prenatal rates. These results show that the impact of birth depends on brain region and maturational state at birth. Separating birth from prematurity offers a framework for interpreting mixed findings in the perinatal literature.

papers.title: Joint Estimation of Mother and Daughter Protein Regulatory Networks Quantifies Inheritance in Yeast Lineages
papers.abstract: Live-cell imaging tracks multiple protein levels within individual cells across divisions in real time, enabling direct measurement of how regulatory dynamics are inherited by a daughter cell from her mother. This technology presents a unique opportunity to directly observe longitudinal dynamics, in contrast to single-cell RNA sequencing, which can only measure cells cross-sectionally. However, there is a lack of computational methods for analyzing live-cell imaging data. Existing frameworks based on ordinary differential equations (ODEs) estimate networks from individual time series, but adapting them to mother-daughter pairs poses a dilemma: pooling both cells forces complete inheritance, while fitting each cell separately starves the short daughter trajectory of timepoints needed for reliable estimation. To address this gap, we develop PRNODE (Protein Regulatory Networks via ODEs), which models each cell's network as a deviation from a shared regulatory scaffold and estimates the scaffold and both deviations jointly under a fused group-lasso penalty. The mother's longer time series thereby supports the daughter's estimate, while allowing the two networks to differ wherever the data demand it. We then propose a novel measure of inheritance based on comparing the rate of change of protein levels between the mother's and daughter's networks. Across simulation studies, we find that PRNODE outperforms existing ODE estimation methods in recovering the networks of daughter cells and in estimating inheritance. Finally, we apply PRNODE to many mother-daughter pairs of Saccharomyces cerevisiae observed over a 9-hour period at 12-minute intervals. Many estimated networks show a negative feedback loop between the cell-cycle inhibitor Whi5 and the cyclin Clb2, which together sustain cell-cycle oscillations. We also find that the measured inheritance tracks the number of regulatory edges a daughter shares with her mother with the same sign, more than the presence of any single edge. PRNODE is available as an R package at https://github.com/shirmath/LIC_methods.

papers.title: Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype that lacks actionable cell-surface receptors, restricting frontline systemic management to cytotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we present an interventional network inference framework that integrates large-scale single-cell CRISPR-interference perturbation sequencing (Perturb-seq; GSE224986, 95,678 cells across 11,975 sgRNAs) with ENCODE Factorbook ChIP-seq physical transcription factor binding priors across 819 somatic mutation-associated enhancer loci in human TNBC (MDA-MB-231). Our pipeline reconstructed a tripartite network yielding 5,935 physical TF-enhancer edges, 383,757 functional enhancer-gene edges, and 542,760 unique TF-target gene functional pairs across 372 active enhancers. Explainable machine learning (SHAP TreeExplainer) revealed non-linear, thresholded transactivation dynamics for AP-1 and MYC. Quantitative benchmarking against held-out CRISPRi ground truth demonstrated strong discriminatory accuracy (AUROC = 0.8999, AUPRC = 0.8745, Precision = 90.13%, FDR = 9.87%), substantially outperforming GENIE3 (AUPRC = 0.6323, FDR = 35.73%) and co-expression correlation (AUPRC = 0.6814). Finally, in silico perturbation modeling indicated that multi-target epigenetic combinations achieved 93% topological disruption of oncogenic regulatory connectivity, nominating prioritized candidate circuits for experimental validation.

papers.abstract: Background: Virtual knock-out methods rank genes by the change predicted after deleting one gene in silico and nominate targets without perturbation data. papers.title: Nuclear confinement from matrix stiffness drives epigenomic reprogramming of gingival fibroblasts
papers.abstract: Stromal fibroblasts reside in a three-dimensional (3D) extracellular matrix (ECM) that physically confines the cell and its nucleus. Nuclear mechanobiology studies have relied largely on two-dimensional substrates, on which cells spread freely without confinement. Therefore, it remains largely unknown how confinement in 3D stiff tissues regulates the fibroblast epigenome. Healthy human gingiva is characterized by a dense, stiff collagen ECM that undergoes softening in periodontal disease. A reduction in collagen in human gingiva correlated with elevated stromal H3K27 acetylation. In 3D hydrogels with stiffness matched to healthy and diseased gingiva, stiffness-dependent matrix confinement compacted the fibroblast nucleus, folded the nuclear envelope, and maintained low H3K27 acetylation through DNA methyltransferase activity, independently of actomyosin contractility. Stiff-matrix confinement increased DNA methylation at pericentromeric satellite repeats and decreased it at CTCF motifs. A stochastic chromatin model showed that broadening the range of chromatin contacts is sufficient to increase methylation in highly methylated regions and decrease it in less methylated regions, with changes concentrated at methylation-domain boundaries in both the model and the data. Stiff-matrix confinement also reduced CTCF occupancy uniformly across the genome, independent of CTCF expression and local DNA methylation. These changes led to hypomethylation of collagen gene promoter sequences, whereas hypermethylation of the MAP3K14 promoter attenuated non-canonical NF-{kappa}B inflammatory signaling. These findings establish stiffness-dependent 3D confinement as a physical regulator of the stromal epigenome and inflammatory states and motivate new mechanotherapies that restore tissue stiffness to resolve stromal cell states in chronic inflammatory diseases.
