papers.title: HTRA1-AS1, an ARMS2-region long non-coding RNA, is downregulated in retinas of age-related macular degeneration patients
papers.abstract: PurposeThe human 10q26 locus is a major genetic risk factor for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Fine mapping by linkage and large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) has narrowed this region to a 30-kb interval encompassing the ARMS2 and HTRA1 genes. However, the causative gene(s), risk variants, and underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain unresolved. MethodsLong non-coding RNA (lncRNA) candidates within the ARMS2-HTRA1 region were identified using human postmortem retinal RNA-seq data and public databases (NCBI, Ensembl). Candidate transcripts were validated by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing. Published single-cell RNA-seq datasets were analysed to define cell type-specific expression, and RNA levels were compared between AMD and non-AMD donor retinas. Additionally, expression changes were assessed in human iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells exposed to cigarette smoke extract (CSE) and paraquat (PQT). ResultsWe identified and characterized the long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) HTRA1-AS1 and its transcript variants within the ARMS2 locus. HTRA1-AS1 overlaps ARMS2 and is transcribed in the antisense orientation. It is predominantly expressed in rod photoreceptors, Muller glia, and choroid/RPE tissues. Retinal HTRA1-AS1 expression was significantly reduced in AMD donors compared with controls (43 AMD vs. 44 controls, P = 0.007), whereas HTRA1 mRNA expression showed no significant difference (P = 0.121). In induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived RPE cells, cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced oxidative stress markedly increased HTRA1-AS1 and ARMS2 expression by up to 8-fold and 75-fold, respectively, whereas paraquat treatment produced no significant changes. ConclusionThese findings identify HTRA1-AS1 as an AMD-associated lncRNA within the ARMS2 locus that exhibits cell-type-specific expression, disease-associated downregulation, and responsiveness to cigarette smoke-induced oxidative stress. These results suggest that HTRA1-AS1 may contribute to AMD pathogenesis through noncoding regulatory mechanisms, warranting further functional investigation.

papers.title: Dual-platform plasma proteogenomics prioritizes GSTA1 and ARG1 as druggable cross-domain targets in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome
papers.abstract: BackgroundCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects shared pathophysiology across metabolic, renal and cardiovascular systems, yet circulating proteins with causal effects spanning multiple CKM domains remain unclear. We aimed to identify and prioritize cross-domain candidate proteins using an integrative, dual-platform plasma proteogenomic framework. MethodsWe combined genetic causal inference, statistical colocalization, single-cell expression mapping, and structure-based druggability assessment. Cis-protein quantitative trait loci (cis-pQTL) instruments were derived from two independent plasma proteomic platforms, UKB-PPP (2,030 proteins with valid cis instruments) and deCODE (1,640 proteins). Genetic causal inference (two-sample Mendelian randomization) was performed against seven CKM-related outcomes across the metabolic (type 2 diabetes [T2D], body mass index [BMI]), renal (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR], chronic kidney disease) and cardiovascular (coronary artery disease, heart failure, stroke) domains. Proteins showing false discovery rate (FDR)-significant associations in at least two CKM domains independently on both platforms were prioritized, and cross-platform directional concordance was evaluated as a robustness measure. Prioritized proteins were followed by colocalization, and characterization using single-cell expression, disease-association and druggability resources. Structural and ligand-efficiency analyses were performed for the leading candidate using its co-crystallized inhibitor complex. ResultsProteome-wide analysis yielded 9,734 (UKB-PPP) and 8,837 (deCODE) protein-outcome estimates, with 77.9% two-platform directional concordance. Cross-domain prioritization identified six proteins (ARG1, GSTA1, INHBB, ITIH1, NCAN, SHBG), all acting across the metabolic-renal axis. Colocalization provided strong support for GSTA1 with eGFR (posterior probability of a shared causal variant 0.97) and ARG1 with BMI (0.93). Genetically higher GSTA1 was associated with lower eGFR and higher T2D risk, with kidney expression confined to proximal tubule cells. Genetically higher ARG1 was associated with lower BMI and lower T2D risk, consistent with hepatocyte-restricted expression. Both proteins were small-molecule tractable. For GSTA1, the inhibitor-bound structure (PDB 1GSF) showed a deep, enclosed H-site, and three chemotypes with previously reported low-micromolar potency against recombinant hGSTA1-1 (ethacrynic acid and the dietary flavonols fisetin and myricetin) all exceeded the lead-like ligand-efficiency threshold (0.30 kcal mol-1 per heavy atom). ConclusionsUsing dual-platform proteogenomics, we identify genetically supported cross-metabolic-renal candidate proteins in CKM syndrome, with GSTA1 and ARG1 emerging as the most robust, pharmacologically tractable candidates. These findings nominate actionable targets and mechanistic entry points for CKM syndrome.

papers.title: Single-cell lung eQTL colocalization implicates alveolar epithelial regulatory effects at COPD lung-function loci
papers.abstract: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung function are highly heritable, but for most genome-wide association study (GWAS) loci, the effector gene and the lung cell type in which it acts are unknown. Single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) offer a way to resolve the cell types in which regulatory variants act. ResultsWe integrated a multi-ancestry GWAS of the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC; Shrine et al., n = 588,452) with single-cell lung eQTLs across 38 cell types (Natri et al., n = 114) by colocalization. We identified 20 candidate colocalizations (posterior probability of a shared causal variant > 0.7) for 13 genes in nine cell types, predominantly epithelial and immune. The two strongest signals localized DSP, an established COPD effector gene, and NRP2, a candidate effector gene, to alveolar type 2 epithelial cells; only these two colocalizations remained supported under a more conservative shared-effect prior. Both signals, together with FAM13A, were also detectable in bulk lung eQTLs, whereas most remaining loci colocalized only in the single-cell analysis. ConclusionsSingle-cell eQTL colocalization resolves the alveolar epithelium as a cellular context for DSP and nominates NRP2 as a candidate lung function effector gene in the same compartment, highlighting the additional cellular resolution provided by single-cell data. The remaining candidate colocalizations warrant replication.

papers.title: Safety Frontiers in Professional Mechanical Plaque Removal (PMPR): A Scoping Review of Current Evidence
papers.abstract: Background: Professional mechanical plaque removal (PMPR) is an established cornerstone of periodontal and peri-implant therapy, yet a comprehensive mapping of its associated iatrogenic risks and hard tissue modifications remains methodologically fragmented. This scoping review mapped the current literature regarding the safety profiles and substrate alterations resulting from contemporary PMPR modalities. Methods: Conducted in strict adherence to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature search was executed on PubMed/MEDLINE without date restrictions. Eligible studies were screened based on predefined Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) criteria. Two independent reviewers performed a two-stage screening process, with consensus achieved via a third reviewer. Results: From 97 initially identified records, full-text evaluation of 18 eligible articles yielded 5 pivotal studies meeting all quantitative safety criteria. The evidence demonstrates that substrate alterations—including surface roughness, abrasive wear, and structural degradation across enamel, dentin, cementum, and titanium—are critically dependent on device selection, application force, tip geometry, and powder abrasivity. Conclusions: Contemporary PMPR modalities demonstrate a high degree of clinical safety when operated within standardized thresholds; however, iatrogenic substrate degradation remains critically dependent on device selection and application parameters. Establishing standardized quantitative safety metrics is imperative to systematically minimize surface trauma while preserving anatomical and biomaterial integrity.

papers.title: Integrative Analysis of Nucleotide Metabolism-Related Genes Reveals a Diagnostic Signature and In Silico Functional Disruption in Hypertrophic Scarring.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scar (HTS) is a fibrotic skin disease characterized by excessive extracellular matrix accumulation and chronic inflammation. This study aimed to investigate cellular heterogeneity, immune alterations, and nucleotide metabolism-related biomarkers in HTS and to explore their potential mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed using Seurat for cell clustering and annotation. Nucleotide metabolism activity was evaluated to identify key cell populations and candidate genes. Bulk transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were used for differential expression analysis, and machine learning algorithms were applied to develop a diagnostic model. Sixteen cell clusters were identified, with macrophages showing prominent activation of nucleotide metabolism pathways and immune-related signaling. The optimal Enet + svmLinear model achieved strong predictive performance (area under the curve = 0.934), and Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified NCF1 and GPR34 as key predictive genes. These genes were also associated with immune cell infiltration. In vitro validation using THP-1-derived M2 macrophages showed that NCF1 and GPR34 promoted transforming growth factor-β1 secretion and enhanced fibroblast activation, while their knockdown reduced α-smooth muscle actin and collagen I expression. Collectively, this study reveals the important role of macrophage-associated nucleotide metabolism in HTS and identifies NCF1 and GPR34 as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Decoding the lymphangioleiomyomatosis niche microenvironment via integrative analysis of single cell multiomics and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare, destructive lung disease caused by mutations in tuberous sclerosis complex 1 (TSC1) or TSC2, leading to mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) hyperactivation. While mTOR inhibitor sirolimus, the only US Food and Drug Administration approved drug for this disease, stabilises lung function in most LAM patients, the drug does not eliminate LAM cells, underscoring a critical gap in our understanding of the tumour microenvironment and cellular heterogeneity that drive disease progression. This study provides the first comprehensive multiomics atlas of the human LAM niche, integrating single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-sequencing, single-nucleus ATAC-sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics to deconvolute its complex architecture. We elucidate LAM cellular heterogeneity by identifying three distinct subtypes: the canonical, uterine smooth muscle-like, mTORC1-hyperactive LAMCORE1; a novel, fibroblast-like LAMCORE2 subtype with potent extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling activity; and LAMCORE3, a substate of LAMCORE1 that shares LAM and myogenic signatures, but is characterised by lower transcriptional activity and specific functional enrichment in protein translation. Our analysis reveals the transcriptomic heterogeneity of the LAM subtypes, orchestrated by distinct transcriptional drivers and networks. Furthermore, we uncover spatially resolved LAM-associated fibroblast (LAF) states, LAF-seed and LAF-niche, that coordinate transforming growth factor-β signalling, ECM deposition and remodelling, and niche expansion. Spatial mapping uncovers a structured ecosystem where LAMCORE1 cells form a central core enmeshed with the lymphatic endothelium, which is surrounded by LAFs, LAMCORE2 cells, and reprogrammed immune and epithelial cells. Findings were validated through multimodal imaging technologies. Present work advances the field by providing the first high-resolution blueprint of the LAM niche microenvironment, revealing novel cell states and crosstalk that identify promising novel therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Scleroderma renal crisis as first manifestation of presumed colorectal cancer recurrence: a rare paraneoplastic presentation.
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc), or scleroderma, is a multisystem disorder characterised by cutaneous and visceral fibrosis, uncommonly presenting as scleroderma renal crisis (SRC), a life-threatening complication involving renal failure, microangiopathy and hypertension. papers.title: Navigating Combined Laser Modalities Versus Monotherapy for Atrophic Acne and Postsurgical Scar Improvement: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundCombined laser protocols are increasingly used for atrophic acne and postsurgical scars, but no laser-only network meta-analysis has assessed these regimens within a focused laser-versus-laser framework.ObjectiveTo map randomized evidence for laser monotherapy and combined-laser treatment, identify evidence gaps, and generate provisional treatment rankings.MethodsPubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials comparing at least 2 laser modalities, either as monotherapy or in combination, for atrophic acne or postsurgical scars. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2.0, and a random-effects frequentist network meta-analysis synthesized standardized mean differences and P-scores.ResultsTwenty-six RCTs enrolling 771 participants across 14 laser nodes were included. Only 17 of 91 possible pairwise comparisons (19%) were supported by direct randomized evidence. The 4 combined-laser regimens were each evaluated in a single RCT; the 5 trials contributing at least 1 combination-versus-monotherapy comparison enrolled 172 participants. The largest trial reported better Goodman-Baron improvement with PDL plus nonablative fractional laser than with NAFL alone (standardized mean difference, approximately 0.56). In the main connected monotherapy network, picosecond Nd:YAG ranked highest (P-score, 0.858), but certainty was very low. Overall risk of bias was low in 4 studies and showed some concerns in 22.ConclusionEvidence for combined-laser scar treatment remains sparse and insufficient to recommend a specific dual-laser regimen. This review mainly clarifies current evidence gaps and priorities for future comparative trials.

papers.title: Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na+ and Ca2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. Beyond protons, endogenous ligands, toxins, and small molecules modulate ASIC gating through direct or synergistic mechanisms. ASICs have emerged as key players in pain and psychiatric disorders. Tissue acidosis drives hyperalgesia via sustained ASIC activation, synaptic plasticity disruption, and central sensitization, thereby promoting chronic pain. In limbic circuits, ASIC1a expression in the amygdala, periaqueductal gray, and dorsal raphe nucleus links these channels to anxiety and depression, with ASIC1a antagonists demonstrating robust efficacy in preclinical models. Selective ASIC modulators represent promising therapeutic candidates for pain-psychiatric comorbidities. This review integrates ASIC biophysical properties with their molecular and circuit-level mechanisms in disease, offering a framework to guide future translational efforts targeting ASIC-mediated pathologies.

papers.title: Additively Manufactured Implants for Mandibular Overdentures RCT Part 2: Functional and OHRQoL outcomes.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated and compared the functional outcomes and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) associated with immediate and conventional loading protocols in a randomized clinical trial of mandibular overdentures supported by two additively manufactured narrow-diameter implants. papers.title: Perineural Invasion Is Associated With Stromal Remodeling, Angiogenesis, and Neural Features in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: BackgroundPerineural invasion (PNI) is known as a pathological indicator of aggressive tumor behavior and is associated with poor survival in colorectal cancer (CRC). Although individual biological features associated with PNI have been reported, the relationship between PNI and neural cell attraction and stromal features within the tumor microenvironment remains incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize the clinical, genomic, immune, stromal, vascular, and neural features associated with PNI-positive CRC.MethodsClinical and transcriptomic data from 179 CRC patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed. PNI status was morphologically determined from pathological records, yidlding 45 PNI-positive and 134 PNI-negative cases. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) using Hallmark gene sets characterized transcriptomic differences. Genomic features, immune cell composition, consensus molecular subtypes (CMS), stromal and vascular features, and neural features were compared between groups.ResultsPNI-positive CRC was associated with advanced T category, distant metastasis, advanced stage, and worse progression-free survival. There was the enrichment of proliferation-related pathways, including E2F targets, the G2M checkpoint and MYC target pathways, in PNI-positive CRC. However, genomic differences were limited, with higher homologous recombination deficiency and TP53 mutation frequency in PNI-positive CRC. PNI was not associated with broad changes in xCell immune scores but showed reduced interferon-α and interferon-γ responses. PNI-positive CRC was enriched in the mesenchymal consensus molecular subtype 4 (CMS4) and showed increased stromal fraction and extracellular matrix gene expression. Vascular features were also increased, including endothelial cells and lymphatic endothelial cells, together with enrichment of angiogenesis and increased transforming growth factor (TGF)-β-related features. Notably, PNI-positive CRC showed increased Schwann cell and neuron projection guidance scores and higher expression of axon guidance genes. These findings identified concurrent stromal, vascular, and neural features associated with PNI-positive CRC.ConclusionsPNI-positive CRC is characterized by a coordinated mesenchymal and stromal phenotype accompanied by angiogenic and neural features, with relatively limited genomic and immune differences. These findings provide a biological framework that may help explain the aggressive clinical behavior of PNI-positive CRC.

papers.title: A cell-type-resolved proteomic atlas reveals intra- and intercellular signaling in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) arises from pathological interactions among diverse brain cell types, but cell-type-specific proteomic changes remain underexplored. Here, we present deep proteomic profiling of sorted or proximity-labeled brain cells from AD mouse models (5xFAD and AppNL-G-F) at multiple ages, quantifying 13,411 proteins in microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocyte precursor cells, and neurons, with additional spatial information. We identified 3,028 differentially abundant proteins, most of which were absent in a bulk proteomic dataset, and constructed cell-type-specific networks to define functional modules and hub proteins. Comparison with transcriptomic data revealed that ∼30% of proteomic changes are RNA discordant. Further analyses uncovered cross-cell-type signaling proteins conserved in human AD brains, such as pleiotrophin (Ptn), which is transcriptionally enriched in astrocytes but accumulates in microglia. Importantly, recombinant PTN activates human induced microglia (iMG) cells. Thus, these findings provide a comprehensive cell-type-resolved proteomic atlas of AD models, highlighting novel intra- and intercellular signaling events.

papers.title: Unplanned reoperation after facial fracture surgery: Pooled proportions, causes, and associated Factors-A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Facial fracture surgery is generally intended to provide definitive restoration of skeletal anatomy and function, and yet a subset of patients requires further operative treatment. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the reported proportion, causes, and associated factors for unplanned postoperative surgical reintervention following operative treatment of traumatic facial fractures. PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched for English-language reports published from January 1, 2000, through June 30, 2026. During revision, an additional high-sensitivity search omitting mandatory reoperation-related outcome terms was performed to assess search completeness. In total, 118 eligible reports were included in the systematic review, and 76 non-overlapping studies, comprising 14 311 patients, were included in the primary meta-analysis. Random-effects binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models were used to pool patient-level reoperation proportions. The pooled reported reoperation proportion across heterogeneous study-specific follow-up periods was 4.7% (95% CI 3.6-6.2%), with a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.6-27.7%, indicating substantial between-study variation. Corresponding pooled reported proportions were 5.9% for orbital, 5.2% for mandibular, and 1.6% for ZMC/midfacial fractures, with a significant overall difference among the three principal anatomical groups (likelihood-ratio test, p = 0.025). Exploratory cause-specific analyses, restricted to incompletely and variably reported subsets with adequate ascertainment of each individual cause, identified nonunion/delayed union, infection-related complications, and orbital implant malposition among recurrently reported indications for reoperation. These findings should be interpreted descriptively because cause-specific reporting was incomplete, reporting subsets differed across outcomes, and individual causes were not necessarily mutually exclusive. In exploratory analyses, follow-up duration was not significantly associated with the reported reoperation proportion (OR 1.06 per additional 6 months; 95% CI 0.89-1.27; p = 0.487). The review was retrospectively registered on OSF (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/DS7RM). Across the heterogeneous follow-up periods reported in the included studies, the pooled reported proportion of unplanned reoperation was approximately 4.7%. However, the wide prediction interval and substantial variation in follow-up duration, outcome definition, fracture severity, and treatment setting limit direct application of this estimate to individual patients or institutions. Standardized patient-level and time-specific outcome reporting is needed before clinically interpretable fixed-time benchmarks can be established.

papers.title: Does pterygomaxillary junction anatomy affect separation patterns during orthognathic surgery in patients with cleft lip and palate?
papers.abstract: Pterygomaxillary separation during Le Fort I osteotomy may be influenced by anatomical variations, particularly in patients with repaired cleft lip and palate (CLP). The groups were similar in age and sex distribution, and all patients had a skeletal Class III deformity. On both sides, pterygomaxillary junction thickness and width were significantly greater in patients with repaired CLP, while medial pterygoid plate length was significantly shorter (all P < 0.05). The right side pterygomaxillary angle was also greater in the CLP patients. Separation patterns were similar on the right side, whereas a significant difference was observed on the left side (P = 0.012), with a higher frequency of type 4 separation in patients with repaired CLP. Additional exploratory subgroup analyses according to cleft morphology showed no significant difference between the lesser and greater segments in unilateral complete cleft patients or between isolated cleft lip and isolated cleft palate subgroups. These findings indicate that repaired CLP is associated with distinct pterygomaxillary junction anatomy and altered separation behaviour, supporting careful preoperative CBCT assessment for surgical planning and risk reduction.

papers.title: Patient-specific customized titanium mesh for alveolar bone regeneration: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesCustomized titanium meshes are increasingly being used for guided bone regeneration (GBR) of complex alveolar ridge deficiencies. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their clinical performance with respect to horizontal, vertical and volumetric bone gain, percentage of planned bone volume achieved, healing complications, and implant-related outcomes and, where comparative evidence was available, assessed their performance relative to other GBR approaches.Materials and methodsElectronic databases were searched up to April 15, 2026 to identify randomized and non-randomized comparative studies and prospective or retrospective single-arm studies evaluating customized titanium mesh for alveolar ridge augmentation. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2), Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist. The certainty of the evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.ResultsThirty reports representing 29 independent studies involving 840 participants and 966 augmented sites were included. The pooled mean vertical and horizontal bone gains were 4.61 mm (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.08 to 5.14) and 5.45 mm (95% CI, 3.97 to 6.94), respectively, while the pooled volumetric bone gain was 1.07 cm³ (95% CI, 0.73 to 1.41). The pooled percentage of planned bone volume achieved was 82.5% (95% CI, 73.1% to 92.0%). Mesh exposure was the most frequent complication, with a pooled rate of 19.75% (95% CI, 14.41% to 26.46%), whereas postoperative infection (2.87%; 95% CI, 1.38% to 5.86%) and implant failure (1.33%; 95% CI, 0.67% to 2.64%) were less common. Network meta-analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences in vertical bone gain between customized titanium mesh and the alternative GBR approaches evaluated. The certainty of the evidence ranged from low to very low.ConclusionsWithin the limitations of the available evidence, customized titanium meshes were associated with clinically relevant alveolar ridge augmentation, while mesh exposure remained relatively frequent. Postoperative infection and implant failure were less frequent. Current comparative evidence does not demonstrate clear superiority over alternative GBR approaches, and the certainty of the available evidence remains low to very low.Clinical trial numberNot applicable.

papers.title: Temporomandibular joint pseudogout diagnosed by arthrocentesis associated with peri-odontoid calcification: A case report.
papers.abstract: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystal deposition disease, also known as pseudogout, rarely involves the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and is often difficult to diagnose because of its nonspecific clinical and radiographic features. In many reported cases, a definitive diagnosis has been established only after biopsy or surgical intervention. An 84-year-old woman presented with swelling and pain in the right preauricular region accompanied by neck pain. Imaging revealed calcified lesions around the right TMJ with joint-space enlargement, as well as peri‑odontoid calcification. The differential diagnoses of the TMJ lesion included synovial chondromatosis and pseudogout. Arthrocentesis of the TMJ was performed, and microscopic examination of the aspirated fluid under compensated polarized light microscopy revealed positively birefringent rhomboid crystals, leading to a definitive diagnosis of TMJ pseudogout without the need for surgical biopsy or other invasive intervention. Treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs resulted in rapid symptom resolution, and no recurrence was observed during a 2-year follow-up period. This case highlights that TMJ arthrocentesis can serve as a useful and minimally invasive diagnostic procedure for establishing a definitive diagnosis of pseudogout while potentially avoiding unnecessary surgical biopsy or invasive intervention. In addition, the presence of peri‑odontoid calcification may suggest CPPD deposition at multiple anatomical sites.

papers.title: Concomitant Temporomandibular Joint and Orthognathic Surgery in Patients With Dentofacial Deformities: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: The management of temporomandibular disorders (TMD) in patients with dentofacial deformities remains controversial, particularly regarding the role of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) surgery in addition to orthognathic treatment. While orthognathic surgery alone may improve TMD symptoms, some patients may require additional TMJ procedures because of established intra-articular pathology. Clinical outcomes including pain, joint sounds, function, maximal interincisal opening (MIO), and quality of life were analyzed. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Four studies comprising 5 cohorts and 155 patients were included. All studies were retrospective and showed low to moderate methodological quality (NOS scores: 8-11/16). papers.title: Natural product integrated metal-organic frameworks for chronic wound healing: From pathological signal responsiveness to on-demand drug delivery.
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) possess remarkable structural diversity and broad biological activities, giving them substantial potential in chronic wound therapy. papers.title: Cellular senescence in skin inflammation: molecular mechanisms and potential clinical implications.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence is increasingly regarded as a mechanism linking chronic tissue stress to persistent skin inflammation. Senescent cells are defined by stable cell-cycle arrest with remodeling of morphology, metabolism, and secretory phenotype, of which the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) is central. It further notes that clinical translation depends on defining senescence-maintained lesion subtypes, establishing combinatorial biomarkers and spatial maps, and validating the efficacy and safety window of local therapies in suitable models and human tissues.

A key stromal population, fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), has attracted considerable attention. Yet FAPs are not a fixed mesenchymal lineage. They form a plastic, heterogeneous compartment with context-dependent functional states that shift with injury stage, anatomical site, disease, and species. Understanding what drives this plasticity is essential. This review examines how biochemical, inflammatory, mechanical, and epigenetic signals shape FAP states. We synthesize evidence from multiple species, including mouse, human, bovine, porcine, and camel muscle systems. Four regulatory modules are considered: TGF-β/PDGFRα signaling and immune crosstalk, canonical and non-canonical Wnt pathways, epigenetic regulation, and extracellular matrix mechanotransduction. Through these pathways, FAPs adopt distinct functional programs. These include homeostatic maintenance, reparative support, fibrogenic activation, adipogenic differentiation, inflammatory response, and senescence. Each program differentially influences muscle stem cell function and tissue remodeling outcomes. These programs reflect context-dependent FAP states, not a uniform lineage with fixed functions. Several concepts require clarification. We emphasize that fibrogenic and adipogenic programs can be differentially regulated yet coexist within diseased muscle, and that pathological FAP states may retain context-dependent reversibility. These insights clarify the constraints on cross-species translation and inform the design of stage-matched, context-appropriate, or combinatorial FAP-directed therapeutic strategies for muscle disease.

papers.title: Vitreous Transcriptomics in Diabetic Retinopathy: Current Research and Future Prospects.
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, yet the molecular mechanisms behind its vision-threatening complications remain not fully understood. Transcriptomics enables the study of these processes through active gene expression, providing a pathway to the discovery of new biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Vitreous humour is commonly affected in numerous retinal pathologies, including DR, and is accessible through pars plana vitrectomy, making it a good candidate for transcriptomics research. Following PubMed and Embase search, 18 articles on vitreous transcriptomics were included. They were subclassified into themes of non-coding RNA, RNA methylation, angiogenesis, inflammation and fibrosis. We concluded that vitreous transcriptomics has the potential to influence future DR diagnostics and therapeutics. However, current evidence is limited by underpowered studies and lack of standardised protocols.

papers.title: Nanomedicine-Enhanced CAR-Engineered Immunotherapy for Lung Cancer: Focusing on Multimodal Strategies and Precision Therapy.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains a major therapeutic challenge because of its molecular and antigenic heterogeneity, rapid evolution, treatment resistance, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Although chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed the treatment of hematological malignancies, its efficacy in lung cancer remains constrained by antigen heterogeneity, poor tumor trafficking and infiltration, T-cell dysfunction, suppressive stromal and myeloid compartments, manufacturing complexity, and pulmonary on-target off-tumor toxicity. Nanomedicine offers a versatile platform to address these barriers by improving CAR-T manufacturing and functional fitness, enabling targeted delivery of nucleic acids and immunomodulators, remodeling the TME, enhancing local accumulation and controlled activation, and supporting transient in situ generation of CAR-engineered immune cells. This review integrates these advances within a Route-Antigen-Microenvironment-Programming (RAMP) framework and emphasizes the mechanistic interdependence among delivery route, target selection, local tumor ecology, and CAR generation and control. We examine the antigen landscapes of non-small-cell and small-cell lung cancer and propose a quantitative framework for antigen selection that incorporates antigen density, spatial and temporal heterogeneity, normal-tissue safety, and engineering compensability. We further discuss nanotechnology-assisted manufacturing, cell-surface nanobackpacks, tumor preconditioning, local biomaterial reservoirs, in vivo CAR programming, pulmonary delivery, multimodal therapy, and theranostic monitoring. Most nano-enabled approaches are still supported primarily by preclinical studies or evidence from non-lung-cancer settings, underscoring the need for standardized assessment of biodistribution, reproducibility, immunogenicity, pulmonary safety, and long-term material fate. Integrating quantitative antigen profiling with biodegradable and controllable materials and lung-relevant translational models may help advance CAR-engineered immunotherapy toward a spatially controlled, dynamically monitored, and personalized therapeutic platform for lung cancer.

papers.title: Effectiveness of platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) as adjunctive therapy in alveolar bone grafting: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundPlatelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is an autologous biomaterial containing growth factors that may improve bone regeneration and wound healing after alveolar bone grafting (ABG) in patients with cleft-related alveolar defects.ObjectiveTo evaluate whether PRF used as an adjunct improves the outcome of alveolar bone grafting for alveolar cleft reconstruction.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO: CRD420261447817). PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to July 2026. Randomized or non-randomized comparative clinical studies of PRF plus bone grafting versus bone grafting alone were eligible. Outcomes were newly formed bone, graft volume, graft height (resorption), and bone density. Risk of bias was appraised with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tool and certainty of evidence with GRADE.ResultsOf 1101 records identified, five randomized controlled trials with 126 patients were included. Three trials reported more newly formed bone or less graft resorption with PRF, and two found no difference between groups. In an exploratory meta-analysis of two trials, the random-effects mean difference in newly formed bone was 9.31% (95% CI: -1.07 to 19.70; I2 = 83.5%). For graft height (three trials), the mean difference was 0.88 mm (95% CI: -1.13 to 2.90; I2 = 89.4%). Bone density, reported by two trials, did not differ between groups. Certainty of evidence was very low for all outcomes.ConclusionCurrent evidence is too limited and too uncertain to show that PRF improves the results of iliac crest bone grafting alone. papers.title: The role of cellular signaling pathways in the therapeutic effects of sonodynamic therapy against periodontitis: A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dysbiotic subgingival biofilms and driven by a dysregulated host response that destroys the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone. Mechanical debridement remains the cornerstone of therapy, but biofilm tolerance, anatomically inaccessible niches, and the limited action of antimicrobials on host-mediated tissue destruction leave clinically relevant gaps. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) uses low-intensity ultrasound to activate sonosensitizers and generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), offering deeper tissue reach than light-based approaches and a route to site-specific, non-antibiotic adjunctive care. Beyond microbial killing, ROS and co-released mediators may reshape host signaling. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on signaling pathways modulated by SDT and grades it by proximity to periodontitis. Direct evidence from periodontal or jawbone-infection studies concerns NF-κB, NLRP3/caspase-1, Toll-like receptor (TLR) and NOD-like receptor signaling, IL-17 signaling, osteoclast differentiation, M1-to-M2 macrophage polarization, and AMPK and PI3K/Akt-associated osteogenesis. Mechanistic precedents from non-periodontal models concern ROS-PPARγ-NF-κB, Nrf2/ARE, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR-autophagy signaling. Direct periodontal evidence is limited to a small number of preclinical studies, pathway-level claims rest mainly on transcript- or protein-level associations, and the anti-inflammatory and pro-osteogenic effects of some platforms are attributable to co-delivered nitric oxide or metal ions rather than to sonodynamic ROS. We therefore distinguish SDT-dependent from platform-dependent effects, discuss dental translational issues (delivery, ultrasound source and dosimetry, safety, peri‑implantitis, systemic comorbidity), and propose research priorities: pathway-specific validation, standardized ultrasound reporting, and controlled clinical trials of SDT as an adjunct to subgingival instrumentation.

papers.title: Red-emissive thymine-functionalized carbon nanodots potentiate minocycline antibacterial activity at subtherapeutic doses.
papers.abstract: Minocycline (MC), a second-generation tetracycline antibiotic, is commonly used to treat a broad range of bacterial infections, including periodontal infections. However, local application requires high concentrations, leading to a risk of cytotoxic effects on bone-forming cells and likely promoting resistance. Nanocarriers offer a means of concentrating MC at the site of application, yet their use depends on the reliable drug retention, which is governed by the drug-surface interaction. Here, red-emissive carbon nanodots (CNDs) were functionalized with a thymine-containing ligand (CND-L1), a nucleobase whose consecutive hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor sites are complementary to those of MC, enabling drug binding through a defined set of hydrogen bonds instead of by non-specific adsorption to the bare surface. The intrinsic red emission of the CNDs served as a label-free readout for confocal microscopy and quantitative flow cytometry, which revealed that CND-L1/MC associated approximately 4-fold more efficiently with A.a. cells than CNDs/MC, indicating that L1 modification preserves the complex-bacteria association under MC loading. All conjugates maintained MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts viability above 70%. CND-L1 therefore rendered MC active at a concentration at which the free drug had no effect.

papers.title: Prognostic Factors Associated with Treatment Outcomes in Endodontic/Periodontal Lesions: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The complex nature of endodontic/periodontal lesions complicates treatment prognosis, making long-term tooth survival challenging to predict. Identifying key prognostic factors can facilitate evidence-based clinical decision-making. This systematic review aims to evaluate the available evidence on factors associated with treatment outcomes in endodontic/periodontal lesions and to identify potential prognostic indicators. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched from 1 June to 1 July 2026 with no restrictions. Observational studies investigating associations between baseline prognostic factors and treatment outcomes in adults with endodontic/periodontal lesions were eligible for inclusion. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, the findings were synthesized narratively rather than through meta-analysis. Results: Four retrospective studies comprising 501 teeth were included. Risk of bias was predominantly moderate to high, and certainty of evidence was low. No single factor demonstrated directionally consistent independent association across the available adjusted analyses. Conclusions: Despite limited evidence, an overall pattern suggests that endodontic/periodontal lesion prognosis may be most frequently associated with the extent of periodontal tissue destruction and the amount of remaining periodontal support. Prospective studies using standardized endodontic/periodontal lesion definitions, outcomes and appropriately adjusted multivariable prognostic models are needed.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic mapping of anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis reveals perivascular enrichment of type I interferon responses and immune activation.
papers.abstract: Anti-MDA5 autoantibody-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5+ DM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy associated with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease and a high mortality rate, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. papers.title: Oral Microbiota and Secondary Alveolar Bone Grafting Outcomes: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Research Priorities.
papers.abstract: Secondary alveolar bone grafting (SABG) restores alveolar continuity and supports tooth eruption and subsequent orthodontic movement in patients with alveolar clefts. Established determinants of outcome include surgical, anatomical, dental, and behavioral factors. The perioperative microbial environment may also be influenced by cleft-adjacent plaque retention, oronasal communication, local inflammation, and appliance-associated biofilms. This narrative review asks whether perioperative oral microbial features are associated with defined SABG complications and whether they add clinically useful prediction of graft outcomes beyond established clinical factors. Direct SABG reports are distinguished from broader cleft and mechanistic evidence. Two reports describe, respectively, an association of preoperative salivary microbial features with study-defined inflammation at the grafted site 3 months after SABG and postoperative microbial changes; partial participant overlap remains unresolved. Neither report establishes a causal role for oral microbiota in SABG complications or validates microbial features as predictors of long-term bone outcomes or graft failure. The reviewed evidence is insufficient for routine microbiome profiling, pathogen-directed or antifungal treatment based solely on microbial findings, or microbiome-based prediction of SABG success. Without formal quality or risk-of-bias appraisal, conclusions remain provisional. Multicenter prospective studies with standardized local sampling and outcome-specific follow-up are needed to evaluate incremental prognostic value and the efficacy of microbiota-targeted interventions.

papers.title: SpaAxFormer: Fine-Grained Token Modeling of Spatial Transcriptomics with Axial Transformers
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics combines gene-expression measurements with spatial relationships between cells. We investigate how spatial context can be incorporated into gene-resolved representations while preserving explicit input-gene correspondence. SpaAxFormer is a spatially constrained factorized formulation that maintains contextual cell–gene states throughout the encoder. It first contextualizes genes within each cell and then exchanges corresponding-gene states across spatial neighbors, while a separate CLS representation provides a cell-level summary. Contextual gene states support gene-expression reconstruction, while CLS-conditioned reconstruction and contrastive learning provide complementary supervision for the cell-level representation. We evaluate SpaAxFormer on gene-expression imputation and spatial-domain identification across multiple spatial-transcriptomics technologies. Compared with the included baselines, imputation results were most favorable on dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) datasets and more mixed on additional technologies, while post-hoc spatial refinement consistently improved mean ARI on the Visium spatial-domain datasets where it was applied. In a single-slice component-addition analysis, mean clustering ARI increased as CLS-conditioned reconstruction and contrastive supervision were added. Together, these results show that the same gene-resolved formulation can support complementary gene-level prediction and cell-level spatial representation while preserving explicit input-gene correspondence.

papers.title: CellChat Hotspot: A Targeted Approach to Cell–Cell Communication Analysis With Spatial transcriptomics Validation
papers.abstract: In recent years, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell–Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat . This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context-driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Overall, this framework provides a biologically guided strategy for studying intercellular communication in complex systems such as the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Statistical significance testing for spatial domain detection in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: In spatial transcriptomics, domain-detection methods group platform-specific spatial measurement units—cells, bins or multicellular spots—into spatial domains for comparing molecular programs, cellular composition and interactions among tissue regions. However, the number of candidate domains detected in the same tissue can vary with user-specified parameters or model-selection criteria. Whether candidate domains should be merged can be framed as a test of a single-domain null hypothesis, under which each gene has constant mean expression across all spatial units in the combined region. However, testing candidate domains on the same gene-expression data used to detect them may induce post-selection bias and yield anti-conservative p -values, increasing the risk of oversegmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce SigDoTS (statistical Significance testing for Domain deTection in Spatial transcriptomics), a hypothesis-testing framework for spatial domain detection. SigDoTS uses hierarchical testing to determine which candidate domains to retain or merge, with adjustment for family-wise error control. It accounts for gene–gene covariance and spatial dependence and computes p -values by rerunning the upstream domain-detection pipeline on datasets simulated under the fitted single-domain null. In simulations, SigDoTS controlled the type I error rate at the root node under the single-domain null and improved recovery of the true spatial domains when multiple domains were present. In human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, SigDoTS retained superficial and deep Layer 6 domains but merged Layer 3 candidate domains across different initial numbers of candidate domains. In ovarian and colorectal cancers, SigDoTS retained epithelial domains with different gene-expression programs and local immune environments, together with immune, stromal and vascular domains.

papers.title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients

papers.title: Dysregulated B Cell Education Drives Autoimmunity and Immunodeficiency in Down Syndrome
papers.abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) present with both increased rates of autoimmunity and immunodeficiency. To understand this paradox, we first examined lymph node (LN) architecture and immune cell composition in infants with and without DS, as well as peripheral blood B cells from unrelated adults with and without DS. Most strikingly, LNs from individuals with DS exhibited a marked paucity of germinal centers compared with typical lymph nodes. Stromal cells within DS LNs expressed significantly lower levels of the adhesion molecules ICAM1 and VCAM1, accompanied by significantly reduced CXCR5 expression within B cell follicles, suggesting impaired B cell migration and follicular organization. Although fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) were present at comparable frequencies in DS and control LNs, MARCO lymphatic endothelial cells (MARCO-LECs), another critical stromal cell population supporting LN architecture, were significantly reduced. In addition, follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), which are essential for antigen retention and B cell selection within germinal centers, were also substantially reduced. To determine the consequences of these abnormalities on humoral immunity, we performed paired single-cell RNA sequencing and V(D)J sequencing of peripheral blood B cells from adults with and without DS. DS memory and CD86+ switched memory B cell populations exhibited significantly elevated reactive oxygen species and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling gene signatures, coupled with reduced levels of somatic hypermutation in the memory population and increase usage of the autoreactivity-associated IGHV4-34 heavy-chain gene. Collectively, these findings suggest that early-life disruption of LN architecture, characterized by reduced expression of adhesion molecules, selective loss of MARCO-LECs, and depletion of FDCs, impairs germinal center function and B cell education. This defective microenvironment likely contributes to inadequate affinity maturation, as reflected by diminished somatic hypermutation and a more autoreactive B cell repertoire in adults with Down syndrome.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling of human plaques reveals cellular and molecular signatures of symptomatic atherosclerosis
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability drives ischemic cardiovascular events, yet the cellular and molecular signatures distinguishing symptomatic from asymptomatic human plaques remain poorly defined. Here, we compared 53 symptomatic and asymptomatic human carotid plaques using single-nucleus (snRNA-seq; 17 samples, 19,100 nuclei; AtherOMICS biobank) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; 36 samples, 68,983 cells; four public datasets), analysed independently and combined by meta-analysis. Nuclear profiling uncovered a depletion of fibroblasts in symptomatic plaques, marked by downregulation of RGS5. The analyses further nominated higher TWIST1 expression in ECs (colocalized with risk across four atherosclerotic phenotypes), lower GUCY1A1 expression in fibroblasts and macrophages, and higher MRAS expression in T cells as candidate driver mechanisms linking genetic risk to symptomatic plaque transition. These findings provide novel insights into cellular and molecular phenotypes associated with plaque vulnerability and identify potential driver mechanisms of symptomatic plaque transformation that could inform therapeutic development.

papers.title: DisCell: Separating Spillover from Niche Response in Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution measures every cell in its place in the tissue, but diffusion and segmentation errors also add transcripts of neighboring cells to a cell’s counts. This spillover makes a cell resemble its neighbors, and a response to the niche makes cells in the same niche resemble each other. Both tie a cell’s expression to its surroundings. The count data alone cannot tell the two apart. Findings: from single-cell transcriptomes, such as a gene program that is higher in one niche than in another or signaling genes that change depending on the neighborhood, may therefore be artifacts of spillover. Current models describe a cell by its intrinsic state together with either its niche response or spillover, but none models all three. We present DisCell, the first method that models all three components jointly and measures how robust each finding is to spillover. DisCell is a generative model that describes single-cell gene expression profiles in terms of two latent variables, an intrinsic state and a response to the niche, and adds spillover from its neighbors as a separate term. DisCell fits the model at increasing levels of spillover and recomputes each finding on the spillover-free expression to see how much spillover it withstands. DisCell also estimates the most spillover a section can contain, and a finding that holds even at that amount is not explained by spillover. In simulated tissue, DisCell recovers each cell’s intrinsic state and response and tells findings created by spillover apart from genuine responses. On five sections of ovarian and lung tissue, the intrinsic state keeps more of each cell’s own properties, measured by its cell-cycle phase, than any competing method that holds as little of its neighborhood. Within each cell type, the model partitions the variation of each gene into intrinsic state, niche response and spillover. Using DisCell, we rank findings about niches by their robustness to spillover and confirm that a previously reported finding withstands spillover, that esophageal cancer cells in niches infiltrated by immune or stromal cells express more of an epithelial–mesenchymal transition program. DisCell also predicts what the gene expression of a cell type would be in another niche, with its spillover part separated, at lower error on most tasks than the competing method built for this purpose. Training the model takes under ten minutes on one consumer GPU for sections of up to 400,000 cells.

papers.title: smoothclust: Spatial smoothing and boundary-density summaries for spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the measurement of gene expression while preserving tissue organization. A common analysis task is the identification of spatial domains, defined here as spatially coherent regions with consistent expression profiles or cell-type mixtures and represented using categorical spatial tissue maps. However, while numerous methods have been developed to identify spatial domains, interpretable summary measures to quantify spatial domain organization and tissue architecture at the sample level remain less standardized. Here, we present smoothclust, a framework for spatial domain analysis consisting of two components: a spatial-smoothing-based clustering workflow for generating spatial domain labels, and a boundary density (BD) metric that provides local and sample-level summaries of label transitions on a spatial graph. Building on established categorical spatial statistics, the raw BD metric is calculated from the proportion of neighboring spatial locations that are assigned to different domain labels, and requires only spatial coordinates and domain labels as inputs. The metric can be calculated using either our spatial-smoothing-based domain labels or labels from external clustering methods or manual annotations. Relative BD is a composition-adjusted summary, calculated by dividing raw BD by its expectation under random relabeling with the observed label counts. By quantifying label transitions, our framework translates spatial domain label maps into interpretable local and sample-level summary measures of tissue architecture, facilitating exploratory analyses and comparisons across samples and biological conditions. We demonstrate the approach through evaluations across datasets from several spatial transcriptomics platforms and simulations. The spatial-smoothing workflow and BD metric are implemented in the smoothclust R package, which is freely available from Bioconductor and GitHub.

Single SAE fits showed the opposite profile: they covered most concepts with purer gene programs but reproduced only 27–46% of their features. A consensus over five SAE fits combined the two strengths. It was reproducible (78–98% across sources) and as pure as single fits: 11–40% of its features carried marker genes of another lineage, against 44–70% for varimax. Against the strongest baseline, varimax sparsified to the SAE’s sparsity, the consensus covered as many concepts on PCA and Geneformer embeddings and more on learned spatial and text embeddings. The consensus also had costs. It covered fewer lineages than single fits and, like all SAEs, missed weak planted states that rotations recovered; neither a longer single fit nor a second SAE trained on the consensus residual recovered what it discarded. Reproducibility alone therefore ranks features poorly: SAE features should be reported with the number of known concepts they cover and the purity of their gene programs, against a rotation of the same embedding sparsified to the SAE’s sparsity.

papers.title: PLA2G2A across tumor compartments and its relevance to drug resistance.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance in cancer is shaped not only by tumor-cell-intrinsic mutations but also by spatially organized microenvironmental states. PLA2G2A, encoding group IIA secreted phospholipase A2 (sPLA2-IIA), is usually discussed as an inflammatory lipid enzyme; however, its cancer relevance depends strongly on cellular source, localization and disease stage. The pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cancer-associated fibroblast study provides the strongest resistance-proximal immune-functional evidence, whereas mucinous colorectal extracellular vesicles, ovarian ascites, invasive-front fibroblasts, treatment-remodeled stroma and prognostic signatures require more direct therapy-response validation. Gastric and intestinal epithelial data further caution that PLA2G2A may accompany differentiation, invasion restraint, antimicrobial defense or barrier protection. We therefore argue against treating PLA2G2A as a universal oncogenic target. Instead, it should be advanced as a mechanism-matched biomarker or therapeutic hypothesis only when compartment, biochemical-output, functional and perturbational evidence converge.

papers.abstract: The immune-fibrotic axis functions as a vicious feedback loop where age-related chronic, low-grade systemic inflammation (inflammaging) drives maladaptive tissue repair and fibrosis, while senescent fibrotic cells in turn amplify systemic inflammation. In the aging heart, immune dysregulation and fibroblast activation drive tissue scarring and stiffening and a higher risk of heart failure and vascular disease. To identify cardiac regions and cell types affected with age, we monitored transcriptional changes across whole hearts of 6- and 24-month-old male and female mice. Spatially resolved signatures of macrophages and fibroblasts, non-cardiomyocyte populations highly involved in inflammaging, were enriched predominantly in the valves and aorta. With age, two cell types simultaneously adopted maladaptive programs: Macrophages displayed reduced immune homeostasis together with increased chemotactic and stromal programs, while more widely distributed fibroblast-lineage cells displayed alterations in extracellular matrix organization and intercellular signals, as well as upregulation of senescence-associated Cdkn1a (encoding p21) and other activated features shared with human cardiac fibroblasts. The major biological significance of these findings is that cardiac immune-fibrotic remodeling is not a uniform, heart-wide process. Instead, it varies with cell type, with valves and aorta emerging as major sites where age-associated programs converge to progressively compromise cardiac structure and function.

papers.title: Identifying multi-omics spatial domains via masked autoencoder and diffusion-based latent regularization with SpaMEDM.
papers.abstract: Spatial multi-omics data provide complementary molecular views of tissue organization. However, their integration remains challenging due to data sparsity, technical noise, and modality-specific distributions. Here, we present Spatial Masked autoEncoder and Diffusion-based Model (SpaMEDM), an end-to-end graph representation learning framework that augments a dual-attention graph-integration backbone with masked reconstruction and diffusion-based latent noise-prediction regularization. In the masked track, randomly masked spot features are recovered by leveraging modality- and graph-specific neighborhood information. In parallel, Gaussian perturbations are applied to modality-specific latent representations at randomly sampled noise levels, and a spatial-graph-informed network is trained to predict the injected noise. This diffusion-based objective is used exclusively during training to encourage robustness to latent perturbations, rather than to perform iterative reverse diffusion or sampling during inference. Furthermore, cosine-based paired-spot directional alignment and adjacency reconstruction encourage compatible cross-modality representations and preservation of the selected graph structure. SpaMEDM flexibly supports purely spatial, dual feature-spatial, and modality-specific feature-pruned spatial graph configurations. Evaluations across diverse spatial multi-omics datasets demonstrate competitive spatial-domain identification performance and produce integrated embeddings that facilitate downstream exploratory analyses.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics maps region and isoform specific brain alterations in mdx and mdx4cv models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is accompanied by cognitive and neurodevelopmental difficulties. Our findings provide insights into molecular alterations associated with brain-related impairments of DMD and a foundation for future therapeutic studies.

papers.title: The altered T cell landscape in systemic sclerosis patients is characterized by dysfunctional type 1 immunity.
papers.abstract: T cells in patients with chronic autoimmunity show features of dysfunction. However, the functionally defined T cell subsets that are affected by these changes remain poorly characterized. papers.title: Post-transcriptional Regulation of FGF Signaling: Insights From Musculoskeletal System.
papers.abstract: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signaling plays a pivotal role in the development, maintenance, and regeneration of musculoskeletal tissues. papers.title: Monotonic additive modeling reveals candidate biomarkers of cardio-renal-metabolic disorder susceptibility.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus form an interconnected disease continuum driven by shared risk factors, overlapping molecular pathways and reciprocal progression. This convergence has led to the recognition of cardio-renal-metabolic disorder (CRMD) as a unified systemic condition in which dysregulation of metabolic, vascular, inflammatory and renal pathways precedes organ-specific pathology. Despite this understanding, current diagnostic strategies remain disease-centric and are typically initiated after substantial tissue damage, limiting opportunities for early intervention. Identification of early non-invasive biomarkers capturing shared CRMD susceptibility is therefore of utmost clinical importance. In this study, we developed an explainable monotonic additive machine learning framework to identify blood-based molecular biomarkers associated with CRMD susceptibility. Transcriptomic profiles representing cardiovascular, renal and metabolic disease states were analysed within a unified CRMD paradigm. Following transcriptomic harmonization and batch correction, a monotonic additive XGBoost model combined with integrated biomarker score, gene-response analysis and differential expression analysis was implemented to identify biologically interpretable and directionally consistent biomarkers reflective of shared CRMD-associated dysregulation. Importantly, these biomarkers have potential for blood-based detection using established assays such as ELISA, multiplex immunoassays and quantitative PCR, underscoring their translational potential for early CRMD screening, susceptibility assessment and risk stratification.

papers.title: Defining Osseointegration for Biodegradable Scaffolds based on Histological, Immunohistochemical and Ultrastructural Analysis.

papers.title: MorphoANOVA: Dissecting Histology–Gene Expression Relationships in Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures the expression of hundreds to thousands of genes within tissue architecture, often accompanied by histology images. papers.title: Live Spatial Transcriptomics Enables Longitudinal Tissue Mapping
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has become an important technology in biomedical research by preserving the spatial context of gene expression in tissues and enabling the study of cellular states and interactions in situ . papers.title: Multiomics Reveals a Production Signature Resembling Mammalian Metabolic Ageing and That Dietary Spermidine Enhances Lipid Handling in Farmed Salmon.
papers.abstract: Metabolic ageing and associated changes in lipid mobilisation have been heavily studied in humans and model taxa, yet remain poorly understood in farmed animals, with potentially important implications for health and welfare outcomes. Importantly, this occurred in parallel to changes in lipid and protein markers that may reprogram lipid handling, supporting a hypothesis that spermidine supplementation counters the proposed metabolic ageing related phenotype. papers.title: Multi-omics, spatial omics and artificial intelligence in chronic diseases: current applications and future directions.
papers.abstract: Chronic diseases exhibit multiscale heterogeneity and spatial organization, yet analytical frameworks often fail to connect molecular perturbations, tissue architecture, and clinical outcomes within a unified evidence framework. Bulk and single-modality approaches can identify regulatory or cellular alterations but provide limited insight into why pathogenic programs emerge in anatomical regions, how they shape disease niches, and how they drive divergent clinical trajectories. Multi-omics partially addresses this gap by resolving interconnected layers of regulation, transcription, protein activity, and metabolism, whereas spatial omics maps these processes within preserved tissue architecture, enabling the delineation of lesion topology, interface states, and multicellular microenvironments. Artificial intelligence (AI) may further extend this framework by integrating molecular, spatial, imaging, and clinical data into disease representations that support disease stratification, the discovery of mechanistic patterns, and clinically testable predictions, provided that models are externally validated, biologically interpretable, and robust to dataset bias and domain shift. In this review, we examine how multi-omics, spatial omics, and AI can bridge the disconnect between molecular profiling, spatial pathology, and clinical translation in chronic disease research. We discuss six representative disease domains before synthesizing insights into how these approaches define molecular endotypes, map pathological niches, identify recurrent mechanistic patterns, and generate interpretable surrogate readouts for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment stratification. We also highlight limitations, including preanalytical variability, inconsistencies across platforms, limited external generalizability, and the challenges of translating high-dimensional outputs into deployable clinical tools. Finally, we outline priorities for scalable evidence systems, mechanism-guided validation frameworks, multimodal model interpretability, and prospective clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Background and objectivesProphylactic management of early postoperative linear scars remains a clinical challenge. They were divided into a sequential DPL-CO2 laser group and a CO2 laser monotherapy group (19 patients each). All received six monthly prophylactic treatments. Efficacy was assessed by two independent surgeons using the Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS).ResultsAfter six treatments, no statistically significant difference was detected in the total POSAS score between the two groups (p = 0.988, mean difference = -0.26, 95% CI: -1.66 to 1.14). However, compared to baseline, both groups showed significant improvement in several key scar parameters, including vascularization, thickness, color, stiffness, and irregularity. One case of transient reactive hyperplasia in the CO2 group was resolved with conservative management.ConclusionsBoth sequential DPL-CO2 laser therapy and CO2 laser monotherapy were associated with favorable clinical trajectories in early postoperative linear scars over 6 months. The observed parallel trends generate a hypothesis requiring proper prospective randomized evaluation to determine the true utility of CO2 laser alone as a simplified early intervention.

papers.title: Mechanistic study of ECM phenotype switch in epicardial adipose tissue in atrial fibrillation: A bioinformatics study.
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is closely associated with AF, but its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling characteristics of AF-related EAT. Using the publicly available RNA-sequencing dataset GSE135445 (AF: n = 6, sinus rhythm: n = 6), we performed differential expression analysis (DESeq2) on gene-level counts regenerated from the raw sequencing reads, single-gene analysis focusing on ECM gene families, and gene set enrichment analysis. An "ECM phenotype switch" hypothesis was proposed based on the coordinated dysregulation of interstitial and basement membrane collagen genes. Differential expression analysis identified 610 differentially expressed genes. Notably, the basement membrane-specific collagen COL4A4 was significantly upregulated in AF (log2FC = 4.37, Padj = 2.7 × 10-9), accompanied by significant upregulation of COL4A3, whereas interstitial collagen repair genes (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, and FN1) showed consistent downregulation, defining an "ECM phenotype switch" characterized by suppressed interstitial repair coupled with independent basement membrane deposition; the fibrinolysis inhibitor SERPINE1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) was also markedly upregulated (log2FC = 3.89, Padj = .026). Gene set enrichment analysis implicated ribosome biogenesis and translation dysregulation as a potential associated upstream program (normalized enrichment score = 2.26-3.03 and false discovery rate = 0.012-0.013). AF-related EAT exhibits an ECM phenotype switch characterized by suppressed interstitial collagen repair and independent basement membrane collagen deposition, potentially associated with ribosome biogenesis dysregulation. These hypothesis-generating findings provide a novel framework for understanding EAT-mediated atrial remodeling in AF.

papers.title: Revision surgery after total temporomandibular joint replacement: a case series.
papers.abstract: IntroductionTotal temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) is an established treatment for end-stage temporomandibular joint disease. However, biological and mechanical complications may require revision surgery, and evidence guiding surgical decision-making remains limited. Two patients developed heterotopic ossification with mechanically stable prosthetic components and underwent resection while preserving the prostheses. Two patients presented with mechanical failure, including component displacement, fixation loss, or prosthetic fracture, requiring complete revision with patient-specific prosthetic systems. During a follow-up period ranging from 8 to 24 months, all patients showed stable prosthetic reconstruction without reported postoperative complications.DiscussionRevision surgery after TMJR should be guided by the etiology of the complication and the mechanical stability of the prosthetic system. Prosthesis preservation may be considered when the components remain mechanically stable and treatment can be directed toward the periarticular pathology. In contrast, loss of fixation or structural failure may require complete prosthetic revision.

papers.title: Electrochemical interactions in the oral cavity: The clinical significance of oral galvanism - a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Electrochemical reactions in the oral cavity, caused by small-scale electric charges between different metallic prosthetic materials, are often overlooked in modern dentistry. Although multiple metallic alloys are frequently used in dentistry, their unintentional interactions may lead to both localized tissue effects and have been hypothesized to contribute to broader biological consequences. However, awareness of these interactions remains insufficient among dental practitioners and patients. A narrative review of the literature was conducted using electronic databases including PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Embase. Relevant studies addressing the etiology, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, prevention, and management of oral galvanism were identified and qualitatively synthesized. The reviewed literature indicates that electrochemical interactions between metallic dental materials can result in galvanic current generation, corrosion processes, metal ion release, and a variety of oral manifestations. Previous reports have suggested that more than 30 different metallic components may coexist within a single oral cavity, highlighting the complexity of oral electrochemical interactions. While several studies have proposed potential associations with broader biological and systemic effects, the available evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Recognizing the effects of electrochemical activity in the oral cavity is essential for enhancing biocompatibility, ensuring patient safety, and improving the longevity of dental restorations. This review seeks to address existing knowledge gaps and promote further research into this often-overlooked aspect of dental health.

papers.title: IL-27 promotes systolic overload-induced cardiac oxidative stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and heart failure development.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe interleukin-27 (IL-27) signaling axis plays a critical role in immunity and systemic metabolism. While it initiates potent pro-inflammatory responses against cancer and infection, heightened IL-27 activity during sterile inflammation can induce severe tissue damage. Furthermore, pharmacological neutralization of IL-27 effectively attenuated TAC-induced left ventricular (LV) leukocyte infiltration, oxidative stress, fibrosis, and dysfunction. Conversely, administration of recombinant mouse IL-27 exacerbated the TAC-induced cardiac accumulation of multiple immune cell subsets, oxidative stress, fibrosis, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and overall HF progression.ConclusionsOur findings demonstrate that IL-27 acts as a critical pathogenic driver of cardiac inflammation, oxidative stress, and HF development by modulating both immune cell activation and extracellular matrix remodeling following systolic overload.

papers.abstract: BackgroundImmediate molar implant placement requires management of complex socket anatomy, infection, residual bone, and posterior loading.
